author: Unknown
title: “How Has Serving Impacted You?” : Veterans of the US Military in Their Own Words
content:
What is it like to serve in the United States military? If only it were possible for those who are considering enlisting to learn the unvarnished truth. In 2019, a viral

tweet

 from the official US Army twitter account unexpectedly drew over 11,000 candid replies in the course of 48 hours. These responses offer a rare window into the real experiences of servicemembers and veterans. We present a selection of them here for the benefit of anyone who is thinking about joining the military.


This is a document of an

earlier era

 of social media, captured here before it

vanishes

. You can obtain a book collecting the first twenty-four hours of responses

here

.


Just before Memorial Day in 2019, the United States Army made a strategic blunder almost on par with invading Vietnam. They posted this inquiry on their official Twitter account:


In response, veterans and their family and friends posted thousands upon thousands of tweets recounting broken promises and broken people. They described cancer, PTSD, domestic abuse, unpaid college and housing loans, Gulf War syndrome, insomnia, sexual abuse, poverty, Agent Orange, racism, nightmare disorder, unemployment, burying loved ones, misogyny, orphaned children, burn pit syndrome, homelessness, debilitating injuries, divorce, alcoholism, disappearances, a Veterans Affairs department that was unwilling or unable to help, and suicide, suicide, suicide.


The United States military is one of the largest concentrations of power in the world. With

tens of thousands

 of missiles,

millions

 of firearms, and over

5000

 nuclear weapons—about 40% of all the nuclear weapons in the world—the US military can hold the entire world hostage.


The US military is also the largest employer in the United States,

employing

 almost 2,900,000 workers—roughly 17 out of every 2000 people. If we add private military contractors like Blackwater (250,000 workers), the employees of non-combat support companies like Halliburton who build military infrastructure, provide food, and the like (150,000-250,000), US-based war manufacturers like Lockheed Martin and Boeing (1,500,000), and

veterans

 who receive disability or pension payments (2,000,000), we find that roughly 1 out of every 50 Americans is economically dependent on US militarism.


As in all industries, without this workforce, the military would grind to a halt. It especially depends on regular transfusions of young blood—young people sold stories about adventure, duty, and upward mobility.


If we were to ask new recruits why they joined, we’d

likely

 hear a mix of narratives about gaining strength, seeing the world, paying for college, serving God and country, learning life skills, continuing a family tradition, escaping poverty or an unsafe home, obtaining housing, having fun, and protecting loved ones. Most people join the military because they think it will benefit them or because they believe they are serving a higher calling.


Some recruits get to live out their dreams. Some leave instability, danger, or deprivation for a more structured and economically stable life; some even gain a sense of belonging. If they’re lucky, they serve their time without incident, then move on to free college tuition, a no-down-payment housing loan, health insurance, and a free meal at Golden Corral once a year.


But thousands of veterans’ dreams become nightmares. The promises of recruiters, family members, and Hollywood movies offer a gamble at best—a roll of the dice that

frequently

 ends with being harmed physically, psychologically, and sexually. Military service can lead to

substance abuse

,

homelessness

, and

suicide

. It can also end in unspeakable acts of violence against others, whether those be the declared enemies of the United States, noncombatants, or veterans’ own loved ones.


It is striking how many of these responses speak of being hoodwinked out of college, housing loans, and medical care—how many describe the pain of family members lost to PTSD, alcoholism, or suicide after witnessing or committing atrocities.


American media bombards us with war propaganda. Almost every video game spreads the myth that combat makes us stronger: more powerful weapons, tougher armor, a bigger health bar, greater fortunes. Hollywood promises that the hero can weather any fight—or, if he can’t, his death will be meaningful and glorious.


Statistically speaking, the more we are exposed to combat, the more likely we are to be …

author: Archipelago Anarchist Archive
title: Archipelago Anarchist Archive, Perpustakaan Anarkis, and Anarsip: Jurnal Arsip & Perpustakaan Anti-otoritarian (A Brief Introduction)
content:
Initiatives in anarchist archiving, librarianship, and journals of archives & libraries in Indonesia

The Archipelago Anarchist Archive (AAA) is an informal, alternative archives and library initiative established in 2024 with the aim of preserving and distributing anti-authoritarian materials. AAA is driven by a number of anarchist archivists and librarians from various cities in Indonesia.

The materials that AAA focuses on are those produced in, and related to, the archipelago (known as Indonesia), whether in Indonesian or in non-Indonesian languages. These materials can take the form of texts, photographs, audio, video, and so on. All of AAA's digital archive collections can be accessed through the Internet Archive.

Link to the Archipelago Anarchist Archive collection: https://archive.org/details/@archipelago-anti-authoritarian-archive

Perpustakaan Anarkis (Anarchist Library) is an preservation and distribution project for anti-authoritarian materials based on plain text. Plain text was chosen because it makes it easier for authors and translators to distribute their work, easier for publishers to reproduce it, and easier for those who wish to archive it[1]. Perpustakaan Anarkis understands anti-authoritarianism in a flexible manner, though not without limits. Therefore, it can be said that Perpustakaan Anarkis accepts and includes both anarchist materials (from all tendencies, except anarcho-capitalism and anarcho-nationalism) and materials that can enrich anarchism, such as avant-garde(ism) that challenges not only the boundaries of art but also the state and centralized power, libertarian Marxism, autonomism, democratic confederalism, and so on. In addition, Perpustakaan Anarkis also accepts and includes reportage from the front lines (confrontation) and the home front (care) of flashpoints of popular struggle and resistance, labor strikes, and so on.

Because in anarchism, decentralization and prefiguration are important. And by practicing decentralization and prefiguration, we (and us all) no longer need to wait to act and be overly dependent on a single central point.

Besides anarcho-capitalism and anarcho-nationalism, Perpustakaan Anarkis is also not intended for authoritarian Marxists, misanthropic individuals, extractive technologism (automation that subordinates), avant-garde(ism) that leads to fascism, and other authoritarian tendencies and centralized power.

[1] Authors and translators can distribute their works without the hassle of layout, editing, cover design, and other technical work. Conversely, publishers no longer need to go through the trouble of dealing with writing and translation. And archivists—in addition to finding archiving easier—will receive various versions of the work.

Link to the Perpustakaan Anarkis collection: https://id.anarchistlibraries.net/special/index

Anarsip: Jurnal Arsip & Perpustakaan Anti-otoritarian (Anarsip: Journal of Anti-authoritarian Archives & Libraries) (published periodically, every 6 months) is a space for theorizing–practicing–theorizing–practicing anarchist archives and librarianship. Because we believe that anarchist archives and librarianship should not stop at merely the definition of "managed by, and archiving materials of, anarchist(s) and/or anti-authoritarian [movements and ideas]," but also means using methods, practicing ways of working, and thinking in an anarchist and/or anti-authoritarian manner. If the Situationist International said "to be avant-garde is to move in step with reality" (Internationale Situationiste #8); then we say "to be anarchist archiving and librarianship is to move in step with reality and anarchism."

Link to follow the developments of Anarsip: https://id.anarchistlibraries.net/special/anarsip-jurnal-arsip-perpustakaan-anti-otoritarian

Archipelago Anarchist Archive (AAA) adalah inisiatif pengarsipan dan perpustakaan informal nan alternatif yang didirikan pada tahun 2024 dengan tujuan mempreservasi sekaligus mendistribusi materi-materi anti-otoritarian. AAA digerakkan oleh sejumlah arsiparis dan pustakawan anarkis yang berasal dari berbagai kota di Indonesia.

Adapun materi-materi yang menjadi fokus dari AAA adalah materi-materi yang diproduksi di, dan yang berkaitan dengan, wilayah kepulauan (yang kini disebut sebagai Indonesia) baik itu yang berbahasa Indonesia maupun yang berbahasa non-indonesia. Dan materi-materi tersebut bisa berupa teks, foto, audio, video, dan lain sebagainya. Semua koleksi arsip digital AAA …

title: Helau! Kontoerhalt der Roten Hilfe bei der Sparkasse Göttingen!
content:
Helau! Kontoerhalt der Roten Hilfe bei der Sparkasse Göttingen!


Elf Monate hat es gedauert bis nun im Hauptsacheverfahren das Konto der Roten Hilfe bei der Sparkasse Göttingen erhalten werden konnte. Heute am 11.11.26 ist die Entscheidung des Landgerichts Göttingen nun rechtskräftig. Wir hatten gegen die Kündigung durch die Sparkasse Göttingen Klage eingelegt und konnte diese in zwei Instanzen im Eilverfahren vor Gericht gewinnen. Dabei konnte das

OLG

 Braunschweig keine Begründung für eine Kontokündigung feststellt.

Die Göttinger Sparkasse ließ es dennoch auf ein

Hauptsacheverfahren ankommen und kassierte vor Gericht eine Niederlage

. In dem Urteil wird festgestellt, dass der erhöhte Aufwand zur Prüfung aufgrund einer Beobachtung der Roten Hilfe durch den Verfassungsschutz sowie die mutmaßliche Unterstützung einer von der

US

-Regierung auf eine Terrorliste gesetzten und konstruierten »Antifa Ost« nicht ausreicht, um das Konto zu kündigen.

Der

Hinweisbeschluss des

OLG

 Braunschweig vom 15.07.2026 findet sich

u. a.

 auf der Seite der Gesellschaft für Freiheitsrechte

Für uns bedeutet das:

Die Konten der Roten Hilfe sind gesichert und eine existenzgefährdende Bedrohung für den Verein wurde abgewendet.

Doch Druck gibt es weiterhin, auf Linke und linke Bewegungen und damit auch auf die Rote Hilfe. Dagegen braucht es solidarische Gegenwehr.

Wir stehen weiter solidarisch an eurer Seite und leisten Antirepressionsarbeit.

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: "Birds of War": New Film Tells a Story of Love and Journalism from Syria to Lebanon
content:
We speak with Janay Boulos and Abd Alkader Habak, filmmakers and subjects of the new documentary

Birds of War

, which tells their epic love story through years of upheaval in the Middle East. Boulos, a London-based Lebanese journalist working for the

BBC

, and Habak, a Syrian activist and cameraman, first connected while covering the Syrian civil war and stayed in touch through years of war, revolution and exile, forming a relationship that is chronicled in the documentary by drawing on 13 years of their personal videos, voice notes and other correspondence.


The film also examines the unequal relationship between international news organizations and local journalists whose work they rely on, the fraught political history between Syria and Lebanon, and how Boulos and Habak’s personal connection overcame those divisions.


“Without our journalistic relationship, [we] would have never been together. I would have never opened my heart to somebody like him,” says Boulos. “We can be any race, any gender, any religion, any background, but at the same time we’re all humans.”


Birds of War

 premiered at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival, where it won the World Cinema Documentary Special Jury Award for Journalistic Impact.

author: cnt.es
title: CNT valora positivamente el desarrollo de la huelga general del 11N y denuncia la actuación policial contra los piquetes
content:
Imagen

: 13:30h. Manifestación en Bilbao. Bloque propio | Fuente: CNT


La jornada está registrando paros importantes en distintos sectores y una notable movilización en las calles, mientras se repiten las actuaciones policiales contra piquetes en diferentes puntos del Estado.


La Confederación Nacional del Trabajo (CNT) realiza una valoración positiva del desarrollo de la huelga general convocada para este 11 de noviembre. La jornada está dejando importantes paros en distintos sectores productivos, una respuesta desigual según territorios y actividades, y una notable participación en las movilizaciones convocadas durante la mañana.


Los datos conocidos hasta el momento reflejan una incidencia importante en sectores como la automoción, la industria, la logística, los puertos y la recogida de residuos. La demanda eléctrica peninsular también está registrando una caída significativa respecto a jornadas laborables comparables, con diferencias que alcanzaban el 11,8 % respecto al miércoles anterior a primera hora de la mañana.


CNT señala que el seguimiento de una huelga no puede analizarse al margen de las condiciones laborales de cada sector. La precariedad, la temporalidad, el miedo a las represalias empresariales y la imposición de servicios mínimos abusivos dificultan especialmente el ejercicio del derecho de huelga en determinados ámbitos. Por ello, la diversidad de resultados no resta valor a una jornada que está demostrando capacidad de organización y respuesta colectiva.


La movilización también está teniendo una importante expresión en las calles. Las manifestaciones y concentraciones celebradas durante la mañana están registrando una asistencia elevada en distintos puntos del Estado, pese a las fuertes lluvias que están afectando a numerosas localidades y a tratarse de convocatorias en horario matinal. CNT espera que las movilizaciones previstas para esta tarde tengan igualmente una participación masiva.


CNT denuncia la extensión de las actuaciones policiales contra los piquetes


Junto al desarrollo de la huelga, CNT denuncia las actuaciones policiales registradas en distintos puntos del Estado contra piquetes y personas participantes en las movilizaciones. Cargas, golpes, utilización de gas pimienta, identificaciones y detenciones forman parte de los incidentes denunciados por las organizaciones sindicales durante la jornada.


La Confederación considera especialmente preocupante la extensión de este tipo de intervenciones. No se trata de prácticas desconocidas para los movimientos sociales y sindicales: actuaciones similares vienen produciéndose durante las movilizaciones por el derecho a la vivienda y otras protestas sociales. Por tanto, lo ocurrido durante esta huelga se enmarca en una dinámica represiva que las organizaciones sociales llevan tiempo denunciando.


CNT recuerda que el derecho de huelga está reconocido en el artículo 28.2 de la Constitución Española y que el ejercicio de este derecho incluye la actividad de los piquetes informativos. Las actuaciones policiales no pueden convertirse en un instrumento para obstaculizar la organización sindical ni para intimidar a quienes ejercen legítimamente sus derechos.


La organización exige que se investiguen los hechos denunciados, se depuren las responsabilidades correspondientes y se respete plenamente el ejercicio de los derechos sindicales y de manifestación.


La movilización continúa


Este balance es necesariamente provisional. Durante las próximas horas se conocerán nuevos datos sobre el seguimiento en sectores que todavía no han podido ofrecer cifras completas, así como sobre las movilizaciones previstas para la tarde.


CNT valora positivamente la respuesta que está teniendo esta huelga general y considera que la jornada debe servir para reforzar la organización y la capacidad de acción colectiva en los centros de trabajo y en los barrios. Asimismo, recuerda que la jornada del 11N es un paso más en la defensa de los derechos laborales y sociales. El trabajo de organización y movilización continúa.


La entrada

 se publicó primero en

Confederación Nacional del Trabajo

title: Flamingo-Revolution in Albanien gegen Jared Kushners Luxusresort im Schutzgebiet Vjosa-Narta betrifft längst mehr als Umweltschutz und Privatisierung
content:
Dossier


„

Eine Firma mit Verbindungen zum Schwiegersohn des US-Präsidenten will Hotelkomplexe in albanischen Schutzgebieten bauen. Der Regierungschef bestreitet eine Einigung. Bagger roden dennoch bereits Kiefernwald im Projektgebiet. Am Montag sind Tausende in Tirana, der Hauptstadt Albaniens, auf die Straße gegangen. Sie protestierten gegen ein Luxusresort-Projekt, das mit Jared Kushner, dem Schwiegersohn des früheren US-Präsidenten Donald Trump, in Verbindung steht. Das Investmentunternehmen Affinity Partners will küstennahe Feuchtgebiete in ein riesiges Ferienresort verwandeln. Das Projekt sieht Hotelkomplexe auf mehreren Hektar der geschützten Küstenzone Vjosa-Narta bei Zvernec und auf der unbewohnten Adriainsel Sazan vor

…“

Artikel von Anna Flori vom 02.06.2026 bei Euronews

 

 („Albanien: Tausende protestieren gegen Jared Kushners Luxusprojekt“) mit einem Video – siehe mehr Informationen:


Albanien: Studentenbewegung stellt Zweiparteiensystem in Frage. Regierungschef Rama setzt auf Repression, Oppositionsführer Berisha auf Vereinnahmung


„»

Rama ins Gefängnis, Berisha ins Gefängnis« – Mit diesem Banner empfingen albanische Studierende am Sonnabend vor dem Bildungsministerium in Tirana die Opposition. Anhänger der Demokratischen Partei (PD) von Sali Berisha waren von der Parteizentrale aus losmarschiert; die Studierenden hielten sie mit einer Menschenkette auf, es kam zu Handgreiflichkeiten. Vor dem Ministerium und auch am Regierungssitz verlagerte sich die Auseinandersetzung später in Richtung der Polizei: Steine, Böller und Molotowcocktails auf der einen Seite, Pfefferspray, Tränengas und Wasserwerfer auf der anderen.


Seit dem 13. Oktober fordert die Studentenbewegung den Rücktritt von Ministerpräsident Edi Rama. Doch der Sonnabend zeigte, dass sich die Demonstrationen nicht allein gegen die Regierungspartei richten. Dass auch die PD als Oppositionskraft adressiert wird, ist nicht neu. Bereits am 31. Oktober hatten die Studierenden PD-Abgeordnete mit dem Ruf »Die Opposition sind wir« aus ihren Reihen verwiesen. Am 2. November verbrannten die Demonstranten Puppen von Rama und Berisha auf einem Steintisch mit der Aufschrift »Dialog«, den der Premier vor seinem Amtssitz aufgestellt hatte. Rama und Berisha würden das Land seit 36 Jahren in Geiselhaft halten, so ein Aktivist gegenüber dem Portal balkanweb. (…)


Die Bewegung scheint nicht zu erlahmen: Laut der unabhängigen Demotrackingseite Pulsi gehörten die Demonstrationen an den Sonnabenden Ende Oktober zu den teilnehmerstärksten seit Anfang Juli. An diesem Mittwoch soll der nächste Protest stattfinden. Für den 28. November, den Unabhängigkeitstag, haben Aktivisten eine Massenkundgebung zusammen mit der »Flamingo-Bewegung« angekündigt. Offen bleibt die Frage, ob die Proteste – wie die serbische Studentenbewegung, die am 25. Oktober in Belgrad die Wahlen gewann – ohne Anbindung an eine Partei zu einer ernsthaften politischen Alternative werden können

.“

Artikel von Fabio Nacci in der jungen Welt vom 11.11.2026

 

 („»Die Opposition sind wir«“)


Gegen Regierung und Polizeigewalt: In Albanien schließen sich nach 1 Woche der Studierendenproteste und Unterrichtsboykotte auch Hunderte von Dozenten an


Dozenten schließen sich den Protesten der Studierenden an


„

Hunderte von Dozenten und Studenten versammelten sich am Dienstag um 10:00 Uhr auf dem Campus der Polytechnischen Universität, von wo aus sie in einer Solidaritätsbekundung zum Amt des Ministerpräsidenten marschierten. Der Marsch fand eine Woche nach Beginn der Studentenproteste statt, die von Zusammenstößen mit der Polizei und der Festnahme von Dutzenden Demonstranten begleitet waren. Die Kundgebung wurde von der Gewerkschaft der Hochschulbeschäftigten Albaniens organisiert, die die Studentenproteste seit mehreren Tagen unterstützt. Unter dem Motto „Stoppt die Gewalt gegen Studenten“ rief die Gewerkschaft die Dozenten dazu auf, Solidarität mit den jungen Menschen zu zeigen, und äußerte Besorgnis über die Polizeigewalt während der Proteste. title: Çanakkale Emek, Barış ve Demokrasi Platformu: İşçilerin yaşam hakkı sermayenin kâr hırsından değerlidir
content:
Çanakkale Emek, Barış ve Demokrasi Güçleri HABAŞ’ta 19 işçinin hayatını kaybettiği ve pek çok işçinin yaralandığı patlamaya karşı bugün İskele Meydanında eylem ve basın açıklaması yaptı. Açıklamada iş cinayetlerine dikkat çekilirken Çanakkale de Dardanel işçilerinin ücretlerinin ödenmemesine de tepki gösterildi. Açıklamayı Eğitim Sen Şube Başkanı İnal Akoğlu okudu.

İşçilerin bir kez daha alınmayan iş güvenliği önlemlerinin, denetimsizliğin ve sermayenin kâr hırsının bedelini canlarıyla ödediğini söyleyen Akoğlu, “Bugün burada yalnızca acımızı paylaşmak için değil, bu katliamın sorumlularından hesap sormak için bulunuyoruz. HABAŞ’ta yaşananlar sıradan bir iş kazası olarak değerlendirilemez. İlk bulgular, bakım çalışmaları sırasında tavan vincinin düşmesi ve gaz hattının zarar görmesiyle patlamanın meydana geldiğine işaret etmektedir. Ancak asıl sorgulanması gereken, böyle bir facianın yaşanmasına hangi ihmallerin, hangi denetimsizliklerin ve hangi çalışma koşullarının zemin hazırladığıdır. Üstelik aynı fabrikada son üç hafta içerisinde, 21 Ekim ve 5 Kasım tarihlerinde iki işçinin daha yaşamını yitirdiği açıklanmıştır. Daha önce yaşanan ölümlere rağmen gerekli önlemler alınmamış, etkin denetim sağlanmamışsa bunun adı ihmal değil, göz göre göre gelen bir işçi katliamıdır” ifadelerini kullandı.

Türkiye’de işçi ölümlerinin ve emek sömürüsünün artık münferit olaylar olmaktan çıktığını vurgulayan Akoğlu, “Madenlerde, fabrikalarda, inşaatlarda, tersanelerde emekçiler çalışırken ölmekte; farklı işkollarında çalışan milyonlarca emekçi ise güvencesizlik, düşük ücret, ücret gaspı ve ağır çalışma koşullarıyla karşı karşıya bırakılmaktadır. Her facianın ardından aynı açıklamalar yapılmakta, soruşturmalar başlatılmakta, sorumluların hesap vereceği söylenmekte; ancak işçilerin yaşamına mal olan ve emeğini değersizleştiren düzen değişmemektedir” şeklinde konuştu.

İş güvenliğinin yalnızca işverenlerin iyi niyetine bırakılamayacağının altını çizen Akoğlu, “Devletin denetim sorumluluğu, işverenin yükümlülükleri ve çalışanların yaşam hakkı tartışmasız biçimde güvence altına alınmalıdır.

Buradan açıkça ifade ediyoruz. İşçiler çalışırken ölmek zorunda değildir. İş cinayetleri kader değildir. Çanakkale’de yaşananlar da emekçilerin karşı karşıya bırakıldığı tablonun başka bir yüzünü göstermektedir. İlimizde faaliyet gösteren Dardanel fabrikasında çalışan işçilerin ücretlerini zamanında alamaması, emekçilerin en temel haklarından biri olan ücret hakkının dahi güvencesiz bırakıldığını ortaya koymaktadır. İşçinin emeğinin karşılığını alamaması, geçimini sağlayamaması ve ailesinin ihtiyaçlarını karşılayamaz hale getirilmesi kabul edilemez. Ücret, işverenin lütfu değil, işçinin alın terinin ve emeğinin karşılığıdır. HABAŞ’ta işçiler yaşamını yitirirken, Çanakkale’de işçiler emeklerinin karşılığını almak için mücadele etmek zorunda bırakılmaktadır. Farklı biçimlerde ortaya çıksa da her iki tabloyu yaratan anlayış aynıdır: Emeği ucuzlatan, işçiyi güvencesizleştiren ve sermayenin çıkarlarını emekçinin yaşamının önüne koyan düzen. Buradan Dardanel yönetimine de çağrımızdır: İşçilerin birikmiş ücret alacakları derhal ve eksiksiz ödenmeli, emekçilerin ekonomik ve sosyal hakları güvence altına alınmalıdır” dedi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Unknown
title: İspanya: Kiracıların isyanı genel greve dönüştü
content:
İspanya'da kiracı derneklerinin başlattığı barınma hakkı mücadelesi, ülkenin iki büyük sendika konfederasyonu CCOO ve UGT'nin katılımıyla 24 saatlik genel greve dönüştü. “Ücretler. Konut. Fiyatlar.” sloganıyla düzenlenen grev, sanayi tesislerinde üretimi durdurdu, ulaşımı aksattı ve onlarca kentte gösterilerle sürdü.


Madrid, Barselona ve diğer kentlerde grev gözcülerine yönelik polis müdahaleleri yaşandı. İçişleri Bakanlığı'nın gün içindeki verilerine göre 42 kişi gözaltına alındı.


Madrid'deki Mercamadrid toptancı halinde polisin biber gazı kullanmasının ardından en az 13 kişi sağlık ekiplerinin yardımına ihtiyaç duydu. Sendikalar müdahaleleri grev hakkının ihlali olarak nitelendirerek sorumlular hakkında hukuki girişim başlatacaklarını açıkladı.


Fabrikalarda üretim durdu, ulaşım aksadı


CCOO ve UGT, grevin özellikle otomotiv, limanlar, enerji ve ulaşım sektörlerinde etkili olduğunu bildirdi.


Sendikaların açıkladığı oranlara göre otomotiv ve deniz ve hava limanlarında iş bırakma yüzde 90'a, et üretiminde yüzde 85'e, çöp toplama işlerinde yüzde 82'ye, enerji sektöründe ise yüzde 75'e ulaştı.


Barselona yakınlarındaki SEAT Martorell fabrikasında üretim durdu. Navarra'daki Volkswagen tesislerinde de geniş çaplı iş bırakıldı. 


Tren seferleri olağan kapasitenin yüzde 50 ila 75'iyle sürdürüldü. Havalimanlarında 234 uçuş iptal edildi. Barselona'da metro ve otobüs seferleri sınırlandırıldı. Katalonya'da otoyollar, sanayi bölgeleri ve tren istasyonları çevresinde grev gözcüleri toplandı.


Eğitim kurumlarında da iş bırakma görüldü. Ancak perakende ticaret, küçük işletmeler ve bazı kamu hizmetlerinde katılım daha sınırlı kaldı.


Sendikalar grevin başarılı olduğunu açıklarken, işveren örgütleri katılımın düşük kaldığını savundu. Kiracılar Sendikası yaklaşık 4 milyon kişinin greve katıldığı öngörüsünü paylaştı. 


“Polisin görevi grev hakkını güvence altına almak”


CCOO Genel Sekreteri Unai Sordo, Mercamadrid'deki polis müdahalesini eleştirdi:


“Bu tam bir skandal. Yaşadıklarımızın cezai ve her türlü sorumluluğunun hesabını soracağız.”


UGT Genel Sekreteri Pepe Álvarez de polisin grev hakkını güvence altına almakla yükümlü olduğunu söyledi.


Polis, bazı göstericilerin yolları ve işyerlerinin girişlerini kapattığını bildirdi. Barselona'da lastiklerin yakıldığı barikatlar kuruldu; çeşitli kentlerde göstericilerle polis arasında arbede yaşandı.


“36 yaşındayım, hâlâ kendi başıma bir eve çıkamıyorum”


Genel grevin kaynağı, İspanya'da giderek ağırlaşan konut krizi. 


Madrid'de bir hastanenin bilgi işlem bölümünde çalışan 36 yaşındaki Jesús González, Reuters'a barınma sorununu kendi yaşamından hareketle anlattı:


“36 yaşındayım ve hâlâ kendi başıma bir eve çıkamıyorum.”


Ülkede ortalama kiralar son 10 yılda neredeyse iki katına çıktı. İspanya Gençlik Konseyi'nin hesaplamalarına göre ortalama aylık kira, genç bir çalışanın ortalama ücretinin neredeyse tamamına denk geliyor. 


Barselonalı 45 yaşındaki işçi Carlos Ferrer de Associated Press'e yaptığı açıklamada genel grevin gerekçesini şöyle anlattı:


“Yetkililerin bir şeyler yapması için yurttaşların baskısını hissetmeleri gerekiyor.”


Kiracı örgütleri kira artışlarının sınırlandırılmasını, sözleşmelerin otomatik yenilenmesini, tahliyelerin önlenmesini ve konut spekülasyonunun durdurulmasını istiyor.


Maricarmen'in tahliyesinden genel greve


Greve giden süreç, Madrid'de 87 yaşındaki Maricarmen Abascal'ın evinden zorla tahliye edilmesi ve ardından hayatını kaybetmesi üzerine büyüyen protestolarla hızlandı.


Kiracı örgütleri, hükümetin konut krizine karşı hazırladığı bazı önlemlerin 2 Ekim'de parlamentoda sağ partilerin oylarıyla reddedilmesinin ardından düzenlenen kitlesel gösterilerde genel grev çağrısını yükseltti.


Kiracılar Sendikası sözcüsü Alicia del Río, 11 Kasım'da şöyle konuştu:


“Maricarmen'in tahliyesiyle 40 gün önce başlayan öfke büyümeyi sürdürdü ve şimdi kentlerimizin sokaklarına taştı.”


Del Río, konutların yatırım ve rant aracı haline getirilmesine karşı mücadele ettiklerini belirtti:


“Evler, rantiyeci azınlığa hizmet etmek için değil, içinde yaşamak içindir.”


Kiracı örgütleri sendikaları harekete geçirdi


11 Kasım grevinin ayırt edici yanı, çağrının başlangıçta işçi sendikalarından değil, kiracı örgütlerinden gelmesiydi.


Kiracılar Sendikası, büyük konfederasyonlar katılmasa da küçük sendikalarla birlikte genel greve gideceğini duyurmuştu. CGT gibi örgütler çağrıya erken destek verdi. CCOO ve UGT ise 5 Ekim'de greve katılma kararı …

author: infolibre
title: Τέλος ενός κόσμου: Ευρωπαϊκοί ξεσηκωμοί, αμερικάνικοι σεισμοί!
content:
Σκίτσο της Σόνιας Μητραλιά


Του Γ

ιώργου Μητραλιά


Υπάρχουν -σπάνιες- στιγμές στις οποίες η ιστορία της ανθρωπότητας επιταχύνεται σε βαθμό που να προκαλεί ίλιγγο. Και αυτό ακριβώς συμβαίνει σε αυτό το ανεπανάληπτο φθινόπωρο του 2026, που βλέπει τους τυράννους να τρέμουν, ακόμα και να καταρρέουν κάτω από τα ταυτόχρονα πλήγματα των λαών που εξεγείρονται σε μια ντουζίνα χώρες, κυρίως στην Ευρώπη αλλά και πέρα από αυτήν. Είναι σαν να παρακολουθούμε την επανάληψη της πολύ μακρινής «Άνοιξης των Λαών» του 1848, με τη (σημαντική) διαφορά ότι σήμερα το επίκεντρο αυτών των λαϊκών σεισμών βρίσκεται στην απέναντι ακτή του Ατλαντικού, στις Ηνωμένες Πολιτείες της Αμερικής.


Ας μιλήσουμε λοιπόν για τις Ηνωμένες Πολιτείες και τον ιστορικό σεισμό που συνιστούν τα αποτελέσματα των πολυδιαφημισμένων ενδιάμεσων εκλογών τους. Τελικά, αν υπάρχει κάτι που προκαλεί έκπληξη, αυτό δεν είναι τόσο

η συντριπτική ήττα

 των Ρεπουμπλικάνων (1), όσο μάλλον η έκταση του θριάμβου των αντιπάλων του Τραμπισμού. Πράγματι, ενώ οι δημοσκοπήσεις προέβλεπαν την πιθανή εκλογή ενός Δημοκρατικού ακόμη και στο Κάνσας μετά από 94 χρόνια (!), σχεδόν κανείς, με εξαίρεση τον ίδιο τον ενδιαφερόμενο, δεν πίστευε στην εκλογή ενός Αφροαμερικανού στο Μισισιπή μετά από… 150 χρόνια, μετά από ενάμιση ολάκερο αιώνα! Τι συνέβη, λοιπόν, και φτάσαμε σε μια τέτοια ιστορική ανατροπή;


Η απάντηση σε αυτό το ερώτημα, που έχει κρίσιμη σημασία για την συνέχεια των γεγονότων, δίνεται από την πολύ σοβαρή και αξιόπιστη

δημοσκόπηση

 του CNN (2) αμέσως μετά το κλείσιμο των καλπών. Και το πρώτο πράγμα που μας δείχνει αυτή η δημοσκόπηση είναι ότι η πλειοψηφία εκείνων που ψήφισαν υπέρ των Δημοκρατικών υποψηφίων δεν αυτοπροσδιορίζονται ως… Δημοκρατικοί. Πράγματι, το 35% αυτών αυτοπροσδιορίζεται ως «ανεξάρτητοι» και το 23% ως «Δημοκράτες Σοσιαλιστές (DSA)». Πράγμα που σημαίνει ότι το 58% των δημοκρατικών ψηφοφόρων απορρίπτει το Δημοκρατικό Κόμμα και ψηφίζει υπέρ του μόνο και μόνο επειδή θέλει να απαλλαγεί από τους Ρεπουμπλικάνους του Τραμπ! Με αυτά λοιπόν τα δεδομένα, το ερώτημα που προκύπτει είναι ποιο είναι το κύριο κίνητρό τους όταν επιλέγουν μια τέτοια πολιτική στάση. Η απάντηση της δημοσκόπησης του CNN διαψεύδει κατηγορηματικά όλα όσα λέγονται και γράφονται για το θέμα αυτό: το πρώτο (47%) κίνητρο των δημοκρατικών ψηφοφόρων ονομάζεται «

democracy

» και βρίσκεται πολύ μπροστά από το δεύτερο, που ονομάζεται «

economy

» (37%).


Συνοψίζοντας, οι Δημοκρατικοί ψηφοφόροι παρακινήθηκαν κυρίως να ψηφίσουν όπως ψήφισαν, όχι λόγω των –πολύ πραγματικών– υλικών προβλημάτων τους που απορρέουν από τις αποτυχίες της οικονομικής πολιτικής του Τραμπ, αλλά μάλλον λόγω της επιθυμίας τους να υπερασπιστούν όλα όσα αντιπροσωπεύει η «δημοκρατία», όπως δηλαδή τις δημοκρατικές και κοινωνικές ελευθερίες και δικαιώματα που απειλούνται άμεσα από τον Τραμπ και το αντιδημοκρατικό και φασιστοειδές καθεστώς του! Είναι λοιπόν αυτονόητο ότι ένα τέτοιο κίνητρο προδίδει την ύπαρξη μιας πολιτικής συνείδησης πολύ πιο προχωρημένης από εκείνη που περιορίζεται να αντιδρά (ακόμη και βίαια) στα υλικά προβλήματα της καθημερινής ζωής.


Κατά συνέπεια, δεν είναι τυχαίο ότι αυτή η δημοσκόπηση του CNN επιβεβαιώνει αυτό που τόσες άλλες είχαν διαπιστώσει προηγουμένως: δηλαδή, ότι ένας ολοένα και μεγαλύτερος αριθμός Αμερικανών πολιτών απορρίπτει τον καπιταλισμό και τάσσεται υπέρ του «σοσιαλισμού», ακόμα κι αν ο “σοσιαλισμός¨” του είναι κάτι συγκεχυμένο και όχι πολύ σαφές. Και αυτό εξηγεί με τη σειρά του, τη σημαντική επιτυχία των «σοσιαλιστών», ριζοσπαστικών προοδευτικών και λοιπών αριστερών υποψηφίων στις ενδιάμεσες εκλογές. Έτσι, οι DSA κατάφεραν να εκλέξουν μια συντρόφισσά τους δήμαρχο του Λος Άντζελες, με αποτέλεσμα οι δύο μεγαλύτερες πόλεις της χώρας, η Νέα Υόρκη και το Λος Άντζελες, καθώς και η διοικητική της πρωτεύουσα, η Ουάσιγκτον D.C., να έχουν πλέον δημάρχους των DSA! Και επιπλέον, οι DSA πέτυχαν να εκλέξουν 8 από τα μέλη τους στη Βουλή των Αντιπροσώπων, στα οποία θα πρέπει να προστεθούν τουλάχιστον άλλοι 6 επίσης νεοεκλεγμένοι βουλευτές, οι προεκλογικές εκστρατείες των οποίων υποστηρίχθηκαν ενεργά από τους DSA.


Ωστόσο, αν και αποτελούν τη μεγαλύτερη αριστερή οργάνωση της χώρας, οι Δημοκρατικοί Σοσιαλιστές της Αμερικής (DSA) απέχουν πολύ από το να οργανώνουν ή να εκπροσωπούν όλους τους σοσιαλιστές, τους προοδευτικούς ριζοσπάστες και λοιπούς αριστερούς, τόσο στην κοινωνία όσο και στο Κογκρέσο των Ηνωμένων Πολιτειών. Εξάλλου, πρέπει να αναμένεται ότι βοηθούσης της πολύ βαθιάς κοινωνικής και πολιτικής κρίσης, οι …

title: Rinviato lo sgombero della palazzina di Piazza Miraglia a Napoli
content:
Riceviamo e pubblichiamo il comunicato del Laboratorio Occupato SKA:


Oggi la resistenza dex abitanti di ZIA ADA, occupazione abitativa di piazza Miraglia, ha impedito il tentativo di sgombero di fronte a un dispiegamento di forze senza precedenti.


Contro il progetto speculativo dell’Ordine dei Servi di Maria, determinato a lasciare le persone per strada senza alcun riguardo per le condizioni di fragilità sociale, pretendiamo soluzioni abitative dignitose per tuttx lx abitanti di ZIA ADA, che non strappino le persone dai propri quartieri e dalle proprie reti sociali. La Napoli ormai diventata città vetrina non ha bisogno di ulteriori strutture ricettive o di studentati privati a costi insostenibili, ma di politiche abitative reali e concrete, oltre la monocoltura turistica e al di fuori di ogni speculazione elettorale. Ogni occupazione sarà una barricata, piazza Miraglia non si sgombera!


NAPOLI: OTTENUTI 10 GIORNI DI RINVIO ALLO SGOMBERO DI PALAZZO MIRAGLIA


da

Radio Blackout


Alle 5 di mattina di oggi, mercoledì 11 Novembre, si sono presentate le camionette sotto l’occupazione di piazza Luigi Miraglia per procedere allo sgombero. Il palazzo, occupato dal 2014, 

ospita 30 famiglie

 e storiocamente ha fornito rifugio per donne in condizione di fragilita e soggettività lgbtqia+. Il tenvtativo di sgombero segue al primo accesso dell’ufficiale giudiziario avvenuto mercoledì 4 Novembre. 


La solidarietà e la resistenza degli occupanti hanno ottenuto il rivnio dello sgombero di 10 giorni e l’avvio di un tavolo politico per trovare una soluzione abitativa agli occupanti.


Lo sgombero intendeva destinare l’immobile alla costruzione di uno studentato di lusso e si inserisce perfettamente nel 

clima di speculazione immobiliare

 che imperversa nel centro storico di Napoli. 


Il collegamento in diretta con Davide dello 

Sportello Casa Napoli

:


Aggiornamento sul compagno dello spazio Giardino Liberato portato in questura mentre cercava di raggiungere gli occupati superando il cordone di polizia: il presidio alla questura ne ha ottenuto lo scarceramento.

title: Karkerekî din ku di teqîna HABAŞê de bi giranî birîndar bibû, mir
content:
Abdullah Kilinçê ku di teqîna 9ê Cotmehê de li Kargeha Hesin û Pola ya HABAŞê ya li navçeya Aliagaya Îzmîrê giran birîndar bibû, di nexweşxaneya ku lê dihat dermankirin de jiyana xwe ji dest da.


Li Îzmîrê di kargehê de teqîn pêk hat: Hejmara miriyan derket 18an


10 Mijdar 2026


Kilinç piştî teqînê di destpêkê de biribûn Nexweşxaneya Dewletê ya Aliagayê û paşê sewqî Nexweşxaneya Perwerde û Lêkolînê ya Çigliyê ya Zanîngeha Bakirçaya Îzmîrê kiribûn.


Dermankirina şeş karkerên ku di teqînê de birîndar bibûn di nexweşxaneyan de berdewam dike.


Derbarê karkerên ku di teqîna HABAŞê de mirin em çi dizanin?


10 Mijdar 2026


Hejmara qurbaniyên HABAŞê gihîşt 19an


Ajansa Anadolyê (AA) nivîsî ku bi mirina Abdullah Kilinç re hejmara kesên ku di teqînê de jiyana xwe ji dest dane gihîştiye 18an. Lêbelê di lîsteya AAyê de navê Guner Gokçe cih nagire.


Cîgirê Wezîrê Dadê Can Tuncay, duh (10ê Cotmehê) piştî lêkolîna li tesîsê ji rojnamegeran re gotibû: “Li gorî serlêdana malbatan cenazeyê karkerekî me nehatiye dîtin. Lêkolînên li cihê bûyerê berdewam dikin.”


Piştî vê daxuyaniyê, hin ajansên nûçeyan, platformên nûçeyan ên herêmî û Meclisa İSİGê ragihandin ku termê karkerê bi navê Guner Gokçe di bin kavilan de hatiye dîtin. Ji bo Gokçeyê ku li Paşaliya (navê wê ê berê Berdik) ser bi navçeya Şenkayaya Erzurumê ji dayik bûye, di rûpeleke civata herêmî de jî peyama serxweşiyê hat weşandin.


Navên 19 karkerên ku jiyana xwe ji dest dane bi vî rengî ne:


Abdülkadir Kınacı, Abdullah Kılınç, Barış Güney, Ceylan Bıyıklı, Ersin Oğuz, Fatih Işık, Ferhat Maraşlı, Göksel Ünaldı, Güner Gökçe, Hüsnü Ersoy, İlker Sığırtmaçoğlu, Kadir Kaan Özçelik, Mustafa Sert, Orhan Altay, Özcan Efe, Recep Fedai, Serkan Kurt, Uğur Temel, Yasin Taşçı.

, πιάνουμε το νήμα των θανάτων σε καθεστώς κράτησης στην Ελλάδα.


Παρακολουθήστε την εκπομπή Το Νήμα στο

:


YouTube


PeerTube


Spotify


Το Νήμα: Δείτε όλες τις εκπομπές


Η έρευνα συγκεντρώνει για πρώτη φορά σε ένα ενιαίο

δημόσια προσβάσιμο αρχείο

 στοιχεία για θανάτους σε αστυνομικά τμήματα, προαναχωρησιακά κέντρα κράτησης, κατά τη μεταγωγή κρατουμένων και σε νοσοκομεία όπου οι θανόντες εξακολουθούσαν να βρίσκονται υπό αστυνομική κράτηση.


Διαβάστε εδώ τη δημοσίευση των ερευνητών:

Building an archive of deaths in Greek immigration detention centres


Από τους 112 καταγεγραμμένους θανάτους, 81 σημειώθηκαν σε αστυνομικά τμήματα και 27 σε προαναχωρησιακά κέντρα κράτησης. Οι 82 νεκροί ήταν άνδρες, τέσσερις γυναίκες, ενώ σε 26 περιπτώσεις δεν καταγράφεται φύλο. Από τα 70 άτομα των οποίων είναι γνωστή η ηλικία, τα 45 ήταν κάτω των 40 ετών, με διάμεση ηλικία τα 33,5 χρόνια.


Σοβαρά κενά και αντιφάσεις στα στοιχεία της ΕΛ.ΑΣ.


Οι ερευνητές συγκέντρωσαν στοιχεία μέσω αιτημάτων πρόσβασης σε δημόσια πληροφορία προς την ΕΛ.ΑΣ., τα οποία αφορούσαν μεταξύ άλλων τις

αυτοκτονίες σε αστυνομικά τμήματα από το 2000 έως το 2024

, τους

θανάτους αλλοδαπών σε αστυνομικά τμήματα

 και τους

θανάτους σε προαναχωρησιακά κέντρα

.


Από τη διασταύρωση προέκυψε ότι 34 θάνατοι που είχαν καταγραφεί από δημοσιογράφους, οργανώσεις και φορείς παρακολούθησης

απουσίαζαν από τις στατιστικές που χορήγησε η αστυνομία

. Για άλλους 25 θανάτους, τα αστυνομικά στοιχεία περιλάμβαναν ουσιαστικά μόνο το έτος και τη γεωγραφική περιοχή.


Εντοπίστηκαν επίσης αντιφάσεις ανάμεσα σε διαφορετικές επίσημες καταγραφές. Για παράδειγμα, ενώ στα στοιχεία αυτοκτονιών αναφέρεται θάνατος αλλοδαπού στην Αθήνα το 2002, στα συγκεντρωτικά στοιχεία θανάτων αλλοδαπών υπό αστυνομική κράτηση δεν εμφανίζεται κανένας θάνατος την ίδια χρονιά.


Η ΕΛ.ΑΣ. αρνήθηκε να χορηγήσει συμπληρωματικές πληροφορίες, επικαλούμενη αρχικά

το απόρρητο ερευνών

.


Μια χαρακτηριστική απάντηση της ΕΛ.ΑΣ. σε αίτημα πρόσβασης σε δημόσια δεδομένα.


Μετά από παρέμβαση του Συνηγόρου του Πολίτη, η Ελληνική Αστυνομία επικαλέστηκε το ότι οι πληροφορίες δεν τηρούνται σε ψηφιακές βάσεις και τον

υπερβολικό διοικητικό φόρτο

.


Οι ερευνητές εκτιμούν ότι

ο πραγματικός αριθμός θανάτων πιθανότατα είναι μεγαλύτερος

, καθώς η

ανεξάρτητη παρακολούθηση

 των εγκαταστάσεων είναι περιορισμένη και η

πρόσβαση δικηγόρων, συγγενών και οργανώσεων

 συναντά σημαντικά εμπόδια. Επιπλέον, η κατάσχεση τηλεφώνων, οι περιορισμοί στην επικοινωνία και καταγγελλόμενες πρακτικές εκφοβισμού δυσχεραίνουν τη δημοσιοποίηση περιστατικών κακομεταχείρισης.


Ελλείψεις στην υγειονομική περίθαλψη


Ιδιαίτερη έμφαση δίνεται στην πρόσβαση των κρατουμένων σε ιατρική φροντίδα. Στα αστυνομικά τμήματα δεν υπάρχει ιατρικό προσωπικό, ενώ στα προαναχωρησιακά κέντρα η υγειονομική περίθαλψη παρέχεται από την

ΑΕΜΥ

, με ευρωπαϊκή χρηματοδότηση.


Ωστόσο, σύμφωνα με μαρτυρίες κρατουμένων, αιτήματα ιατρικής βοήθειας συχνά αγνοούνται ή καθυστερούν, ενώ αστυνομικοί παρεμβάλλονται ανάμεσα στους ασθενείς και τους υγειονομικούς.


Στην Αμυγδαλέζα, σύμφωνα με τα

τελευταία διαθέσιμα στοιχεία του Απριλίου 2026

, υπηρετούσαν μόλις επτά επαγγελματίες υγείας για 666 κρατουμένους: δύο γιατροί, δύο νοσηλευτές, δύο επισκέπτες υγείας και ένας οδοντίατρος.


Παράλληλα, το ευρωπαϊκά χρηματοδοτούμενο

πρόγραμμα AMIF 018

 καλύπτει τις αποδοχές 97 συνοριοφυλάκων, στους οποίους ανατίθενται και αρμοδιότητες σχετικές με τη διασφάλιση ιατρικών εξετάσεων και μεταφορών σε νοσοκομεία.


Συνεντεύξεις με εργαζομένους της ΑΕΜΥ αναδεικνύουν ανεπαρκή εποπτεία, μεγάλη εναλλαγή προσωπικού, ελλείψεις εξοπλισμού και παρεμπόδιση της πρόσβασης σε γιατρούς από αστυνομικούς. Οι ερευνητές επισημαίνουν ότι η ύπαρξη υγειονομικού προσωπικού δεν εγγυάται ουσιαστική πρόσβαση σε περίθαλψη.


Το νέο νομοθετικό πλαίσιο


Η δημοσίευση της έρευνας πραγματοποιείται έναν χρόνο μετά την ψήφιση του

Ν. 5226/2025

, ο οποίος αυστηροποίησε το πλαίσιο αντιμετώπισης της παράτυπης εισόδου και παραμονής στη χώρα.

author: Mebratu Kelecha
title: Who can make peace hold?
content:
On October 4, Ethiopian government forces and their Tigrayan allies entered Mekelle

 after fighters loyal to the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) withdrew from the city. Twelve days later, Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed

announced a new caretaker administration

, promising to restore public services, help displaced families return, and prepare elections. From Addis Ababa, this appeared to mark the beginning of a political reset. But the situation in Tigray was far less settled. Armed factions continued to contest authority,

hundreds of thousands of people remained displaced

, and the

territorial disputes

 that had helped fuel the last war were unresolved. Mekelle had changed hands. Whether Ethiopia had moved any closer to peace was another question.

The five-member caretaker administration has six months to begin rebuilding Tigray’s public institutions, and its officials will operate under federal oversight

. Yet the military retreat that preceded its appointment did not end armed resistance.

Some former combatants have sought to return to civilian life; other commanders have vowed to keep fighting

. The

TPLF has also joined an opposition alliance with Amhara and Oromo armed groups

, even as Ethiopia’s relations with its former wartime ally

Eritrea have deteriorated into a border crisis

. This is the government’s dilemma: It must restore everyday order while the alliances, territorial claims, and chains of command that determine that order remain contested.

To understand the danger, it helps to recall how Ethiopia reached this point.

For nearly three decades, the TPLF was the most influential party

 in a ruling coalition that governed a formally federal state through an unusually centralized political system. Abiy’s rise in 2018 disrupted that arrangement. His rapprochement with Eritrean President Isaias Afwerki ended two decades of hostility, but the growing confrontation between Addis Ababa and Tigray culminated in war in November 2020.

Eritrean troops and Amhara forces joined the federal campaign against the TPLF

. Their common enemy concealed sharply different visions of the peace that would follow.

The African Union–brokered

Pretoria agreement of November 2022

 ended the main phase of the fighting. It was not an empty ceasefire. The federal government and the TPLF

pledged to protect civilians, restore services, allow humanitarian access and establish a transitional administration

; disarmament and political dialogue were also envisaged. A

subsequent agreement in Nairobi

 linked the surrender of Tigrayan heavy weapons to the withdrawal of foreign and nonfederal forces. That sequencing mattered: One side could scarcely be expected to disarm confidently while forces it feared remained in place.

The agreement’s weakness lay less in what it promised than in who could deliver.

Eritrea was not a signatory

.

Amhara armed groups that had helped prosecute the war

 did not necessarily answer to federal negotiators. The TPLF, meanwhile, could sign for Tigray without ensuring that its own leadership and fighters would remain united. Pretoria brought a terrible war to a halt, but it could not freeze the balance of power among those expected to implement it. Peace required not only consent at the negotiating table but authority over armed men, budgets and territory.

Western Tigray illustrates why these distinctions are more than diplomatic technicalities. The area, claimed by Amhara actors as Welkait, changed hands during the war. Human Rights Watch and Amnesty International

documented mass expulsions and abuses against Tigrayan civilians

. In April 2026, Human Rights Watch reported that Tigrayan residents

continued to face restrictions on identity documents, movement, work and access to land

. For displaced families, territorial settlement means the possibility of returning home. For authorities entrenched since the war, it may entail surrendering offices, property, and economic advantage. A boundary left unresolved does not stand still when those controlling it can determine who is allowed to live there.

Disarmament poses a similarly concrete problem. A

United Nations–supported reintegration program began in 2024

, and former fighters have continued to register. But registration is not reintegration. A man who hands over his weapon without secure work, protection or confidence in the local authorities may be available to the next recruiter. Nor is reintegration solely a Tigrayan …

author: The Elephant
title: Alternative Leadership As A Decolonial Paradigm
content:
Sarova Stanley, Nairobi | 11 November 2026


Theme: Reimagining Leadership, Reclaiming Citizen Agency


Dr. Kawive Wambua;


The leadership and team of Inuka Kenya Ni Sisi!;

Representatives of civil society;

Distinguished guests;

Fellow Kenyans:


Good morning.


Thank you for inviting me to join you at the launch of the Inuka! Angaza Kura Campaign.


Your theme, “Reimagining Leadership, Reclaiming Citizen Agency,” brings us to the central question of our democracy: The Constitution proclaims Sovereignty of the people, but who truly exercises power in Kenya?


Is it the citizen whose taxes sustain the state, whose labour builds the economy, and whose vote confers authority? Or is it the officeholder who, once elected, hijacks power and behaves like the master, relegating citizens to subjects?


What must the citizens do to reclaim their agency, their power? 


You have asked me to reflect on “Alternative Leadership as a Decolonial Paradigm.”


The language may sound academic, but the issue is profoundly practical.


It concerns the relationship between a Kenyan citizen and the person entrusted to serve them. It concerns whether a police officer offers protection or inspires fear; whether a public office provides a service or demands a favour; whether public money builds opportunity or finances private privilege.


Above all, it concerns whether independence has become an everyday experience of dignity and quality services for us. 


From subjects to citizens


The colonial state was organised to control people and extract resources. Its authority flowed downwards. The population was expected to comply, while those who governed were insulated from meaningful accountability to the governed.


Independence was supposed to transform that relationship.


Yet changing the nationality of those occupying public office could not, by itself, dismantle the habits, incentives and institutions of domination, without changing the mindset of the office holders. Understanding leadership to be service and sacrifice, rather than entitlement and a life of privilege at the expense of basic needs for the people. Imagining leadership as an opportunity to ensure protection of the rights of the people and to uphold and affirm the dignity of the people you serve. Ensuring that, as a leader, you remain loyal to the purpose- service with openness and accountability. These are the minimum standards demanded by the constitution we gifted ourselves. 


Whenever leadership demands obedience without accountability, the colonial model or inheritance survives. Whenever citizens must seek political patronage to obtain public services, it survives. Whenever criticism is treated as disloyalty, it survives.


Decolonising leadership therefore requires us to confront the exercise of power in our own time.


We must ask whether the state serves citizens as people with rights, or manages them as subjects who should remain grateful for favours.


A hospital is a public responsibility. A road is a public investment. Education is an investment in the nation’s future. Every service by leaders is part of their duty to us, funded by our taxes, not a favour. 


None of these should become a personal gift for which citizens owe a politician their silence. Service should not be in exchange for citizens losing their freedom to exercise their right to demand accountability. Service must never be at the cost of citizens losing their agency, their power to oversee leaders, the government. 


An alternative must be radically different in word and deed. 


Comrades,


The word “alternative” carries an obligation.


Those of us who seek to offer alternative leadership must demonstrate how we would govern differently. We must affirm our allegiance to the Constitution, whose main objective is to restrain, or in other words, limit the exercise of power.  Alternative leadership must affirm citizens’ right to seek accountability and readiness to vacate office should citizens unequivocally so demand. The Alternative leadership must pledge allegiance to the Constitution and the people of Kenya, and affirm the sovereignty of the people. Demonstrate an understanding that leadership is a privilege to serve, not a title deed to rule over the people. Our utterances and actions as alternative leadership must so demonstrate. 


It is insufficient to condemn arrogance in government while practising it within our political parties. We cannot promise inclusion while silencing young …

author: AfricanFeminism
title: Eight Years in Prison for Fighting Anti-Black Racism in Tunisia: Free Saadia Mosbah!
content:
For years, Saadia Mosbah has been one of the leading voices against anti-Black racism in Tunisia. As president of the anti-racism organisation Mnemty, she has stood up for Black Tunisians and Black migrants alike. When


violence against Black migrants escalated

 after President Kais Saied’s February 2023 statement against African migrants, she became a target of online hate campaigns.


On May 6, 2024, she was arrested. On March 19, 2026, she was sentenced to eight years in prison and a heavy fine on charges of money laundering and illicit enrichment. On June 23, the Tunis Court of Appeals upheld her conviction, along with those of five Mnemty colleagues and associates. A final appeal, filed on June 29, is now before the Court of Cassation.


Human rights movements and organisations,


including Amnesty International

, have denounced the irregularities in the proceedings and the lack of evidence for the alleged offences. They have also raised the alarm over the racist treatment and violence Saadia has reportedly suffered in detention.


Saadia’s case sits within a wider pattern of repression. Since President Kais Saied seized sweeping powers in July 2021, Tunisia has slid back into authoritarian rule. Since May 2024, the month of Saadia’s arrest, the authorities have waged

a systematic crackdown on civil society

: activists prosecuted, organisations suspended, independent voices jailed. Throughout, the European Union has kept its

2023 migration deal with Tunisia

 in place, funding the country to stop people crossing to Europe and outsourcing its borders to a government that imprisons those who defend Black migrants. In this climate of repression and European complicity, Saadia’s voice and her freedom matter more than ever.


Saadia is more than a case file. Below, three activists tell their stories of the woman they know and the movement she helped build. Read them, then join the call for her immediate and unconditional release and for the convictions to be overturned. Keep fighting for those who fight for us in an anti-Black world.


 


Saadia’s Imprisonment Inseparable from Criminalisation of Black Organising and Solidarity


I first met Saadia Mosbah shortly after the 2011 Tunisian Revolution, when she was active in feminist organisations. Over the years that followed, I witnessed her unwavering commitment to the struggle for Black dignity, justice, and liberation in Tunisia. I watched her organisation, Mnemty, grow. And I watched a dream grow alongside it: the dream of a Tunisia where racism would no longer be denied, normalised, or left unpunished. 


A Tunisia with a law explicitly criminalising racial discrimination. Saadia was determined to bring together as many voices as possible around this struggle. She openly confronted a reality that many preferred to ignore: a significant part of Tunisia’s supposedly progressive and activist civil society remained silent on racism. Even within movements claiming to fight for equality and justice, Black people were too often expected to fight their battles alone.


Saadia refused that silence. She refused to make racism a secondary issue, or to soften her political demands to make others more comfortable.


But through years of persistence, political courage, and collective organising, she helped build a movement strong enough to achieve a historic victory: the adoption of Tunisia’s law against racial discrimination in 2018.


Years later, in 2023, I had the privilege and honour of working alongside Saadia to organise a march against state racism. Following the Tunisian presidency’s disgraceful statement targeting sub-Saharan African migrants, she was there, standing with us on the anti-fascist front line, organising, mobilising, supporting, and defending Black people and migrants in Tunisia. Saadia knew the risks. She understood what it meant to confront state racism in an increasingly authoritarian political climate. Yet she refused to retreat.


Today, Saadia est en prison. Her imprisonment is inseparable from the criminalisation of Black political organising, anti-racist resistance, and solidarity with migrants.


Saadia’s story is also a reminder that political victories are never irreversible.


A law can be adopted while the structures of domination it was meant to challenge remain intact. Rights written into legislation mean little when those who fought for them are deprived of their freedom.


But Saadia’s struggle is bigger than her imprisonment. It …

author: Lovin Kobusingye
title: Africa Can’t Build a Blue Economy Without the Women Who Bring Its Fish to Market
content:
Before dawn, wherever Africa has a coast or a lake, women wait on the shore for the boats. When the catch lands, our work begins. We smoke, dry, salt or ferment the fish, using skills passed down for generations, and carry it to market. We are more than a quarter of the

12.3 million people

 who work in Africa’s fisheries, and

58 percent

 of its fish processors.


In July, African ministers meeting in Luanda promised women, youth and local communities at least

40 percent representation

 in blue economy advisory bodies and financing programmes. The African Union Commission has been tasked with drafting the roadmap to deliver it. Unless that roadmap names women fish processors and traders, and removes the rules that keep us from credit, the promise will pass us by.


 


Many countries still count fisheries only by what happens in the water, so the millions of women who process and trade the catch barely register. But if you are invisible, you receive invisible budgets, invisible investments and invisible policies.


I am one of these women. I run a fish-processing business in Uganda, where our lakes yield more than half a million tonnes of fish a year, more than any other African country’s inland waters. I also represent a network of women fish processors and traders across 46 African countries, and though we are proud of the work we do, we know we can do even more.


We feed our children with the day’s catch. We keep our culture and cuisine alive in the markets, from the sun-dried mukene of Uganda’s lakes to Senegal’s ceebu jën. And we are the first to notice when fish grow smaller, the waters turn muddy or catches suddenly fall.


Massive fishing vessels and bottom trawlers from around the world are scooping up fish off our coasts, and illegal fishing alone may cost West Africa

up to $9.4 billion a year

. The

UN Food and Agriculture Organization

projects that if emissions stay high and climate change continues to escalate, most African countries will lose fish this century, with the steepest losses in tropical waters like ours. Inland, pollution, mining runoff and dams threaten our lakes. Along the coasts, mangroves are shrinking, leaving fewer places for fish to breed.


This matters far beyond the shore. Africa has only

9.1 kilograms of fish

 per person a year, less than half the world average, and

supply must grow 67 percent

 by 2050 just to match the population growth.


But where we have a say, we can reverse the damage. In The Gambia, women oyster harvesters of the

TRY Oyster Women’s Association

 won exclusive rights to manage their fishery in 2012, a first for a women’s group in Africa. They restored mangroves and introduced an eight-month seasonal closure, protecting both breeding grounds and the coastline.

Ghana’s Densu Delta oyster pickers

 copied the model and have managed their fishery the same way since 2020. If we have more of a say, we can replicate these successes.


We have the solutions. Estimates of the catch lost after landing in African small-scale fisheries commonly run from

15 to 50 percent

.

On Lake Victoria

, simple raised drying racks have cut those losses by about 15 percent, and solar tent dryers by about 25 percent.


These fixes are cheap, but they still need capital.

Africa’s blue economy

 already generates close to $300 billion a year, and money is flowing into ports, fishing technology and offshore wind. Little of it reaches the women who process and trade fish. That is the blue economy’s missing piece.


Leaders must break down one of the biggest barriers women face when seeking credit: land titles. Banks ask for them, and few women fish processors have them, because land in many of our communities passes through men. Lenders call that risk. We call it a rule written without us. Our savings groups lend and repay every day; lenders could accept group guarantees, stored stock or mobile-money records instead of title deeds.


The

Luanda Declaration

 offers a path, but its 40 percent target for representation is shared among women, youth and local communities. It could be met without a single woman who smokes or sells fish. The roadmap must name women fish processors and traders as a distinct group, ensure that access to the national blue funds promised by 2027 is not dependent on land titles, and count us, by sex, in the new blue economy accounts across the entire value chain. By the Declaration’s mid-term review in 2028, ministers should be able to say how …

author: Simon Ramapuputla
title: IEC declares 2026 local elections free and fair as coalitions get set to run municipalities
content:
The Independent Electoral Commission (IEC) has declared the 2026 local government elections free and fair, with 14.9-million people having cast their ballots in an election that has left most municipal councils facing the prospect of coalition government.


The African National Congress (ANC) retained its position as the largest party nationally, securing 30.76% of the vote and 3,246 council seats. However, the result represents a significant decline in its electoral support and leaves the party needing to negotiate with other political formations in municipalities where it failed to secure an outright majority.


Announcing the results at the IEC results operations centre at Gallagher Estate on Sunday, IEC chairperson Mosotho Moepya said the elections had largely been conducted in a peaceful environment.


A total of 29.2-million voters were registered, with approximately 14.9-million participating. The national turnout was 52%, an increase of 6.1 percentage points from the 45.9% recorded in the 2021 local government elections.


The Democratic Alliance (DA) came second with 24.64% and 1,695 council seats, followed by the uMkhonto weSizwe Party (MKP) with 9.76% and 785 seats. The Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) received 6.22% and 588 seats, while ActionSA secured 5.67% and 313 seats.


Moepya said the commission’s declaration was informed partly by findings from the 2026 Elections Satisfaction Survey conducted by the Human Sciences Research Council. The survey found that 90% of respondents regarded the elections as having integrity, 91% considered them free and fair, and 95% were satisfied with the services provided by the IEC.


Some voting stations experienced problems with voter management devices. Photo by Mzi Velapi


However, the commission acknowledged that the electoral process had not been without challenges.


In Douglas, Northern Cape, ballot papers were destroyed before counting could take place when political party supporters allegedly stormed the voting station at a community hall. The IEC ordered a revote in Ward 3 of the Siyancuma Local Municipality, saying the affected votes could not be counted since ballot papers had been destroyed. The commission approached the Electoral Court and registered a criminal case with the police.


Chief electoral officer, Sy Mamabolo outlined the scale of the election operation, which involved approximately 188,000 staff deployed across 23,696 voting stations.


The IEC printed more than 100-million ballot papers and deployed approximately 56,000 voter management devices to support voter verification and the administration of the elections.


Mamabolo said approximately 28-million ballot papers had to be superseded following a Constitutional Court order affecting candidate lists. The order affected 181 ANC candidates in six municipalities. The commission extended the same dispensation to other parties in similar circumstances to ensure equal treatment.


The IEC also introduced a virtual results operations centre, allowing political parties and candidates remote access to selected applications and reports during the results process.


Mamabolo said the commission would assess both the successes and shortcomings of the election operation. “Operational excellence is not a destination, but it is a continuous institutional commitment,” he said.

author: Abahlali_3
title: We mourn the loss of Des D’sa
content:
30 October 2026 Abahlali baseMjondolo press statement

We mourn the loss of Des D’Sa, father, uncle, grandfather, and a comrade to many

The death of Desmond D’Sa has plunged many people on the left in Durban and beyond, across numerous organisations, into shock and despair. Siyakhala ngo Des.

Comrade Des was a stalwart in the struggle against apartheid and was a well-known organiser who formed the South Durban Community Environmental Alliance (SDCEA), an environmental organisation that raised the concerns of families living in the oil- and gas-affected areas of Wentworth and the Bluff.

His activism and the fight against injustices did not end with environmental issues and it definitely did not end in Wentworth and the Bluff. Comrade Des fought against all forms of oppression and injustice, including gangsterism and the mining companies in rural areas, and supported everyone from fisherfolk to migrants and poor people, whether living in flats, hostels or shacks. He did not back down when struggle became dangerous. Comrade Des spoke fluent isiZulu and engaged everyone with the same respect.

He joined the first march against ANC councillor Yacoob Baig organised from Kennedy Road in 2005, which became part of the process towards the formation of our movement. He stood with our movement from the beginning, and was one of the few who never wavered in his support even when we were under severe attack and isolated.

Comrade Des was one of the founders of the Right to Know Campaign that fought fought against secrecy while promoting the right to information. He was also one of the founders of The Durban Coalition, which was first formed in response to the devastating floods of 2022. The Coalition, which unites community organisations across the city in a united front, is thriving today and is an important formation in the city.

We will miss Comrade Des so much. He was always on the side of the people. He was always so warm and kind. We always laughed when he was around.

We wish to thank his family for him. And wish to express our heartfelt condolences to his family, friends and comrades.

It is so sad and devastating that you have left us. Till we meet again.

Hamba kahle Comrade Des D’Sa. Ubuyiqhawe.

author: WoMin
title: From Mombasa to Yaoundé, the vision and the demand is for reparative justice
content:
Through WoMin’s work alongside African women organising against extractivism, against the drivers of the climate crisis and its impacts, the destruction of the commons through false solutions, unjust energy transitions (and generally a world order that serves a minority over the global majority), we have been asking: what is the full range of impacts and costs in the face of environmental and climate impacts? Who and whose work absorbs these impacts and costs? And what would repair mean from the perspective of women, their communities and the ecosystems they care for and are cared for at the frontline of the climate crisis, where centuries of continued systems of accumulation by dispossession and destruction meet?


Our experience shows us that reparations cannot simply be another form of compensation. They must confront the very systems producing the harm – extractivism, odious and illegitimate debt, colonial legacies, patriarchy, racism, and corporate power promoting more false solutions whose aim is not climate justice but profit. Reparations must indeed offer us all a real chance to build Pan African feminist futures that centre care, including the restoration of the commons, and the conditions that make life possible.


Connecting the “c-words” – colonialism to climate reparations


The recent

African Symposium on Climate Reparations

 in Mombasa, Kenya, started on that same note: “there is no “c-word” that we cannot bring into conversations on climate reparations”, argued a comrade in his opening remarks. And indeed, the current

climate disorder

1

 is a historical process, and Colonialism (the c-word that in other climate justice spaces some shy away from) is part and parcel of it. As is, we argue at WoMin, capitalism. What is more, not only do climate reparations need to address colonialism and neocolonialism, but also the solution to the climate crisis will not be found within capitalism. Or as Audre Lorde put it, “… the master’s tools will never dismantle the master’s house. They may allow us temporarily to beat him at his own game, but they will never enable us to bring about genuine change.”


Not only we need our own tools, but also a broad alliance, as broad, yet united in principles and analysis, as broad and urgent is the task ahead. And the symposium offered an important space to bring together many working for reparations across the continent and in the diaspora, in conversations navigated along four main tracks: rights of nature and ecosystems stewardship; finance, debt and tax justice; law and human rights; and lived realities from frontline communities.


And the timing matters. We are entering the Decade of Justice and Reparations for Africans and People of African Descent, while the debt crisis in Africa continues to exponentially grow and deepen climate vulnerability, false climate solutions continue to expand, further threatening the commons millions of Africans depend upon for their everyday subsistence, and the African Court considers an Advisory Opinion on States’ obligations in the climate crisis.


As powerful expressed in an

open letter

 which emerged from the symposium, a Pan African position and action plan for climate reparations is urgent, but it cannot be constructed only through states, legal and financial tools. Those at the frontlines absorbing the costs of extractivism, ecological destruction and climate disruption have to shape what counts as harm, what constitutes repair, and what must stop. And importantly, we need to organise at all levels the collective power to make repair possible.


African women united for climate justice and reparations


This was the task of the 4th

Women’s Climate Assembly

 (WCA) in Yaoundé, Cameroon, held in early October under the theme, “Our lands, our voices: African women united for climate justice and reparations!”. The Assembly convened over 75 women community leaders, activists, feminist organisations, civil society groups and allies from twelve countries including Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Côte d’Ivoire, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Guinea-Conakry, Liberia, Namibia, Niger, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, Senegal, and Zambia.


Oh ancestors, watch over Africa and let everything return to Africa! If we are coveted today, if there are wars, it is because our ancestors bequeathed this land to us. They did not abuse its riches. They used them sustainably. So we ask our ancestors to guide us during this Assembly, so that peace and food …

author: Mada Masr
title: Lina Attalah in custody after court issues LE3 mn fine, orders Mada Masr’s closure
content:
Mada Masr Editor-in-Chief Lina Attalah was fined LE3 million by the New Cairo Misdemeanor Court, which convicted her on charges of managing an unlicensed website, issuing an order for the website’s closure. Attalah was taken into custody after the issue of the ruling.


Tuesday’s session at the ninth circuit of the New Cairo Misdemeanor Court, presided over by judge Mohamed Mubarak, was temporarily suspended for deliberations after Attalah’s defense counsel requested time to review the case file.


After the court returned from deliberations, the judge ordered the courtroom cleared of everyone except Attalah and her defense counsel, the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights’ executive director Hossam Bahgat, who was also present, told Mada Masr. The room then filled with plainclothes officers and guards, with a National Security Agency officer in attendance, he added.


The presiding judge and a Supreme State Security Prosecution representative returned to the session and the judge announced that the court has decided to stand by its rejection of all the procedural arguments presented by the defense, including requests to bring in any documentation or hear any witnesses.


The judge then asked the defense team to present its plea. The counsel insisted that it would not submit a plea as long as its requests were unanswered by the court.


The judge then abruptly asked for a lawyer unknown to any member of the defense counsel to be brought in, “in a move that astonished all those present,” said Bahgat, and announced that the court decided to appoint a lawyer for Attalah.


At that point, all members of the defense counsel cried out to reject the court’s appointment of a lawyer when the eight chosen lawyers were present. Attalah herself spoke to say she did not accept the court-appointed lawyer acting on her behalf, an objection the judge refused to have recorded in the session’s minutes.


“In an even more shocking move,” said Bahgat, the judge himself began to log down the requests of the court-appointed lawyer, without the lawyer having said a word. The judge then read out the conviction amid shouts and protests from the defense counsel.


The judge sentenced Attalah to the maximum possible penalty: a LE3 million fine, the closure of Mada Masr’s website and the confiscation of its property.


Security personnel then surrounded Attalah, lifted her off the ground and took her out of the courtroom, where she remains in custody in the courthouse.

Lina Attalah in custody after court issues LE3 mn fine, orders Mada Masr’s closure

 first appeared on

Mada Masr
