author: David Swanson
title: World BEYOND War Education Director Visits Romania, Bulgaria, and Belgium to Discuss Peace, Security, and Youth Participation
content:
By Phill Gittins, World BEYOND War, November 2026


From October 26 to November 4, 2026, World BEYOND War’s Education Director, Dr. Phill Gittins, visited Romania, Bulgaria, and Belgium to meet with peace activists, speak with students and educators, and join discussions on peace, security, and youth participation.


Romania: Chapter Members and University Students


On October 28 in Bucharest, Phill met with Hans Hedrich and George Epurescu of the

World BEYOND War Romania Chapter

. They discussed local peace and anti-war organizing and ways to stay connected.


Later that day, Phill gave a presentation and joined a discussion with an international group of master’s students at the

University of Bucharest’s Faculty of Political Science

, hosted by Associate Professor Luciana Alexandra Ghica. Drawing on WBW’s forthcoming book,

From the War System to a Global Peace System

, he explored different approaches to security, alternatives to war and militarism, and the role of civil society in building peace.


Phill Gittins with Hans Hedrich and George Epurescu of the World BEYOND War Romania Chapter in Bucharest


Phill Gittins speaking with students at the University of Bucharest.


Bulgaria: Peace Education and Practical Action


On October 30, Phill spoke at

Sofia University

 with Bulgarian and international students, doctoral researchers, and faculty members. The presentation drew further on the forthcoming book and led to a lively discussion about non-military defense, including how countries facing armed aggression might protect themselves without relying solely on military force.


Afterwards, Phill spoke with Professor Tatyana Dronzina and Dr. Denitsa Hinkova who expressed interest in possible collaboration, including a summer school for young leaders from Central and Eastern Europe. The idea is to combine peace education, dialogue, and practical training with support for participants to develop projects afterwards.


That afternoon, Phill met with Denitza Vidolova of the

Sofia Platform Foundation

 to learn about its work in civic and history education, including helping teachers address Bulgaria’s communist past and polarizing issues.


While in Sofia, Phill also caught up with

Veronika Botsova

, who served as President of Rotaract Europe during the 2023–2024 term and previously collaborated with World BEYOND War on its

Peace Education and Action for Impact (PEAI)

 programme.


Students and colleagues at Sofia University.


Phill Gittins with Denitza Vidolova of the Sofia Platform Foundation.


Phill Gittins with Veronika Botsova in Sofia.


Belgium: Youth Participation and Dialogue


The final stop was Brussels, where Phill contributed to the

Voices of Change Final Conference at the European Parliament

 on November 3. The Erasmus+-supported event, delivered by

World Scouting

 and the

Erasmus Student Network

 (ESN), brought together young people, youth organizations, civil society representatives, and policymakers to discuss democracy, participation, and peacebuilding.


In a fishbowl discussion titled

“Neutral or silent?”

, Phill considered when neutrality protects dialogue and when it becomes silence in the face of injustice. As he put it: “We are clearly not neutral about war and militarism. We have a position. But having a position does not mean closing down dialogue.”


Conversations with participants from Georgia and Ukraine raised further questions about whether non-military defense could protect societies facing armed threats. The exchanges were challenging but friendly, showing how experiences of war and insecurity shape different views of what keeps people safe.


Phill also spoke with ESN and WOSM representatives about possible contributions to future regional and international student gatherings, including peace education workshops.


Meeting Erasmus Student Network representatives.


Voices of Change Final Conference at the European Parliament.


Participants at the Voices of Change conference.


The visit was also a chance to reconnect with

Donna-Marie Fry

, a WBW Advisory Board member and longtime contributor to its education courses, and Belén Luna Sanz, who took part in a peace education program Phill led in Bolivia in 2014 and now works in digital policy.


Many thanks to everyone who hosted the visits, joined the discussions, and shared their ideas.


Phill Gittins with Donna Marie Fry in Brussels.


Phill Gittins with Belén Luna Sanz in Brussels.

title: A fightback is building as crackdown deepens against civil liberties (Workers’ Voice)
content:
Dozens of activists are accused by the federal government of contributing to bogus “criminal conspiracies.” In Minnesota, two separate conspiracy cases accuse 54 people of participating in illegal conspiracies for participating in protest and journalistic activities. The Minnesota 15, Righteous 39, Michigan 8 (now 12), Spokane 3, and Prairieland Defendants are the most well known cases in the ongoing crackdown. All of these cases are attacks on organized labor.

The California Faculty Association and the Graduate Employee Organization at University of Michigan (GEO-AFT 3550) are facing frontal attacks on their unions by the right-wing press and FBI. Doctored video of a CFA meeting was leaked to Trump booster Bari Weiss’s Free Press in an attempt to scandalize the union with false accusations of antisemitism. The Department of Justice first charged GEO President Hiab Teshome with felonious financial crimes. Those bogus charges were dropped the same day that a grand jury subpoenaed GEO’s books, including all member lists, meeting minutes, and financial records. The union is fighting to retain basic privacy rights.

Fueled by National Security Presidential Memorandum-7, U.S. intelligence and police apparatuses are being explicitly targeted at anyone standing for basic democratic rights, immigrant communities, and racial justice. As the world drifts closer to major inter-imperialist conflict and expanding zones of overt imperialist military occupation takes hold in the semi-colonies, Western imperialisms are tightening restrictions on protest, speech, and organizing for progressive movements.

While there are many additional cases of “lawfare” and anti-protest policing, it is worth taking a moment to review two of the cases mentioned above to understand the tactics and scope of the current crackdown.

Around two dozen protesters held a noise demonstration on July 4, 2025, outside of the Prairieland Detention Center in Texas. As the protest was winding down and many of the participants had left, Alvarado Police Officer Thomas Gross sped onto the scene and almost immediately aimed his gun at a demonstrator moving away from him. Video evidence indicates that Gross discharged his weapon, something that would appear to have been covered up by the judge and prosecutors.

In response to seeing a potentially lethal attack on a protester, Marine Corps veteran Benjamin “Champagne” Song let out a warning shot into the ground away from the officers. Gross went to the hospital for superficial wounds that the government alleges resulted from being shot by Song, but video evidence released after sentencing indicates Gross was likely hit by shrapnel produced from his own weapon’s discharge.

Using the presence of guns and defensive action of Song as pretext, 22 people were ultimately indicted as part of an alleged conspiracy to attack cops and carry out an armed prison break. One person, Daniel “Des” Rolando Sanchez Estrada, was not at the protest at all. Des was convicted for “corruptly concealing a document or record” and sentenced to 30 years for possessing legally protected political materials.

After arrests, pressure and legal sabotage was mounted by the judicial system against the defendants. Many were initially held in solitary confinement, with one reporting that human feces coated their cell. U.S. District Judge Mark Pittman blocked the defendants from retaining a private attorney, meaning they had to use public defenders. Song’s legal team was not allowed to make an argument that the warning shot was taken in self-defense. Eight defendants became cooperating witnesses, providing coerced testimony to validate the government’s made-up conspiracy theories.

Before the trial even began, the deck was stacked against non-cooperating defendants. In an explicit “warning” to the left, Judge Pittman laid down ridiculously high sentences of between 30-100 years to non-cooperating defendants.

The Minnesota 15 are 15 activists accused of a “conspiracy to impede or attack federal agents.” The majority are current or recent union members and all are community activists. They are not accused of participating in or coordinating any acts of violence. Instead, the original 92-page indictment against them lists “evidence” including participating in rapid response group chats, protests, and mutual aid activities. title: Investigate police, doctors involved in Duterte’s ‘drug war’
content:
Forensic pathologist Dr. Raquel Fortun, also a member of the commission, presents one of the questionable certificates during the commission's truth-telling session last Friday. (Truth Commission photo)

The Truth Commission has called on the Philippine government to investigate the police officers’ misconduct and promotion and the doctors’ questionable death certificates in the course of the “drug war” campaign of former President Rodrigo Duterte.

“My son was alive when they arrested him, but they killed him. They could’ve let him live. They did not show mercy, they planted drugs and guns,” Marissa Lazaro, mother of extrajudicial killing victim Cristopher Lazaro, said in Tagalog during the commission’s truth-telling session.

The Truth Commission pointed to a failed system for investigating deaths, marked by careless police and forensic work, and little concern for victims’ families. Lazaro’s account also showed that the police officers were asking money from her, indicating a potential trail of corruption.

Cristopher, 20, and Alberto Paragas, 32, died in police operations on August 5, 2017 in Marilao, Bulacan. Police reported that the two resisted (nanlaban) after an alleged attempted holdup. Cristopher’s friends also died hours earlier in Bocaue, a separate town in Bulacan.

Lazaro added, “They asked me to sign a waiver, indicating that I consented to their illegal operation. I did not sign it. They told me: the day will come that I will seek their help. I told them, what help could you give my son? You killed him. He’s already dead.”

A similar incident happened to Marissa Quiamco, sister of Alberto, after she paid the P10,000 fee to release the cadaver of her brother. A police officer asked her and Alberto’s partner to sign a document, indicating consent for the operation but they refused to sign.

“I wish I could fight for my brother. Even my neighbors asked me to file a complaint. But I told them: we don’t have money. We don’t have the capacity or resources to get a lawyer,” Quiamco said during the truth-telling session. “I’m only earning enough to help my mother and father.”

In October, an analysis of public records by the Truth Commission recorded a pattern that commanding police officers were promoted and reassigned, instead of being subjected to criminal and administrative sanctions.

Lito Patay, who commanded Batasan police station that killed 108 people in drug operations during his term, was named chief of the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG) in Central Luzon.

In Caloocan, the commission’s own records documented 284 killings in 2016, before the leadership of Chito Bersaluno in the City Police. During his watch, 105 more deaths were recorded from February to August 2017. He was removed from his post after the killing of Kian delos Santos. However, he was made police director of Bulacan Province in 2018 and promoted to the rank of brigadier general in 2022.

In 2020, human rights organizations flagged the reassignment of Debold Sinas, former chief of the Central Visayas Police Regional Office, to the National Capital Region. The Commission on Human Rights (CHR) Regional Office said back then that Sinas’ watch in Central Visayas was marred by unresolved killings linked to the illegal drugs trade and the anti-insurgency campaign “Oplan Sauron.” Duterte appointed him as the Philippine National Police Chief on November 9, 2020, serving a six-month term. A year after, he was appointed as an undersecretary of the Office of the President.

Read: [LIST] Gross human rights violations under Debold Sinas

“Any inquiry must look at promotions as closely as it looks at cash payments,” said Christopher Magno, the commission’s executive director and an expert on state violence in the Philippines. “No police officer should gain in any way from the blood of people killed outside the law.”

Former Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office (PCSO) General Manager Royina Garma, who also served as Cebu City police chief under the Duterte administration, revealed the incentivization of police officers through the “Davao Model” in a quad committee hearing of the House of Representatives in 2024.

“First is the reward if the suspect is killed. Second is the funding of planned operations. Third is the refund of operational expenses,” Garma said, stressing that the rewards started from P20,000 ($343.95) to P1 million ($17,197.50), depending on the profile of the suspects. content:
ABD Başkanı Donald Trump, Senato ve Temsilciler Meclisinde çoğunluğu Demokratlara kaybettiği 5 Kasım ara seçimlerinin ardından İran savaşı konusunda ağız değiştirdi. Seçim öncesi nükleer bomba tehditlerine kadar varan saldırı tehditlerinin yerini "Çatışma yakında sona erecek" söylemleri aldı.

Beyaz Saray'da brifing odasında katıldığı basın toplantısında İran savaşına dair soruları yanıtlayan Trump, "Şu anda askeri operasyon düzenlemek pek gerekli gibi görünmüyor ancak her türlü ihtimale karşı hazırız" dedi.

Trump: İran'la çatışmaların sona ermesine yönelik olumlu bir ivme var

İran'la savaşın bitiş sürecinde olduğunu söyleyen Trump, "Bu çatışmanın sona ermesine doğru bir ivme görüyoruz. Bence oldukça yakında sona erecek" ifadelerini kullandı.

İsrail ve Orta Doğu'nun "İran tehdidine" karşı korunduğunu öne sürüp İran'ın nükleer silaha sahip olamayacağını söyleyen Trump, İran'la görüşmelerin iyi gittiğini de iddia etti. Trump, sürecin yakında sona ermesini umduğunu belirtti.

Öte yandan Trump, bir soru üzerine, "İran'ın aksi yönde bir adım atması halinde" yeniden saldırılara hazır oldukları tehdidini yöneltti: "Hiçbir şey garanti edemem ancak geri dönmemiz gerekirse her şeye hazırız. Eğer mecbur kalırsak, bu konuyu çok ciddiye alacağız. Tamamen hazır durumdayız. Yeni bir uçak gemimiz daha var. Hepsi yeni ve muhteşem ekipmanlarla ağzına kadar dolu. Umarım bunları kullanmak zorunda kalmayız."

author: Chiara Joos
title: Das Recht auf sexuelle Selbstbestimmung
content:
Zwangssterilisation ist verboten. Dennoch erfahren Frauen mit Behinderungen häufig Druck von Angehörigen, Ärzt*innen oder Betreuer*innen, sich sterilisieren zu lassen.

Weißt du, wie viele Menschen ich begleitet habe, die darunter gelitten haben, dass sie sterilisiert wurden?“, fragte mich eine Beraterin am Telefon. Sie schult Menschen mit Behinderungen in Selbstbestimmung. Es war eines von hundert Gesprächen, die meine Kollegin Ramona Arzberger und ich geführt haben, um zur Verhütungspraxis bei Menschen mit Behinderungen zu recherchieren. Nach fast einem Jahr ist daraus der Film „Hauptsache, du kriegst kein Kind“ unseres Magazins „andererseits“ entstanden. Er begleitet mehrere Frauen in Deutschland und Österreich, die mit Lernschwierigkeiten leben und auf Unterstützung angewiesen sind. Drei von ihnen sind sterilisiert. Keine entschied allein. Elf Prozent der Frauen in deutschen Einrichtungen geben an, sterilisiert zu sein, so der Forschungsbericht zu Gewalt und Gewaltschutz in Einrichtungen der Behindertenhilfe des deutschen Bundesministeriums für Arbeit und Soziales von 2024. title: Ukraine’s internal aggressor seeks a counteroffensive in the social war: some clarifications for anarchism abroad after the riot near Kiev
content:
There is no fascism in Ukraine. Only a Gestapo, death squads, and a nationwide concentration camp

The activity of our DIY community media depends solely on its audience. Please support our work on this fundraising page for further telling the truth of the streets and the trenches that is forbidden or invisible to the pro-capitalist press. Many thanks everyone!

Following the anti-busification protests that took place over the summer in Kiev and cities in Western Ukraine, the flame of unrest has flared up with renewed intensity. Ukrainian masses have tried to strike back at those who, since 2014, had come to view themselves as an untouchable, sacred caste—a "master race" (on a financial leash of the country’s biggest capitalist, Rinat Akhmetov). Those in Ukraine who had arrogated to themselves the right to speak on behalf of its civil society are now gripped by fear and rage toward those who dared to challenge their monopoly.

A new spark of rebellion flared up on November 2 at 7-A Sunny Street in the village of Petropavlovskaya Borshchagovka (Petropavlivska Borshchahivka). A mobilized man named Andriy Kuleshov had escaped from the 52nd International Assault Regiment "Forge" (military unit 3121)—part of the 1st Corpse of the National Guard "Azov"—and, after his recapture, was held in a private house of this village that had been put up for sale by Sense Bank. According to the unit commander, the unrest began following an attempt to free Kuleshov for $7,000. A 49-year-old plastic surgeon, Valentyna Moloda, arrived at the property in a private ambulance, alleging that men were being held illegally and tortured inside the building. Then, on trial, she stated that she had not intended to incite any provocation; instead, she had come to help persons allegedly being held against their will, acting on a request from a woman who had told her about a man being tortured in an undisclosed location. Moloda denies demanding money for the release of the recruits, maintaining that the sum in question was intended to cover the costs of a private medical evacuation.

One way or other, the statements from TikTok appear to have triggered an unexpected public reaction. A crowd of over a hundred angry people gathered at an NGU deployment site, demanding the release of the men kept hostage there. Some of the protesters claimed to be relatives of those in detention. Military personnel and police subsequently arrived at the scene, and clashes broke out. The crowd rocked a National Guard bus, attempted to break down the gates of the clandestine detention facility, threw eggs and stones at the building’s windows and at the punishers, chanted "Shame!" and "Faggots!" Their vehicles were smashed; someone even used a sledgehammer for this. Tear gas was used against the people. Later, unknown black-clothed ones, wearing balaclavas and carrying wooden bats, appeared on the scene and used force against the protesters. A reporter of the pro-government media outlet UNIAN was also kicked in the stomach by an unidentified person. One of the victims claimed that he and his son were beaten while simply passing by. The NGU stated about 16 militaries injured during deterrence of the crowd.

Then, announces appeared on social media calling on far-right militants to unite for "restoring order" and "responding to outrages" on an ongoing basis. And compelling video evidence of how this went down that evening: "We form a column, four fighters abreast. The question was raised: what if people are waiting for us up ahead—armed, carrying knives? After all, they were the ones who slashed the tires. Did anyone want to step aside? Everyone said, 'We’re going.' We form up and begin to march forward. And we recite the Prayer of the Ukrainian Nationalist: 'Death to the enemies... You shall win freedom or perish in the struggle. Rest assured—you shall not perish; you shall win freedom. I go into battle.' title: Update: Polizeihund bei Demo misshandelt – Staatsanwaltschaft stellt Ermittlungen ein

Symbolbild


Bei einer Demonstration gegen den AfD-Parteitag am 11. Januar 2025 in Riesa kam es zu

Wir von PETA Deutschland kritisieren dies scharf, erstatten Strafanzeige gegen die Verantwortlichen und fordern, dass der Einsatz von Polizeihunden endlich beendet wird. Erfahren Sie hier, was bei der Demonstration vorgefallen ist und warum Gewalt gegen „Polizeihunde“ kein Einzelfall ist.


Update vom 7. November 2026


Staatsanwaltschaft Dresden stellt Verfahren ein


Nachdem im Januar 2026 ein Video für einen medialen Aufschrei sorgte, das zeigt, wie ein sogenannter

Polizeihund

 bei einer Demonstration gewaltsam gegen einen Demonstranten eingesetzt wurde, erstatteten wir von PETA Deutschland Strafanzeige gegen die Verantwortlichen.


Im August 2026 wurde bekannt, dass die Staatsanwaltschaft Dresden in dem Fall nicht weiter ermittelt – angesichts des traurigen Videos mit absurden Begründungen. Die Staatsanwaltschaft erklärt diese Entscheidung in dem Einstellungsbescheid damit, dass ein „Verstoß gegen das Tierschutzgesetz […] nur vorliegen [würde], wenn man einem Tier ohne vernünftigen Grund aus Rohheit erhebliche Schmerzen zufügen würde.“ Der im Video dokumentierte Umgang des Beamten mit dem Hund sei keine „Rohheit“ im Sinne des Tierschutzgesetzes, da die ergriffene „Maßnahme […] zum Aufrechterhalten der öffentlichen Sicherheit und Ordnung erforderlich war […]“ und der Hund „nur kurz eingesetzt“ worden sei.


Die Staatsanwaltschaft begründet die Entscheidung darüber hinaus damit, dass „Diensthunde […] legal bei der Polizei als Hilfsmittel auch in Stresssituationen eingesetzt […]“ werden. Die Tiere würden dabei automatisch Belastungssituationen ausgesetzt. Die Interessen und das Wohl der Hunde rückten jedoch im Verhältnis zu den polizeilichen Interessen der Gefahrenabwehr in den Hintergrund, da die „Diensthunde“ zu diesem Zwecke ausgebildet würden. Der den Hunden zugeschriebene „Nutzen“ rechtfertigt laut Ansicht der Staatsanwaltschaft Dresden, dass die Tiere bewusst in Gefahrensituationen gezwungen werden.


PETA kritisiert Entscheidung der Staatsanwaltschaft: Gesetz erlaubt Gewalt gegen Diensthunde


Die Einstellung unserer Anzeige ist ein weiteres Beispiel dafür, dass das Gesetz die „Diensthunde“ nicht vor einem gewaltsamen Umgang und Missbrauch schützt. Hunde sind keine Einsatzmittel, sondern fühlende Lebewesen, die einen respektvollen, liebevollen Umgang verdient haben – nicht die missbräuchliche Verwendung  als Waffe oder Schutzschild.


Wir vertreten die Ansicht, dass moderne Polizeiarbeit ohne Tiere auskommt und fordern daher Politik und Behörden auf, „Diensthunde“ zu verbieten.

Gewalt gegen Polizeihunde bei einem Einsatz gegen Demonstranten in Riesa


Videos von der Demonstration zeigen deutlich wie gewaltvoll einige Diensthundeführer:innen mit den „Polizeihunden“ umgehen. Einer der

Hunde

 wurde von einem der Beamten am Hals gepackt und gegen eine Leitplanke und einen Demonstranten gedrückt. Dadurch sollte der Hund offensichtlich dazu gebracht werden, den Demonstranten zu beißen. Der Hund zeigte hierbei unübersehbare

Anzeichen

 von massivem Stress, Überforderung und Meideverhalten. Ein weiterer völlig überdrehter Hund verbiss sich in den Arm eines anderen Polizisten.


https://www.instagram.com/p/DExO_Z1Mcvv/?hl=de


PETA erstattet Strafanzeige und fordert den Einsatz von Polizeihunden zu beenden


Dieser gewaltsame Umgang der Einsatzkräfte mit den Hunden ist tierschutzwidrig. Hunde sind nicht dazu da, für die Arbeit der Polizei ausgenutzt zu werden. Wir fordern deshalb, den Einsatz von Hunden bei der Polizei endlich einzustellen. Zudem erstatten wir bei der Staatsanwaltschaft Dresden Zweigstelle Meißen Strafanzeige gegen den verantwortlichen Polizisten. „Die aktuellen Aufnahmen aus Riesa zeigen eindeutig, dass Hunde bei Polizeieinsätzen nichts zu suchen haben. Wir hoffen, dass es den betroffenen Hunden gut geht und sie keine körperlichen Schäden von dieser grausamen Behandlung davontragen. Die Psyche der Hunde leidet nach solch einem Einsatz ganz sicher. title: SAVE THE SOUTH SUFFOLK ONE!
content:
Oh, wait… sorry. The Judge already did that in court.


John ‘Pinocchio’ Henty’s case ends in acquittal

.


Thank you to


South Suffolk Hunt Sabs


for this guest article.


A court case brought by former Essex & Suffolk Hunt huntsman John Henty against a hunt saboteur has ended in a resounding victory for the defence, with the saboteur found NOT GUILTY.


John Henty outside court.


Following allegations made to police, former Essex & Suffolk Hunt huntsman John Henty pursued a prosecution alleging abusive and threatening behaviour under Section 5 of the Public Order Act. The case followed an incident on a quiet country lane in which Henty pursued the hunt saboteurs’ vehicle, blocked it in, approached it and attempted to provoke a reaction.


What followed was a lengthy legal process based on Henty’s account of events. However, when his evidence was examined in court, serious questions arose about the credibility of that account and whether the alleged behaviour actually amounted to a criminal offence.


A case that should never have reached court?


The Judge was highly critical of the way the case had been handled by the CPS and the police officers involved, making clear that the alleged actions did not meet the legal threshold required for a criminal offence.


Both the prosecution and the defence barrister sought to discontinue the case on more than one occasion. The case was nevertheless directed to proceed. The circumstances surrounding that decision raise serious questions about why so much time and public money were spent pursuing a prosecution that ultimately failed.


Former Essex & Suffolk Hunt huntsman John Henty is now at The Ludlow Hunt.


The evidence tells a different story


Henty submitted two video clips, recorded by himself, which were played in court. The footage showed Henty pulling his vehicle alongside the hunt saboteurs’ Land Rover, getting out of his own accord and filming the encounter.


Our saboteur told Henty to ‘f*ck off’ before closing the vehicle door. Rather than disengaging, Henty continued filming and engaging with the occupants. Despite claiming under oath that he had been alarmed and distressed, the circumstances captured on his own footage told a different story.


The prosecution was unable to produce further evidence demonstrating that Henty had experienced the alarm or distress alleged.


Henty spun a yarn of lies that should never have made it to court.


The judge’s conclusion


Having heard Henty’s evidence under cross-examination and considered the footage and relevant law, the Judge concluded that:


Henty had parked his vehicle alongside the saboteurs’ vehicle of his own accord.


He had got out of his vehicle voluntarily.


He had chosen to film the encounter.


He had continued the interaction of his own accord.


He had not contacted the police immediately, instead reporting the incident to 101 approximately two hours later.


These circumstances were central to the Judge’s assessment of Henty’s claim that he had experienced fear, alarm and distress. Following Henty’s evidence and cross-examination by the prosecution and defence, the case concluded without our hunt saboteur needing to take the stand.


The verdict

:

Not guilty. Acquitted.


After all the allegations, the police involvement, the CPS proceedings and the considerable expenditure of public resources, the case ended in an acquittal. A considerable amount of time, money and public resources had been spent pursuing this matter, only for the court to reach a conclusion that raises serious questions about why the prosecution was pursued in the first place.


Hunt saboteurs will not be intimidated out of exposing illegal hunting. And they will not be silenced by allegations that cannot withstand scrutiny in court.


The South Suffolk One stands vindicated.


SAVE THE SOUTH SUFFOLK ONE!


South Suffolk Hunt Sabs remain steadfast and will not be intimidated or silenced.

Hunt Saboteurs Association

author: Sophie Lemcke
title: So ist es, als weibliches Rind in der Milchindustrie zu leben
content:
Die Milchindustrie ist ein grausamer Kreislauf des Leids und endet mit einem gewaltvollen Tod.


Wie fühlt es sich an, in dieses System hineingeboren zu werden, ohne die Möglichkeit, dem zu entkommen?


Der einzige Grund, weshalb die Industrie dich „produziert“ hat: Auch du sollst Kinder gebären, immer wieder, damit du Milch produzierst. Milch, die dann von Menschen, statt von deinem Kalb konsumiert werden kann.


Du wirst fixiert, während jemand das Besamungsgerät in deine Vagina sowie seinen Arm in deinen Anus einführt. Wenn die Zwangsbefruchtung nicht beim ersten Mal zur Trächtigkeit führt – was oft der Fall ist –, wird dieser Vorgang mehrfach wiederholt.


Neun Monate – wie bei uns Menschen – wächst dein Kalb in dir heran. Du spürst eine Verbindung, merkst, wie es sich bewegt und immer größer wird. Je schwerer du selbst wirst, umso stärker werden deine Gelenkprobleme. Die rutschigen und harten Spaltenböden, auf denen du fast dein ganzes Leben verbringst, führen oft zu Verletzungen.


Dann bringst du dein Kalb zur Welt. Um dich herum riecht es extrem nach Kot und Ammoniak, von den Ausscheidungen der Tiere.


Endlich ist es da, noch ganz nass und schwach. Du leckst ihm über das Fell, um es zu wärmen. Es sucht deine Nähe und will an deinem Euter die für ihn so wichtige Erstmilch trinken. Sie stärkt sein noch schwaches Immunsystem und gibt ihm Kraft. Doch dann kommen die Arbeiter*innen.


Sie zerren dein noch ganz wackelig stehendes Kalb weg von dir. Es ruft nach dir. Du versuchst, bei ihm zu bleiben, aber du hast keine Chance. Die Menschen haben es weggebracht – du wirst es wahrscheinlich nie wiedersehen und nach nur zwei Monaten direkt wieder gewaltvoll befruchtet.


Du wirst nach der Geburt monatelang mehrmals täglich in den Melkstand getrieben – und die meiste Zeit davon bist du bereits wieder schwanger. Dein Körper muss gleichzeitig ein neues Kalb versorgen, das in dir heranwächst, und täglich über 22 Liter Milch produzieren. Dein Euter und deine Zitzen schmerzen. Aufgrund der extremen Überzüchtung produzierst du viermal so viel Milch, wie du es natürlicherweise für dein Kind tun würdest.


Die Prozeduren und Haltungsbedingungen zehren stark an deinem Körper. Dein Euter ist entzündet und schmerzt bei jeder Berührung. Andere Tiere humpeln, weil ihnen jeder Schritt wehtut. Viele sind schwach und ausgelaugt.


Wenn du nicht schon vorher stirbst oder getötet wirst, weil dein Körper nicht mehr kann, dann wirst du voraussichtlich nach nur fünf Jahren getötet – obwohl du unter natürlichen Bedingungen 25 Jahre alt werden könntest.


Dann kommt der Tag, an dem du als nicht mehr profitabel giltst. Du wirst aus dem Stall getrieben – das erste Mal nach Jahren verlässt du ihn, aber das ist kein Grund zur Freude.


Zusammen mit anderen erschöpften „ausgedienten Milchkühen“ wirst du auf einen Transporter verladen. Du hast Mühe, über die Rampe zu gehen. Deine Gelenke schmerzen vom jahrelangen Stehen auf Spaltenböden. Im engen Transporter stehst du dicht an dicht mit den anderen Tieren, der Lkw wackelt. Manche fallen hin und werden versehentlich getreten. Eure Fahrt in den Schlachthof dauert mehrere Stunden, ohne Wasser, ohne Nahrung, ohne Pause.


Angekommen erwartet dich ein brutaler Tod. Überall riecht es nach Blut, du bekommst Panik, aber es gibt keinen Ausweg. Dann ein Bolzenschuss in deinen Kopf. Wenn die Betäubung korrekt durchgeführt wurde und wirkt, brichst du zusammen. Wenn nicht, kann es sein, dass du bei Bewusstsein und unter extremen Schmerzen erlebst, wie dir deine Kehle aufgeschnitten wird und du verblutest.


Es ist unvorstellbar, was Mutterrinder in der Milchindustrie erleiden müssen.


Der wahre Preis von Milch


Ein Ermittler von Animal Equality hat mehrere Monate undercover in einem deutschen Milchgewinnungsbetrieb gearbeitet und den Alltag der Tiere dokumentiert. Was unsere Undercover-Recherche zeigt, ist der wahre Preis von Milch: Ausbeutung, Gewalt, Schmerz, Leid und Tod.


Auf unserer Webseite erfährst du mehr und kannst die Stellungnahme des Betriebs nachlesen:


Zur Undercover-Recherche


Unterstütze dieses grausame System nicht!


Entscheide dich konsequent für pflanzliche Lebensmittel. Im Supermarkt findest du zahlreiche Alternativen zu Milch, wie:


Hafermilch – mild, cremig, perfekt für Kaffee und Müsli (oft die günstigste Option!)


Sojamilch – proteinreich, ideal zum Kochen und Backen


Mandelmilch – leicht nussig, besonders lecker in Smoothies


Reismilch – süßlich und gut verträglich …

author: PETA-Team
title: Neue Aufdeckung: Kamele in Marokko für Tourismus missbraucht
content:
Recherchen von PETA Asien dokumentieren immer wieder wie

Kamele

 in der marokkanischen

Tourismusindustrie

 ausgebeutet werden. Die Tiere, die für Ausritte ausgenutzt werden, werden geschlagen und ohne Schutz vor der Witterung angebunden. Sobald sie keinen Profit mehr einbringen, werden sie im Schlachthaus getötet. Erfahren Sie hier, wie es den Kamelen in Marokko geht und was Sie dagegen tun können. 


PETA Asien deckt erneut auf: Missbrauch von Kamelen in Marokko  


PETA Asien hat 2026 erneut die Misshandlung von Kamelen am Rande der Sahara in Marokko aufgedeckt, wo die Betreiber:innen sie zwingen, Tourist:innen durch die trockenen Wüstendünen zu tragen:  


Die Tiere sind außerhalb ihrer Einsätze häufig angekettet und schutzlos extremer Hitze, intensiver Sonneneinstrahlung und Sandstürmen ausgesetzt. 


Viele Kamele verbringen einen Großteil ihres Lebens isoliert und haben kaum die Möglichkeit, sich frei zu bewegen oder Sozialkontakte zu pflegen.  


Die Kamele werden meist nur dann von ihren Ketten befreit, wenn sie kurz Wasser trinken dürfen oder um weitere Tourist:innen durch die Wüste zu tragen. Ein Kamel wurde dabei beobachtet, wie es nicht nur zum Trinken, sondern auch zu einem Pfosten rannte, um sich dort zu kratzen. Es wurde jedoch zurück zu seinem Anbindeplatz gejagt.  


Tierhalter:innen schlugen Kamele wiederholt mit Peitschen, traten sie und zerrten gewaltsam an ihren Schwänzen. 


Kamele sind intelligente, soziale Wesen mit eigenen Bedürfnissen, Wünschen und Interessen. Wenn sie frei in ihrem natürlichen Lebensraum umherstreifen, leben sie in Herden und kommunizieren miteinander durch Laute und Körperbewegungen. Als Zeichen der Freundschaft blasen sich Kamele manchmal gegenseitig ins Gesicht. In der Tourismusindustrie müssen diese Tiere ein Leben lang Elend und Leid ertragen.


 PETA Asien Recherche aus dem Jahr 2025


Bereits 2025

veröffentlichte

PETA Asien

 Videomaterial, dass die Ausbeutung und Misshandlung von Kamelen in Marokko dokumentiert.

Das beunruhigende Video zeigt Kamele, die an nur wenigen Meter langen Seilen angebunden sind. Ein Betreiber wurde dabei gefilmt, wie er ein gefesseltes Kamel wiederholt mit einem langen Stock schlug, während das Tier versuchte, den Schlägen auszuweichen. Ein weiterer Betreiber erklärte den

Ermittler:innen

, dass Kamele, die bis zu 40 Jahre alt werden können, in der Regel etwa fünf Jahre lang ausgebeutet werden, bevor sie getötet oder als

Fleisch

 verkauft werden.


Globales Muster der Grausamkeit


Frühere PETA-Untersuchungen von Kamel- und Pferdebetrieben in Ägypten offenbarten ähnliche Misshandlungen: Tiere wurden blutig geschlagen, gezwungen, Menschen in brütender Hitze ohne Zugang zu Schatten oder Wasser zu tragen, und wie Müll entsorgt oder ins

Schlachthaus

 geschickt, wenn sie zu alt, krank oder verletzt waren, um noch „nützlich“ zu sein. Airbnb, booking.com, Klook, Marriott und viele andere Unternehmen erklärten sich bereit, die Werbung für Tierfahrten bei den Pyramiden von Gizeh einzustellen, nachdem sie von PETA über das Leid der Tiere informiert worden waren.


So können Sie Tieren in der Tourismusindustrie helfen


Tourist:innen, die für Kamelritte bezahlen, halten diese herzlose, unmenschliche Industrie am Laufen. Wenn Sie einen Urlaub planen, vermeiden Sie Angebote mit Tieren und entscheiden Sie sich für tierfreundliche Alternativen. Unterstützen Sie unsere Petition, um das Leid der Kamele und Pferde bei den ägyptischen Pyramiden zu stoppen.  


		Jetzt unterschreiben!


The post

Neue Aufdeckung: Kamele in Marokko für Tourismus missbraucht

 appeared first on

PETA Deutschland e.V.

.

author: hsa_oryx
title: OCTOBER ROUND UP
content:
First conviction under Hunting with Dogs (Scotland) Act 2023


October kicked off with

Glasgow Hunt Sabs

 reporting that Claire Bellamy, ex-huntswoman and former Master of the Lauderdale Hunt, was found guilty under the Hunting with Dogs (Scotland) Act 2023. Footage which was obtained by sabs shows hounds chasing a fox outside the area covered by a licence that had been granted by NatureScot, and was described by the judge as “

gut wrenching

.” This is the first ever conviction under the new Scottish legislation and you can learn more about the legislation in Scotland and what led to Claire’s conviction

here.


Claire Bellamy found guilty of deliberately hunting a fox with dogs in January 2025.

Image: Glasgow Hunt Sabs


Drone theft


On the 3

rd

 of October Dorset Borders Sabs reported that their drone had been stolen by The Cattistock Hunt as they hunted in Corscombe, Dorchester. The last image visible on the drone was a known member of the hunt running towards it in a field. The incident has been reported to the police and thanks to the generosity of supporters

Dorset Borders Sabs

 raised enough funds to replace the drone.


What do you do when you receive a CPW? If you’re a fox hunt then you break it as soon as possible of course


It didn’t take the Four Burrow Hunt long to break their Community Protection Warning (CPW) which had just been freshly issued by Devon and Cornwall Police. On the 10

th

 of October the hunt was caught breaking condition 7 of the CPW, by failing to give police 24 hours’ notice of their meet. As they had failed to give the details of the meet this means they won’t have provided a map of their “trail” meaning they will have broken more conditions that just number 7. It remains to be seen what action the police will take.

Read our recent article about CPW’s.


Four Burrow Hunt were issued with a CPW after years of trespass and livestock worrying.

Image:


Kernow Sabs, Monitors and Animal Rights Team-Cornwall


Stag hunting horror continues


The horror of stag hunting has continued to escalate in the south west. On the 12

th

 of October the Quantock Staghounds hunted a stag towards the A39 between Nether Stowey and Holford. This is a stretch of road where the hunt are continually causing chaos and putting people’s lives in danger.


This particular incident resulted in a

hunted stag running across the road and colliding with a car.

 A witness described how the terrified stag “

was flipped over the top of the car. Its leg kicked out smashing the rear nearside window. The Stag landed heavily on the verge.”

 Luckily the woman driving and her small child were not hurt but were badly shaken up.


The cruelty doesn’t end there. Two weeks later

North Dorset Hunt Sabs

 reported that the Quantock Staghounds had once again inflicted sickening suffering and pain on a stag. This particular large stag had a visibly infected wound on his side and it is also suspected he had a broken leg. These injuries unfortunately indicate that it is likely the stag that was hit by the car. Despite these injuries the hunt continued to torture him, subjecting him to a chase through thick gorse which no doubt would have caused him unbearable pain.


A stag hunted and terrorised by the Quantock Staghounds.

Credit: North Dorset Hunt Sabs


On the 22

nd

 of October hunt master of the Quantock Staghounds, Christopher Gibbons and huntsman Martin Watts, appeared at Taunton Magistrates Court. Gibbons is facing two counts of hunting a wild mammal under the Hunting Act, and Watts is facing one relating to the barbaric five-hour chase and ultimate

killing of a stag on the 23

rd

 of April 2026

. Both have pleaded not guilty and the case has been adjourned until the 18

th

 of January 2027 for a case management hearing; no trial date has been set. In the meantime, the Quantock Staghounds are continuing to commit abhorrent levels of animal cruelty whilst putting the safety of the general public at great risk.


This stag was tortured for five hours and ultimately killed on the 23

rd

 of April by the Quantock Staghounds.

 Huntsman and hunt master have both pleaded not guilty to charges under the Hunting Act.

Credit:


Mendip Hunt Sabs


They’re blatantly hunting foxes


Amidst the CPW’s, convictions, court hearings, road chaos and trespassing, foxes are still being chased, like the one pictured below.


Beds and Bucks Hunt Sabs

 along with

Peterborough Hunt Sabs

 have been keeping the pressure on …

author: L214
title: Enquête abattoir Cooperl
content:
L214 publie une enquête sur l’étourdissement des cochons au CO₂ dans l’un des plus gros abattoirs de France : l’abattoir Cooperl de Montfort-sur-Meu, en Ille-et-Vilaine (Bretagne).

Les images, commentées par l'écrivaine Marie Darrieussecq, montrent la cruauté de cette méthode d'étourdissement dont les instances scientifiques ont établi qu’elle est source de peur, de détresse et de souffrance.

Plus de trente vétérinaires signent un appel publié ce jour pour demander l’interdiction du gazage au CO₂ des cochons. L214 se joint à cette demande et entame un recours contre l’État pour faire interdire cette pratique. L’enseigne de supermarchés Carrefour fait fabriquer par son partenaire Cooperl ses produits à base de viande de porc sous ses marques distributeurs, notamment sa marque Filière Qualité Carrefour. L’association demande à Carrefour de refuser le gazage des cochons et de signer le Plant Protein Pact.

Le musicien Moby apporte son soutien et appelle à signer la pétition.

Chaque heure d’abattage, plus de 800 cochons sont gazés au CO₂ à l’abattoir Cooperl de Montfort-sur-Meu, en Bretagne. Plongés dans une fosse à haute concentration en CO₂, les cochons ont la sensation de se noyer : ils hurlent, paniquent, cherchent désespérément à fuir. Il leur faut entre 21 et 60 secondes pour perdre conscience…

Ce n’est ni instantané, ni sans souffrance. Les instances scientifiques européenne (EFSA) et britannique (AWC) l’affirment depuis 20 ans : cette méthode provoque douleur, peur et détresse respiratoire. Le Royaume-Uni envisage même d’y renoncer, et plus de trente vétérinaires demandent son interdiction.

Pourtant, l’abattoir Cooperl de Montfort-sur-Meu a investi en 2024 environ 5 millions d'euros dans cet équipement qui permet d’abattre un nombre gigantesque d’animaux, de conquérir de nouveaux marchés, d’augmenter les cadences et la productivité. L’enseigne Carrefour fait fabriquer par son partenaire Cooperl des produits à base de cochons gazés sous ses marques, dont la Filière Qualité Carrefour, tout en se disant « pionnier sur le bien-être animal »…

À l’État français : interdire le gazage au CO₂ des cochons ;

À Carrefour : ne plus s’approvisionner en produits issus de cochons gazés et participer à un changement collectif en s'engageant dans le Plant Protein Pact, pour prendre part à une réduction de moitié du nombre d’animaux tués d’ici 2030.

Plus nous serons nombreux et nombreuses, plus il sera difficile pour les responsables de fermer les yeux. Signez et partagez : les cochons ne peuvent pas parler pour eux-mêmes, mais nous, oui.

Contre la souffrance des animaux, agissez à nos côtés avec un don.

title: Varto Ekoloji Platformu’ndan, Doğu Anadolu Kalkınma Ajansı’nın toplantı planına tepki
content:
Varto Ekoloji Platformu Varto kültür Merkezinde, Doğu Anadolu Kalkınma Ajansı tarafından düzenlenmesi planlanan etkinliğe tepki gösterdi. Daha önce Muş’ta halktan ve ekoloji örgütlerinden gizlenerek yapılan toplantıda, daha sonra jeotermal güzellemesi yapıldığının ortaya çıkması üzerine, benzer bir etkinliğin de Varto da yapılması tepki çekti. Platform tarafından paylaşılan açıklamada, Varto halkının, toprağını ve suyunu hedef alan, halkın yararına olmayan sömürü projelerine karşı 8 aydan fazladır iradesini direnerek ve mücadele ederek net bir şekilde gösterdiği vurgulandı.

Açıklamada, Varto halkının mücadelesine rağmen düzenlenmesi planlanan toplantıya karşı, “Varto Kültür Merkezi’nde sözde bilim insanı İskender Dölek’in katılımıyla gerçekleştirilmesi planlanan toplantı, halkın aylardır sürdürdüğü bu kararlı direnişi kırma ve doğamızı yıkıma uğratacak projeleri meşrulaştırma çabasıdır. Halka ait kamusal alanların, Varto’nun geleceğini karartmak isteyenlerin propaganda alanı haline getirilmesini kesinlikle kabul etmiyoruz. Bilim; şirketlerin fonlarıyla hareket edenlerin değil, halkın ve doğanın hakikatini savunanların yanındadır” ifadelerine yer verildi.

Açıklamanın devamında, şu ifadelere yer verildi:

“Bu doğrultuda Varto Ekoloji Platformu olarak açık tavrımızdır:

Fonlu ve Şirket Odaklı Anlayışa Soruyoruz:

Sermaye grupları ve maden/enerji şirketleri tarafından fonlanan, talan projelerine zemin hazırlayan bu sözde bilgilendirme toplantılarını hangi çıkarlar karşılığında yürütüyorsunuz?”

STK, kurum ve muhtarlara çağrı yapılan açıklamada, “Varto halkının 8 aydır ilmek ilmek büyüttüğü direniş iradesine sahip çıkın. Şirket fonlarıyla hazırlanan bu meşrulaştırma toplantısına kesinlikle katılmayın, boykot edin” çağrısı yapıldı.

Kamusal mekan vurgusu yapılan açıklamada, “Varto halkının ortak malı olan alanların, halkın onaylamadığı sömürü projelerine tahsis edilmesini reddediyoruz. Varto halkı toprağına, suyuna ve yaşam alanlarına sahip çıkmaya; bu sömürü projelerine karşı mücadelesini kararlılıkla sürdürmeye devam edecektir” denildi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Alex Cuadros
title: Bill Gates’ $29B Stake in Landfill Company Tied to Major Methane Emissions
content:
Gates has called on businesses to fight climate change. But his own investments tell a different story.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

In November 2015, world leaders descended on Paris to negotiate a historic agreement to limit global warming. But on the summit’s opening day, attention turned to a private citizen slouched awkwardly in a chair on stage: Bill Gates.

Gates, with his characteristic flop of sandy hair, grinned impishly as President Barack Obama called him a “visionary” and a “driving force” behind a pair of pledges that both saw as key to the larger agreement. First the world’s largest economies would double their spending on research into clean-energy technologies. Then investors like Gates would back the startups that emerged. The Microsoft cofounder had already enlisted two dozen other billionaires to join the effort.

For Gates, who’d become increasingly consumed by this unprecedented threat to human well-being, the moment marked his arrival as a leading figure in the fight against climate change.

“If we back over 50 different breakthrough approaches, we know that several of those will give us the solution that we need,” Gates said during his own speech. He would invest at least $2 billion of his own money in companies developing geothermal wells, new kinds of nuclear reactors and machines that pull carbon from the air, to name just a few.

With much less fanfare, however, Gates has put more than double that amount into a very dirty, old-school industry. At the time of the Paris summit, he was already the dominant shareholder of America’s No. 2 landfill operator, Republic Services. He has since increased his stake to 38% of the company, a position worth $29 billion.

While fossil fuels get most of the attention, scientists increasingly see landfills as a crucial climate issue. They’re responsible for as much as a fifth of the country’s emissions of methane, a highly potent greenhouse gas, studies show. Republic alone generates as much climate pollution as 3 million gasoline-burning cars each year, according to its own reports.

One might imagine that a landfill operator with Gates as its largest shareholder — and with three people closely linked to Gates on its board — would lead the way in tackling those emissions. Even after seemingly softening his stance on global warming in a controversial blog post last year, Gates remains one of the world’s most prominent voices on the issue. As he did in his bestselling 2021 book “How to Avoid a Climate Disaster,” he continues to advocate for cutting emissions, and he has called on his fellow business leaders to do their part.

Gates, though, has failed to make Republic live up to his own climate principles, a ProPublica investigation has found. Federal inspectors have repeatedly found methane escaping from Republic landfills at levels above federal limits. The company has refrained from adopting the ambitious emissions-reduction goal embraced by its main competitor. Republic has even lobbied against policies that could make the wider industry cleaner, including by keeping organic waste out of landfills in the first place.

“It seems very likely that Bill Gates has the power to influence Republic’s behavior to make it more climate-friendly, even if that costs the company profits,” said Ann Lipton, a legal scholar who studies corporate governance at the University of Colorado, Boulder.

As for whether he should, in her words, “put his money where his mouth is,” Lipton said, “you can leave it to the reader to make the moral judgment.”

Gates didn’t respond to repeated requests to discuss his landfill investments, and ProPublica couldn’t find any public comments he’s made about them. But the bet has proven wildly lucrative. Since November 1999, when he emerged as the owner of 5% of Republic’s shares — “It’s ‘Garbage In’ for Gates,” the New York Post headline read — the company’s stock price has soared thirtyfold. And Gates has personally received $2.6 billion in dividends, a ProPublica analysis of securities filings shows.

In those early days, Gates hadn’t yet awakened to the threat of global warming. It was a different time. Microsoft Windows ran on more than 80% of personal computers. Gates was the world’s richest person, and his bespectacled face graced the cover of Time magazine twice that year. He was simultaneously criticized for what a …

author: ROAPE
title: South Africa’s water crisis is about more than water
content:
Komani—formerly known as Queenstown—is a town in the Eastern Cape province, in the eastern part of South Africa. It is part of the Chris Hani District and serves as an important commercial and administrative centre for surrounding rural communities and smaller towns. Its current water crisis is therefore not simply a local inconvenience in a little-known South African town. It is a window into a much larger question facing many countries: what happens when ageing public infrastructure, unreliable energy supply, weak public finances, fragmented institutions and unequal historical development intersect?


South Africa is an upper-middle-income country with sophisticated water infrastructure, major dams, treatment works and publicly owned bulk-water institutions. Yet access to reliable water remains deeply unequal. The country’s democratic Constitution recognises access to sufficient water as a right, while the practical responsibility for getting water from national and regional systems to households is spread across several institutions. This distinction is important: a water crisis can occur even where there is water in dams and substantial treatment capacity, because the infrastructure and institutions required to move that water to households can fail.


Komani makes this problem tangible. During September 2026, residents, community organisations and technical personnel examined the local water system, including the treatment works, pumping arrangements, reservoirs and community experience of repeated interruptions. Their findings, set out below, should be read both as evidence about Komani and as a case study of a wider infrastructure problem. The purpose is not to present Komani as unique, but to show why water security has to be understood as a chain linking water sources, energy, treatment, bulk supply, municipal distribution, finance, maintenance and public accountability.


South Africa’s water crisis

 is usually narrated as a story about drought, ageing pipes, leaking infrastructure or municipalities that cannot deliver. Those explanations are not wrong, but they are incomplete. The more revealing question is what happens between the moment water exists in a dam and the moment it reaches a household tap. The answer is a chain: raw-water abstraction, pumping, treatment, electricity, storage, bulk conveyance, reservoirs, municipal distribution and maintenance. A failure at any critical point can turn available water into a dry tap.


The Komani water crisis makes this chain unusually visible. Community fieldwork undertaken between 15 and 17 September 2026 combined a technical visit to the Komani Water Treatment Plant with community testimony and a public mobilisation. The technical evidence identified electrical faults, damaged control panels, faulty generators and electricity interruptions affecting pumping to reservoirs. The community then connected these failures to their own experience of recurring water interruptions and called for reliable electricity alongside reliable water.


The national lesson is

bigger than Komani

. South Africa has to stop discussing the water crisis as if water and electricity were two unrelated service-delivery sectors. Water systems are energy systems. Treatment plants, booster stations, transfer schemes and reservoir pumping require reliable electricity. The Department of Water and Sanitation’s own recent regulatory standards recognise this dependency by requiring water-service institutions to provide backup generation or alternative electricity sources for critical water and wastewater infrastructure.


The Komani numbers expose the difference between ‘water available’ and ‘water delivered’


The Komani field report records a reported pumping capacity of 360 litres per second for the newer treatment plant and 122 litres per second for the older plant — a combined nominal figure of 482 litres per second. If that rate were sustained continuously, it would correspond to about 41.6 megalitres (ML) per day. But this is a theoretical conversion, not a measurement of actual daily production.


The same fieldwork records Waterdown Dam at 189 litres per second and Xonxa Dam at approximately 180 litres per second. Bokolo Dam’s contribution was not confirmed. The two confirmed figures together amount to 369 litres per second, or about 31.9 ML/day. That gap is important: the system cannot be understood by looking only at treatment-plant nameplate capacity, because the upstream …

author: winter oak
title: True anarchy will banish the psychopaths
content:
by Paul Cudenec, who reads the article

here


I wrote a

piece

 in September about the roots of the word “anarchy” and wondered “if the deep meaning of anarchy is, in fact, our human struggle against vitaphobic, authoritarian and psychopathic forces known as archons”. [1]


The Swedish writer

Per Shapiro

 [2] subsequently sent me a pdf of a 2014 essay by John Lamb Lash on the archons of gnostic tradition in which he likewise presents anarchy as the antidote to their domination.


In ‘

The True Anarchy of Life on Earth

‘ Lash writes of “the scheme of the Archon mind-parasites to insinuate themselves into human reality and take it over, making humans become like them, robotic, slavish, incapable of intention, discovery, or novelty”. [3]


He stresses: “To fall under the spell of the Authorities is to concede power to their false magic: under the power of deception, we deceive ourselves about what power really is and lose all sense of our own power”. [4]


In order to resist this rule we need to embrace anarchy in the

real

 [5] sense of the word: “We cannot realize our true humanity without beating the Authorities. There is more than one way to do so, but the central and decisive way is to choose anarchy in defiance of

any

 authority that does not demonstrate benevolence toward life in all forms… Even the word carries the essential message: an-arch, ‘against authority, against archons'”. [6]


Lash equates the gnostic version of the archons with “globalist predators and serial killers, who are one and the same breed of conniving, murderous deviants”. [7]


Wondering what makes them so different from us, and how they achieve their deception and control, he suggests: “Archons and their human counterparts gain control over humanity through a particular ‘seizure’ that operates in the back of the brain and in the field of peripheral vision simultaneously” – this involves the “reptilian brain

in its deviant or exaggerated mode

“. [8]


“In large measure, the quasi-magical or occult power attributed to globalist perpetrators is a hoax, operating under the Wizard of Oz effect. Note that to enforce their presumed magical powers, the perpetrators need to exert enormous continual efforts of two kinds: brainwashing through the media, and threat of force through the military.


“Without a constant dual-barreled barrage, requiring the complicity of human beings to suppress and deceive their fellow creatures, their vaunted magic would quickly fade and dissipate…


“In reality, the NEWOs [New World Order psychopaths] can only sustain the

illusion

 of magical supremacy as long as they suppress and deviate human potential, where the true magic abides: that is,

in our species’ innate capacity for interactive magic with the animating powers of the planetary goddess

. Unless the NEWOs can suppress

that

 capacity in a brutal manner all the time, it will naturally and spontaneously assert itself”. [9]


This is how I also see anarchy – as the life force within humankind, constantly surging forth in each new generation and trying to break out of the industrial-imperial prison in which we have been locked up for so long.


Of course, the system has to lie about what anarchy is, as Lash sets out. “The supreme moral illusion confronting humanity operates like this: those who falsely assume authority over others demand obedience to their commands

on the claim that disobedience would result in social chaos and anarchy

.

author: TJ Jordan and Cécile Marchand
title: How a French Oil Executive Is Working With the Trump Administration to ‘Kill’ Europe’s Methane Plan
content:
A TotalEnergies executive is working with U.S. officials to delay the implementation of new European Union methane rules, raising questions over the company’s pledges to tackle leaks of the potent greenhouse gas.


François-Régis Mouton, formerly vice-president of gas advocacy at TotalEnergies, has been representing the International Association of Oil and Gas Producers (IOGP), a London-based fossil fuel lobby group, on an assignment from the French oil giant since 2018.


Mouton has repeatedly shared and engaged with hard right, anti-renewable energy and climate science-denial content on his personal social media, a review by DeSmog and French environmental newsroom Vert found.


Mouton, who serves as IOGP’s Europe managing director, met with U.S. federal officials on at least three occasions to discuss the European Union Methane Regulation (EUMR) in the past 14 months, according to social media posts. The new framework would force oil and gas importers to meet certain standards for methane leaks in their supply chains or face big fines.


In October 2025, Mouton visited the White House to brief the National Energy Dominance Council, a pro-fossil fuel Trump administration advisory body, on how the IOGP could “work together to address and remove regulatory barriers such as…the #EUMethaneRegulation,” according to LinkedIn

posts

 by Mouton and the council’s executive director Jarrod Agen.


This year, U.S. officials have repeatedly cited IOGP arguments for delaying the regulations after meeting with Mouton, including in a 27 April

op-ed

 in the Financial Times by U.S. Ambassador to the EU Andrew Puzder headlined “The EU’s methane regulation could spark an energy crisis.” Puzder’s office sent an email, seen by DeSmog and Vert, to EU member states on 20 October, which similarly echoed IOGP language warning that the regulations could threaten gas supplies to Europe.


These incidents form part of a wider pattern of closed-door meetings and public statements that place Mouton in a key role in campaigns by the Trump administration and oil industry to delay the rules by at least three years, according to a DeSmog-Vert review of social media feeds, freedom of information requests, industry documents and interviews.


Mouton assumed this role despite his employer TotalEnergies and its CEO Patrick Pouyanné spending the past decade painting the company as a leader on methane action and publicly backing the EU Methane Regulation. Pouyanné is one of three top oil industry figures championing the Oil and Gas Decarbonization Charter, a voluntary initiative to curb greenhouse gas emissions from across the sector, which is due to launch a status update at the UN climate conference COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, which opens today.


By sponsoring trade groups such as the IOGP, TotalEnergies can work at arm’s length to delay, weaken and ideally defeat the regulation altogether, according to sources involved in industry discussions of the rules.


“They are coming to kill this regulation,” said one of the sources, who spoke on the condition of anonymity for fear of professional repercussions.


On Friday, the European Council — made up of heads of state or government of the EU’s 27 countries —

endorsed

 a European Commission proposal for a one-year delay in implementing the rules, which had been due to take effect on 1 January, 2027. The Council will now have to negotiate the final decision with the 720-seat European Parliament, which has voted for a three-year delay amid the fossil fuel industry lobbying.


This story was published in partnership with French environmental newsroom

Vert


and the

EUobserver

.


 


‘Emergency Brake’


The U.S. has been

on track

 to eclipse Norway as Europe’s biggest supplier of natural gas — used to heat tens of millions of the continent’s homes and power industry — since the February, 2022 invasion of Ukraine prompted the bloc to seek alternatives to Russian supplies.


TotalEnergies imports more American liquefied natural gas (LNG) to Europe than any of its rivals,

according

 to research and advocacy group Oil Change International.


Methane, the main component of natural gas, has a heating effect on earth’s atmosphere more than 80 times stronger than carbon dioxide over 20 years. Scientists say that urgent action to stop plumes of the gas

seeping

 from the fossil fuel industry’s sprawling networks of pipelines, wellheads, storage tanks, and transport vessels represents a potential …

author: Solarpunk Magazine
title: Solarpunk Horror, Lunarpunk Submissions, and 2027 Magazine Submissions
content:
We’ve got some exciting announcements to share! There’s a brand-new lunarpunk anthology seeking submissions, our special horror-themed issue of Solarpunk Magazine is available for preorder, we’re going to start publishing solarpunk novellas and novels, and our complete 2027 submissions schedule is now up on our website’s submissions page.

So whether you’re a reader looking for your next great story or a writer dreaming up better futures, here’s what’s coming.

Submission Window: November 1 – December 31, 2026

Android Press is preparing to venture into the shadows with What Blooms in Darkness: A Lunarpunk Anthology, edited by our co-editor-in-chief, Justine Norton-Kertson, and scheduled for publication in autumn 2027.

Lunarpunk shares solarpunk’s commitment to ecological regeneration, social justice, community, and liberatory futures, while exploring the possibilities that emerge in darkness, mystery, privacy, dreams, and the hidden corners of our world.

What Blooms in Darkness asks some fascinating questions: What kinds of communities thrive beyond the reach of surveillance? What knowledge survives underground? What forms of liberation become possible when people are free to remain unseen?

Android Press is seeking stories about everything from nocturnal ecosystems and underground communities to secret mutual-aid networks, hidden cultures, rituals, and resistance movements. The anthology welcomes imaginative interpretations of lunarpunk, especially stories that challenge the assumption that darkness is inherently dangerous or frightening.

Genre: Lunarpunk, climate fiction, and related speculative fiction

Eligibility: Original, unpublished fiction by human authors worldwide

Expected publication: Autumn 2027

Whether you’re a writer or a reader, you can easily sign up to get a notification when the anthology’s crowdfunder launches in March 2027!

We’ve spent years exploring what better futures might look like. Now we’re inviting some monsters into the garden. We’re thrilled to reveal the cover and complete table of contents for Solarpunk Magazine Issue #30, our special Solarpunk Horror issue, arriving November 10, 2026!

Horror and solarpunk might seem like an unusual combination, but we think they have a lot to say to each other. What happens when the ghosts of ecological destruction refuse to stay buried? What kinds of monsters might haunt societies struggling to heal centuries of exploitation? And how do things like fear, grief, survival, and resistance fit into our visions of better futures?

This extra large special issue brings together fiction, poetry, essays, and artwork that explore the darker edges of solarpunk imagination. We’re especially excited about the lineup of writers and artists contributing to this issue.

“The Unrooted Sea” by Seiba Rosario

“The Ordinary Was Extraordinary All Along: A reflection on loss, appreciation, and radical hope from Gaza” by Aya Al-Hattab

“Reemergence of the Past” by Victoria Black

We’re incredibly grateful to all the contributors who helped bring this experiment in solarpunk horror to life.

Issue #30 releases November 10, 2026, and is available for preorder now for $6.

author: Administrador
title: Auf was wir aus sind. Was ja und was nein.
content:
Obacht – Familien Sucherinnen, mit oder ohne Kollektiv.

Obacht – diejenigen, die Familien Sucherinnen begleiten.

Schwestern, Compañeras [Familien Sucherinnen]:

Dies ist der erste von verschiedenen Texten, in denen wir einige Zweifel und Fragen klären werden, die uns erreichten. Wir werden darin antworten auf einige Kränkungen und Beleidigungen und Euch nach und nach den Zeitplan der Delegation bekanntgeben. Wir bitten Euch, diesem Schreiben sowie den folgenden gegenüber aufmerksam zu sein.

A.- Wir haben eine Reihe von Verwirrungen, Unverschämtheiten und Manipulationsversuche über Ziele, Daten, Orte und Aktivitäten der Delegation der Comisión Sexta Zapatista für diesen Dezember und die erste Januar-Woche 2027 entdeckt.

Es wird von einem angeblichen mexikoweiten Treffen zwischen Familien Sucherinnen und der zapatistischen Delegation am 6. Dezember an der sogenannten »Glorieta de los Desaparecidos« (*1) gesprochen und fehl informiert, sowie von anderen öffentlichen Aktivitäten der Comisión Sexta Zapatista zu anderen Daten und an anderen Orten.

Dies ist falsch, Schwestern und Compañeras Sucherinnen. Vielleicht werden einige, die dazu aufrufen, ihre Versammlung an diesem Ort halten oder anderen Orten, welche in Bezug stehen zu Eurem gerechten Kampf; wir werden dort jedoch nicht teilnehmen.

Nicht nur weil die »Einladung«, die wir von dort erhielten, Ignoranz, Unredlichkeit und Grobheiten widerspiegelt. Keine*r wird eingeladen, indem er*sie beleidigt wird. Bei passender Gelegenheit werden wir darüber mehr erklären. [Wir werden nicht teilnehmen] auch weil wir nicht auf Massenversammlungen mit den Familien Sucherinnen aus sind.

Die Gruppen, Kollektive* und Familien Sucherinnen, welche sich an den Glorietas oder wo auch immer versammeln, können sich mit uns persönlich treffen, Gruppe für Gruppe – an dem Aufenthaltsort der Delegation in Mexiko-Stadt und an Orten, die öffentlich gemacht werden – indem sie sich via des [Menschenrechtszentrums] Frayba registrieren, zu den ihnen passenden Tagen und Uhrzeiten – wenn sie es derart möchten.

B.- Schaut, Ihr und wir, die zapatistischen Pueblos, wissen, dass Ihr nicht nur Differenzen habt sondern offene Rivalitäten und Dispute – zwischen Kollektiven der Sucherinnen, zwischen Netzwerken und Bewegungen. Sogar einschließlich dass versucht wird, gegen gewisse Kollektive Einspruch zu erheben und zu bestimmen, wer sich mit der zapatistischen Delegation trifft oder nicht. Vielleicht wächst deshalb die Anzahl der Familien Sucherinnen, die in keiner Gruppe oder keinem Kollektiv sind und die uns direkt kontaktieren.

Wir werden keine*n beurteilen, verurteilen. Wir werden nicht sagen, welche die korrekte und welche die falsche Strategie ist, welche legitim ist oder nicht, welche gut ist oder schlecht.

Wir denken, dass der*diejenige – die*der Wahrheit und Gerechtigkeit sucht und zum Ziel hat, den*diejenige*n zu finden, der*die ihm*ihr auf Grund eines gewaltsamen Verschwundenmachens fehlt – kann und soll all die Wege durchlaufen und an all die Türen klopfen, die seinem*ihrem Schmerz Erleichterung bringt:

Ob sie draußen mit Spitzhacke und Schaufel die Suche umsetzen; auf lokale, bundesstaatliche oder staatliche Justiz-Instanzen zurückgreifen; sich mit der Präsidentin und ihrer Funktionärspyramide treffen; internationale und mexikoweite Kampagnen machen; oder es lediglich schaffen, die Fotos ihrer Vermissten in ihren Straßen und Stadtteilen zu plakatieren; sich an Menschenrechts-NGOs wenden; die Unterstützung von Spezialist*innen in der Verschwundenen-Suche und der Analyse von menschlichen Überresten anfordern; auf Demos, Kundgebungen, Mahnwachen, Besetzung von Gebäuden sowie Straßen- und Autobahnblockaden zurückgreifen; beten; verfluchen; all das zuvor Gesagte.

Und immerzu mit der Erinnerung, dem Eingedenken als Antrieb.

Was auch immer Ihr entscheidet und macht, es ist eine Entscheidung von Euch, von denjenigen, die diesen Schmerz tragen und diese Angst erleiden – und von sonst niemanden.

Somit werden wir Euch nicht sagen, was zu tun ist, noch für/ statt Euch tun. Wir werden Euch kennenlernen, Euch zuhören, Euch umarmen.

Wir werden nicht sagen, welches Netzwerk oder Kollektiv besser als die anderen ist.

C.- Deshalb bevorzugt unsere Reise weder Massenaktionen noch Medienspektakel, weder Vollversammlungen noch das Schaffen von Bündnissen, Zusammenschlüssen oder Ähnlichem, auch keine neue Organisation, die alle Kollektive und Familien Sucherinnen umfasst, oder außerhalb von ihnen.

Auch …

author: Shannia Cabuello
title: Artists, Ayta sing vs Pax Silica
content:
Photo by Shannia Angel Cabuello

Artists and other advocates amplified their opposition against a US-led initiative through song.

On November 6, an artist group launched the anti-Pax Silica anthem “Get Off Our Lands” in a solidarity night filled with protest songs.

Produced by the Concerned Artists of the Philippines (CAP), the song was accompanied by a documentary music video featuring the Ayta community in Sitio Kalangitan, whose ancestral lands and natural resources are threatened by displacement and plunder.

Through the song, CAP aimed to expose the false promises behind the Pax Silica and to condemn those in power who allowed it.

Cultural performances and solidarity messages completed the program as part of the Trump Out campaign and the ‘12 Days of Protests’, building up the major protest actions on November 16 and 17.

Ayta elders also attended the solidarity night and expressed their strong rejection of Pax Silica, chanting “Ako Labay Ya Pax Silica!” (I don’t like Pax Silica!).

They led a community dance ritual to drive away “bad spirits,” which they associate with the Pax Silica Initiative and the impending visit of US President Donald Trump for the ASEAN Summit.

Ayta Chieftain Nelson De Guzman countered the statement of Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA) President Joshua Bingcang that no Indigenous community would be affected by the Pax Silica Initiative. He said that no proper consultation was conducted within their community.

“They learned that they were being driven away from their land even before they knew about the project,” said Sandiwa Network project coordinator Gina Cambronero.

“The Pax Silica will kill our future. We nurtured our lands. We cannot allow foreigners to claim it,” said Ayta Indigenous woman Tessie Sanchez.

Sanchez told Bulatlat that planting rice, taro, and sweet potato helped support her seven children. She feared that the signing of the agreement could dry their water sources and take away their farmlands.

“The ruling class used the term pax which meant peace. But is there peace in it? They use it as instruments for deception,” Cambronero said.

“We just want peace in our tribe and in our land,” De Guzman said in the song’s documentary music video.

Around 20,000 peasants and 15,000 Ayta could be reportedly displaced once its Artificial Intelligence hub was established on the 1,620 hectares of land in Tarlac.

The anthem started by introducing the Philippines as a friendly Southeast Asian country that shares its homeland to everyone, even to foreign ones.

The music video explained that Ferdinand Marcos Jr. volunteered to give the agricultural and ancestral lands in Tarlac to the United States to establish an Economic Security Zone.

CAP said that the establishment of an Artificial Intelligence hub in Tarlac and the Luzon Economic Corridor (LEC) in Subic Bay, Clark, Manila and Batangas that claims of job creation and economic security are false promises. The group said that it only “prioritizes corporate profits and militarization, fueling war for the US benefit.”

“In the past years, we have always been at a disadvantage with US relations. There are already several trade agreements that only lead to our losses,” said Attorney Rey Cortez of National Union of People’s Lawyers (NUPL).

Cortez added in a solidarity message that it only allowed for the United States to mine the country’s lands and determine how to exploit its resources. He described the government’s marketing of the country’s environment and sovereignty as unconstitutional, as only the Filipinos are allowed to explore the Philippines’ critical minerals.

“Development should not be measured by the number of investments, infrastructure, and technology advancements. Its effect on the people, community, and environment must also be analysed,” said College of Social Work and Community Development Dean and CAP member Justin Nicolas.

Arthur Cadungon of CAP and writer of Get Off Our Lands said that the anthem is not just for the fight against the Pax Silica Initiative, but also a song of protest against the reclamation of Manila Bay, Laguna Lake, and Pasig River Expressway (PAREX).

“An example of this is the Laguna Lake, which before sources at least 40% of protein food sources like mussels and freshwater fish tilapia,” said Environmental Advocates group Nilad coordinator Samantha Yzabel.
