title: KESK Samsun Şubeler Platformu: Atakum Belediyesinde işten atılan işçiler yalnız değildir
content:
Kamu Emekçileri Sendikası (KESK) Samsun Şubeler Platformu, Atakum Belediyesinde işten atılan işçilerle dayanışma açıklaması yaptı. “Emeğin hakkı, işçinin onuru ve örgütlü mücadelesi teslim alınamaz” denilen açıklamada, Atakum Belediyesindeki çalışma koşullarına da tepki gösterildi.

KESK Dönem Sözcüsü Uğurcan Albak imzasıyla yayımlanan açıklamada, “Atakum Belediyesi’nde aylardır ücretlerini alamadıkları için haklarını arayan, insanca yaşam ve güvenceli çalışma koşulları talep eden işçi arkadaşlarımızın işten çıkarılması, yalnızca birkaç emekçinin işsiz bırakılması değildir. Bu karar, emeğin haklı taleplerine karşı geliştirilmiş açık bir baskı ve sindirme politikasıdır. Samsun’un Atakum ilçesinde yaşananlar, yerel yönetimlerin emek karşısındaki tutumunu ve siyasi söylemleriyle uygulamaları arasındaki çelişkiyi bir kez daha gözler önüne sermiştir. Kendilerini emekten, halktan ve demokrasiden yana tanımlayan yönetimlerin de emekçilerin en temel hakları söz konusu olduğunda bu ilkelerin gereğini yerine getirmediği görülmektedir” ifadelerine yer verildi.

İşçinin ücretini istemesinin suç olmadığı vurgulanan açıklamada, “Emeğinin karşılığını talep etmesi, sendikal örgütlenme hakkını kullanması ve insanca çalışma koşulları için mücadele etmesi en temel demokratik ve sendikal hakkıdır. Bu hakları kullanan işçileri işten çıkarmak, sorunları çözmek değil, emekçileri işsizlik tehdidiyle susturmaya çalışmaktır. Belediyeler, hangi siyasi anlayışla yönetilirse yönetilsin, kamusal sorumluluklarının ve emek karşısındaki yükümlülüklerinin gereğini yerine getirmek zorundadır. Sosyal belediyecilik, emekten yana olmak ve halkçı yönetim anlayışı, seçim dönemlerinde kullanılan söylemlerle değil; çalışanların ücretlerinin zamanında ödenmesi, iş güvencesinin sağlanması, sendikal haklara saygı gösterilmesi ve emekçilerin iradesinin tanınmasıyla mümkündür” denildi.

Atakum Belediyesi’nde yaşananların, yalnızca belediye işçilerinin sorunu olmadığı, Samsun'da emeğiyle geçinen bütün işçilerin, kamu emekçilerinin ve emek örgütlerinin ortak problemi olduğu vurgulanan açıklamada, “Çünkü biliyoruz ki bir işyerinde işçinin hak arama mücadelesine yönelen saldırı, başka işyerlerindeki emekçilere de verilmiş bir gözdağıdır. İşçi sınıfının tarihsel kazanımları, bağımsız ve öz iradeleriyle gelişen bağımsız, demokratik, mücadeleci sendikal örgütlenme ve birleşik sınıf dayanışmasıyla elde edilmiştir. Emekçilerin iradesini esas alan, mücadeleyi dar pazarlıklara sıkıştıran ve işverenlerin politikalarına yedeklenen sendikal anlayışlara karşı gerçek bir emek ve demokrasi mücadelesini büyütmek zorundayız. .Sendikalar, yalnızca üyelerinin aidatlarını alan, toplu sözleşme dönemlerinde masaya oturan kurumlar değildir” vurgusu yapıldı.

Açıklamada talepler şu şekilde sıralandı:

“İşten çıkarılan bütün işçiler derhal işlerine iade edilmelidir.

Birikmiş ücretler ve işçilerin tüm özlük hakları eksiksiz ödenmelidir.

İşçilerin sendikal örgütlenme ve hak arama özgürlüğüne yönelik baskılara son verilmelidir.

İşçilerin iradesi ve çalışma yaşamında demokratik hak ve özgürlükler güvence altına alınmalıdır.

Emekçileri işsizlik ve yoksullukla karşı karşıya bırakan uygulamalardan vazgeçilmelidir.”

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Unknown
title: Murder of Vesile Akın leaves five children without their mother
content:
On 9 November, Vesile Akın, 35, was attacked with a knife on Bismarck Street in Düren, in Germany’s North Rhine-Westphalia state, by her 39-year-old husband, Ferhat Akın. The couple had been living separately due to severe marital problems. Vesile Akın, a mother of five originally from Mardin (Mêrdîn), died in hospital from her severe injuries. Ferhat Akın, who fled the scene, was subsequently caught by police.


She had previously requested protection


It was reported that Vesile Akın had contacted the police and requested protection because she had been threatened by her husband. Reports indicate that police had previously taken action against him due to their marital problems and his threats, and that restraining measures had been imposed. However, the woman reportedly continued to be harassed.


Despite her previous complaints and the protective measures reportedly put in place, Vesile Akın was murdered. Her death has raised serious questions about the effectiveness of security measures and mechanisms designed to protect women from violence.


Calls for investigation into possible failures


The murder of Vesile Akın has once again highlighted the importance of ensuring that women facing threats of violence receive timely and effective protection. Calls have been made for a review of the previous complaints filed in connection with the case, the protection orders issued, and the security measures taken. There have also been demands for any possible negligence to be exposed and for those responsible to face the necessary legal action.

author: Unknown
title: Fuel crisis in Kobanê takes heavy toll on residents
content:
The increase in fuel prices across Syria has deepened the economic crisis in Kobanê. Following the rise in fuel costs, prices for food, transport and other essential goods have also increased. In the city, where the cost of many products has doubled or tripled, people's purchasing power continues to decline, while concerns over heating are growing ahead of the winter months.


Rising fuel prices are particularly affecting traders and small business owners involved in commerce and production. Higher transportation and production costs are being passed on to consumers through increased prices. Meanwhile, difficulties in obtaining diesel have forced residents to turn to electric heaters for warmth, placing additional pressure on the electricity network.


Speaking to ANF, residents and shopkeepers in Kobanê said they would face numerous difficulties this winter. They stated that although the amount of fuel being distributed had not changed, the prices of almost every product they purchased had increased.


The cost of transporting a truckload of goods has doubled


Kamıran Baz, a business owner in Kobanê, said there had been serious difficulties in obtaining fuel this year. He explained that residents struggling to find diesel had begun purchasing electric heaters, which was also having a negative impact on the electricity network.


Noting that rising fuel prices had increased transportation costs, Baz said that transporting a truckload of goods, which previously cost $100, now cost $200 — twice as much.


Emphasising that rising diesel prices were directly affecting not only transportation but also the prices of goods and services, Baz said shopkeepers were being forced to pass their increased costs on to consumers.


Prices increased


Mihemed Memiş, who works in metal fabrication and also sells stoves, said the increase in fuel prices had raised production costs. Stating that almost all products had become more expensive this year compared with last year, Memiş called for diesel prices to be reduced. He said: “Everything has become much more expensive this year compared with last year. Our current demand is for diesel prices to be reduced somewhat. I manufacture doors, and whereas I previously sold each door for 30 US dollars, I now sell them for 40 US dollars. This is because diesel has become so expensive.”


No diesel for stoves


Memiş said he had to run his generator for long hours to keep his metal fabrication business operating. He added that rising diesel prices had forced him to increase the cost of manufacturing doors. He explained that they had also started selling stoves ahead of the approaching winter season. However, because diesel was difficult to obtain and insufficient quantities were being distributed, people could not afford to buy stoves. Stressing that the fuel shortage was affecting both production and people's ability to heat their homes, Memiş called for prices to be reduced and the problems surrounding fuel supplies to be resolved.

title: YRK Commander pays tribute to the martyrs: We will ensure that their goals are achieved
content:
On 5 November, the Press Center of the People’s Defense Forces (HPG) announced the identities of nine guerrilla fighters from Rojhilat who lost their lives between 2006 and 2022 in various regions of Kurdistan.


On 9 November, the HPG Press Center announced the identities of 15 guerrilla fighters from the Maku city of East Kurdistan who joined the Kurdish freedom movement and lost their lives at different times and in various locations between 2007 and 2024.


Speaking to ANF, Şiyar Şevger, a member of the Command Council of the East Kurdistan Units (Yekîneyên Rojhilatê Kurdistan, YRK), made the following remarks in memory of the martyrs:


https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/2ff679a0_20261111095750_2026-11-11-habermerkezi-siyar-sevger-yrk-komutanligi-uyesi-nirxandin-1.mp4


“I dedicate this process that has been initiated to all our martyrs. I commemorate all our martyrs across the four parts of Kurdistan and bow respectfully before their memory.


Recently, the names of martyrs from East Kurdistan (Rojhilat), as well as followers of Apo from Rojhilat who fell in North Kurdistan (Bakur), have been announced. These martyrs have fostered a spirit of unity among Kurds. The martyrs have consolidated the paradigm put forward by Leader Apo [Abdullah Öcalan] to defend the Kurdish people. The martyrs are leading the way for humanity in the Middle East. The paradigm they have championed is intended to serve all humanity and the unity of the Kurdish people.


In fact, the martyrs have enabled us to understand ourselves and our history. More importantly, they have helped us recognize our enemies who have carried out massacres against our people. It is thanks to Leader Apo’s ideas and philosophy, together with the sacrifices of the martyrs, that we have reached this point today. Their goals will undoubtedly be achieved, and the struggle they waged will not have been in vain.


As the people of Rojhilat, we must honor and stand by the martyrs with great pride. Regardless of which city or village they come from, all our people, families and patriots must rally around the families of the martyrs, come together and show solidarity with them. They must not be left alone. The pain of every family is the pain of all Kurds. Our families have paid a heavy price and sacrificed their loved ones. Their grief is immense. Therefore, no one should leave them alone. We owe to the martyrs who gave their lives to defend our honor.


There are many martyrs from Sine in particular. There are martyrs from our other cities as well, but Sine is a city of resistance and revolution. All our people in Sine must unite around these families and stand by them. We have nothing to fear.


The role of our mothers in this revolution is particularly important. Everyone must stand by the mothers who raised their children and entrusted them to this movement. Mothers are the hope of the Kurdish people and the peoples of the Middle East. As long as our mothers are alive, Kurdistan will undoubtedly achieve success.


To the martyrs whose names have been announced so far, particularly those from Rojhilat and the other parts of Kurdistan, and to all the martyrs whose names will be announced in the future, we make this pledge: We will certainly uphold their struggle and ensure that their goals are achieved.


Recently, some reports have appeared in the media questioning why the names of our martyrs have been announced so late. I believe all our people know that we are a movement engaged in struggle in the mountains of Kurdistan. The Apoist Movement has fought against the occupiers of our homeland everywhere, including in the mountains. It has carried out this struggle in the face of all kinds of technology, weapons and chemical weapons.


Amid such intense warfare, there was no opportunity to announce the deaths of our comrades in a timely manner. A peace process began following Leader Apo’s call. This peace process also marks a transition to a new phase of struggle. This transition has created an opportunity to announce the names of the martyrs. The names of martyrs from Bakur, Rojava and Bashur had been announced previously. In recent days, the names of the martyrs from Rojhilat have also been announced. This is the reason for the delay in announcing their deaths.


Our people must understand that all other speculation is part of a special warfare strategy. They should not give credence to such speculation. The Apoist Movement is not that kind of movement …

author: Unknown
title: The importance of Kurdish democracy
content:
While the Kurdish people and their friends everywhere have been eagerly anticipating “national unity,” news that even the existing administration in Southern Kurdistan has split into two has, frankly, caused considerable astonishment. Moreover, it has provoked significant anger and backlash. At the same time, it has prompted everyone to reassess their expectations and views and question the reasons behind this situation.


Yet the call made in recent months by Kurdish People’s Leader Abdullah Öcalan for the establishment of a “Democratic Unity Government” had generated considerable hope and expectations among the public. National unity was also the most widely discussed issue in the Kurdish press and public discourse. Although everyone expressed it from their own perspective, the need for national unity was the issue on which there was the greatest consensus. Both political awareness and collective sentiment reflected this need.


Admittedly, the persistent fragmentation among Kurdish principalities throughout history left those who contemplated and advocated national unity with little hope or confidence. This situation has been a constant source of criticism and frustration. The experience of Southern Kurdistan offered little reason for optimism in this regard.


Although the Kurdistan National Congress (KNK) was established a quarter of a century ago, it has been unable to fulfill its role or function effectively because certain parties have refused to participate and have obstructed its work. Despite nearly two years having passed since the elections in Southern Kurdistan, parliament had not convened, and a new government had not been formed.


Undoubtedly, all of this led to disappointment among Kurdish society and its supporters, weakening their faith in the prospect of national unity. Nevertheless, the Kurdish people remained determined and steadfast in their pursuit of unity, aware of the immense importance of Kurdish national unity for the Kurds, the Middle East and humanity as a whole. Considerable knowledge and understanding have been developed on this issue, accompanied by an increasingly strong sense of its significance. Accordingly, the Kurdish people never abandoned their demand for unity, while continuously questioning the factors obstructing it and seeking ways to overcome them.


The stance and efforts of the Kurdish Freedom Movement on this issue have always been positive. In fact, the movement has consistently devoted a substantial proportion of its resources to efforts aimed at achieving national unity. Abdullah Öcalan’s creative approach and extensive efforts, in particular, have always been worthy of recognition.


Indeed, it was Öcalan who carried out all the preparations for the establishment of the Kurdistan National Congress. Had he not been subjected to an international conspiracy, his aim was to organize the national congress under favorable conditions and through effective methods, assume its leadership and ensure that all activities were coordinated at the highest level through this institution. This was also the primary reason he chose to travel to Europe when confronted with a conspiratorial campaign against him.


This leadership project was thwarted by the October 9 and February 15 attacks of the international conspiracy. Although the KNK was subsequently established on the basis of those preparations and has continued its activities for a quarter of a century, its achievements have fallen far short of realizing Öcalan’s vision.


Why, then, has Kurdish national unity not been achieved despite so much discussion and demand, and why has the KNK not been made effective? In fact, this is one of the most important questions facing the Kurds today, perhaps even the most important, and one that must be answered accurately and adequately. The current developments in Southern Kurdistan provide an opportunity to raise this question courageously and seek answers. The discussions conducted in this context are marked by a considerable lack of courage and an overly superficial approach. Moreover, the rhetorical grandstanding of nationalist perspectives prevents these discussions from becoming comprehensive and in-depth.


According to the nationalist perspective, such discussions are essentially unnecessary because the national leadership of the Kurds is embodied by the Barzanî family! From this standpoint, national unity means rallying around the Barzanî family! Furthermore, Kurds are …

title: Families of fallen guerrilla fighters demand access to their graves
content:
Nearly three decades after the deaths of their loved ones, families of fallen Kurdish guerrilla fighters gathered for a two-day commemoration. Organized by MEBYA-DER (Association for Solidarity, Assistance, Unity and Culture of Families Who Lost Relatives in the Cradle of Civilizations), the event honored 19 people who lost their lives in the Kurdish freedom struggle during the 1990s. For many families, it was the first opportunity in years to mourn their children and siblings together. Their most important demand remains unfulfilled: they want to know where the remains of their loved ones are located and to be able to visit their graves.


The families linked their commemoration to the hope of an end to the decades-long war. They emphasized that the ongoing Peace and Democratic Society Process must produce concrete results. They said they did not want other families to suffer the same loss or spend decades living without certainty about the fate of their loved ones.


https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/6a4204e4_20261110234226_2026-11-11-amed-filiz-bayram_mehmet-emin-kilic_seniha-yolay-sehit-aileleri-sehit-anma_1.mp4


“As a mother, this is my only demand”


Seniha Yolay is among the mothers who still do not know where their children are buried. Her son Şahabettin Yolay, who went by the name Siyabend in the guerrilla movement, joined the PKK in 1994 and fell in 1998. She had not seen him since he left home. It was only years later that the family learned of his death, without ever receiving further information about his whereabouts.


“My son left the house saying he was going to school. He never came back. In 1998, we learned that he had lost his life. Since then, we have heard nothing more about him. I kept asking questions, but no one could tell me anything. Today, after 30 years, we held a memorial service for him. I want to know where my son’s grave is. As a mother, this is my only demand,” Yolay said.


Yolay stated that being able to mourn her son alongside other families now held great significance for her. For many years, she added, the families had been left alone with their grief and uncertainty.


“Being able to mourn them, even after all these years, is very important to us. The fighting has continued for decades. This peace process must achieve its goal, and no more bodies should be brought home. We families want peace. We do not want anyone else to suffer or lose their life.”


Yolay emphasized that the families had never forgotten their loved ones, despite the many years that had passed.


“This bloodshed has continued for 50 years. It must stop. From now on, people should no longer have to live in fear of receiving another news of death.”


“We want them to have a grave”


Filiz Bayram also attended the commemoration. Her brother Meki Bayram, known by the name Çiya Dilbirîn, joined the PKK in 1992 and was martyred in 1994. The passing decades have done nothing to diminish the family’s memories of him or their grief.


“My brother is gone. I hope that from now on, no one else will lose their life. The peace process must finally be realized through concrete steps. No one should have to suffer anymore. Enough is enough,” Bayram said.


She noted that the collective memorial service had brought back memories that remained as vivid as ever for the families, despite the passage of time.


“After 33 years, we are mourning here and shedding tears once again. To us, everything feels as though it happened yesterday. No mother, no sister ever forgets their fallen loved ones or those days. We have forgotten neither the suffering we endured nor the people we lost.”


Bayram called for an end to the armed conflict and a peace process that would go beyond political statements.


“The war must finally end, and the sounds of tanks and artillery must fall silent. We have endured everything imaginable over the years. Now, peace must finally come to this country. Genuine peace.”


Above all, however, she said she wanted to have a place where she could commemorate her brother.


“We want them to have graves. And if there are no graves, we at least want to know where their remains are. We want to be able to stand at their graves, even if only once. This is not just our demand, but the demand of every family in the same situation.”


Many families have still been unable to say goodbye

title: Freedom for Abdullah Öcalan vigil in Strasbourg enters its 750th week
content:
The freedom for Abdullah Öcalan vigil, held in Strasbourg, France, since June 25, 2012, has entered its 750th week. Through the protest, which has continued for more than 14 years, participants are demanding the physical freedom of the Kurdish leader who has been incarcerated in İmralı Island Prison since 1999.


During the new week of action, Tori Orak, Kurbet Dağ and Adalet Rojhilat from the Liège region of Belgium have taken over the vigil.


In a joint statement, the activists commemorated the fallen members of the Kurdish freedom movement whose deaths have been announced in recent months. They reaffirmed their remembrance with the slogan “Şehîd namirin” (Martyrs are immortal).


Call for support for the peace process


The activists called on the families of the martyrs and the entire Kurdish population to support the Peace and Democratic Society Process initiated by Abdullah Öcalan. They emphasized that they wanted to see Öcalan free and once again among the people.


The group said they had taken responsibility for the vigil this week as representatives of the Kurdish community in Liège.


“We hope that the entire Kurdish people will embrace this process, organize themselves and prepare for the developments ahead,” the activists said.

title: Nine Kurds, including seven political activists, remain forcibly disappeared in Iran
content:
Nine Kurdish citizens, including seven political activists, remain forcibly disappeared months or years after their arrests by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Intelligence Organisation and the Ministry of Intelligence of the Islamic Republic of Iran.


They are Osman Mameh, Arman Khalegh-Panah, Edris Feqhi, Mohsen Ghaderi, Sara Rashidi Kachalanlou, Zahra Pir-Dehghan, Parvin (Akhtar) Rasegh Ghezelbash, Khaled Barzanji and Sirwan Habibi.


Seven are members of the Kurdistan Free Life Party (PJAK) or the Free Women’s Society of Eastern Kurdistan (KJAR). Their arbitrary arrests took place in Bukan, Saqqez, Baneh, Orumiyeh, Paveh and Kamyaran from August 2021 onwards, without minimum legal safeguards.


The Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) has established that security and judicial authorities verbally informed the families of Ghaderi and Khalegh-Panah that the two men had been killed.


Neither family has received official documentation or a death certificate substantiating the claim, and neither man’s body has been returned.


The other families have also received no clear answers about the fate or whereabouts of their loved ones, despite repeatedly approaching security and judicial authorities. The authorities concerned have denied knowing about the arrests.


All nine have been denied access to independent lawyers of their own choosing and all contact and visits with their families since their arrests.


In light of the evidence and circumstances of each case, KHRN considers the authorities’ refusal to acknowledge the arrests or disclose the individuals’ fate and whereabouts to constitute the crime of enforced disappearance.


These continuing violations affect both the disappeared individuals and their families, who are denied the right to know the truth about what has happened to their loved ones and where they are held.


Given the continuing nature of enforced disappearance and the international obligations of the Islamic Republic of Iran, KHRN calls on the international community to pursue these cases urgently and exert effective, meaningful pressure on the authorities to disclose the disappeared individuals’ fate and whereabouts and ensure accountability.


This appeal is directed particularly to the UN Human Rights Council, the UN Special Rapporteur on the situation of human rights in the Islamic Republic of Iran, the UN Special Rapporteur on torture and other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment, and the UN Working Group on Enforced or Involuntary Disappearances.


KHRN calls for:


– Increased international pressure on the responsible authorities

: Use official communications, public statements and diplomatic and human rights mechanisms to require the authorities of the Islamic Republic of Iran to acknowledge responsibility for the arrests, disclose the disappeared individuals’ fate and end their enforced disappearance.


– Guarantees for the liberty, safety and rights of the disappeared individuals:

Demand an immediate end to secret detention, disclosure of places of detention, access to independent lawyers of the individuals’ own choosing and their families, and judicial and independent oversight.


– Independent and effective investigations:

 Demand prompt, independent, impartial and effective investigations into the arrests, transfers and secret detention, including the roles of IRGC Intelligence Organisation and Ministry of Intelligence forces and contradictory claims that some individuals may have been killed.


– Support for families and their right to the truth:

 Require documented and transparent information about the disappeared individuals’ fate, an end to threats, intimidation and pressure against families, and guarantees of their right to seek the truth and access justice.


– Accountability and an end to impunity:

 Identify and hold accountable everyone who ordered, carried out or bears official responsibility for these continuing enforced disappearances, through investigations and prosecutions consistent with fair-trial standards.

author: Unknown
title: Kurdish political prisoner sentenced to 15 years in prison and fined in Iran
content:
Branch 26 of the Islamic Revolutionary Court in Tehran has sentenced Kurdish political prisoner Ahmad Tamouei to a total of 15 years in prison and a fine of 12.5 billion rials on charges of “assembly and collusion against national security” and “carrying and possessing weapons,” the Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) has reported.


The court issued the sentences in recent months against Tamouei, who is held in Greater Tehran Central Penitentiary.


Under Article 134 of the Islamic Penal Code, which governs sentencing for multiple offences, only the most severe punishment, 10 years’ imprisonment and the fine, will be enforceable.


Tamouei, a political activist from Salmas, had previously spent 14 years in Orumiyeh Central Prison before his release in 2021.


He then moved to Tehran, where he worked as a driver for the ride-hailing service Snapp.


In the early hours of 23 February 2026, Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) forces violently arrested him without a warrant at a checkpoint on Kargar-e Jonoubi Street in Tehran and took him to a security detention facility.


IRGC forces subjected him to severe physical and psychological torture for one day before transferring him to Ward 2A of Evin Prison on 24 February.


Following the outbreak of war, Tamouei and several other detainees were moved from the ward to a secret security detention facility in eastern Tehran. He was transferred to Greater Tehran Central Penitentiary on 4 March.


His case was opened at Branch Three of the Public and Revolutionary Prosecutor’s Office in Tehran’s District 33, and was referred to Branch 26 of the Islamic Revolutionary Court in Tehran after the issuance of an indictment.


Background


Tamouei was previously arrested by IRGC intelligence forces in Mahabad on 24 October 2007 and taken to the IRGC intelligence detention facility in Orumiyeh.


In an open letter written in 2016 to Ahmed Shaheed, then UN Special Rapporteur on the situation of human rights in Iran, Tamouei described being tortured for two months in solitary confinement at the facility following his arrest on charges of “membership of PJAK”.


The methods of torture described in his letter included “electric shocks”, “suspension of the body”, “flogging” and “mock execution”.


In February 2008, Branch One of the Islamic Revolutionary Court in Mahabad sentenced him to 15 years in prison and internal exile to Orumiyeh Central Prison on charges of “enmity against God” (moharebeh).


The sentence was upheld in summer 2008, and he was transferred to Orumiyeh Central Prison to serve it.


During his 14 years and two months in prison, the Ministry of Intelligence’s special office inside the prison repeatedly threatened and interrogated him over his participation in strikes by political prisoners.

author: Joshua Carroll
title: Ex-Met Police Boss Works As Paid Advisor for Palantir
content:
A former head of the Metropolitan police, who was ousted amid scandals over misogyny and racism in the force, is now working as a paid advisor for spytech firm Palantir, the

Bureau of Investigative Journalism has revealed

. 


Cressida Dick resigned as the force’s commissioner in 2022 after London mayor Sadiq Khan publicly said he had lost confidence in her, a move seen as effectively sacking the senior officer. 


In September 2025 she joined Palantir, the Bureau reported on Tuesday, becoming the latest of a number of high-profile public figures taking up work for the firm. 


Former Labour deputy leader Tom Watson

became the firm’s newest senior vice president

 in September this year, while former Conservative defence minister Leo Docherty

joined the firm

 in February 2025.  


Palantir has supplied technology to the Israeli military throughout its genocide in Gaza and has worked with ICE amid its campaign of

abductions and killings

 in the US. 


Palantir told the Bureau that Dick’s role was to advise the firm “on how our software could help improve the delivery of services in the public sector, drawing on more than 40 years of public service in a variety of roles.”


Dick told the outlet: “My role is limited to providing advice on the ways in which products such as theirs may assist public sector services. I do not and have not ever lobbied or advocated for Palantir with any organisation or individual in any sector, nor have I ever introduced Palantir to any contact of mine.”


In 2005, Dick was in charge of the operation during which police shot and killed Jean Charles de Menezes after mistaking him for a suspect in the 7/7 bombings. 


Earlier this week,

the Citizens reported

 that Palantir had won a five-year contract with Bedfordshire, Cambridgeshire and Hertfordshire police forces worth £10m. Palantir also has a £9m contract to oversee the firearms licensing system for all of the UK’s police forces.


“It never ceases to amaze me how willing people are to pay money to Palantir for the shoddy goods that they deliver,” Martin Wrigley, a Liberal Democrat MP, told the Bureau. “They think themselves the best in the world but they are just not that good – and keep on hiring people to bend ears to get them in via the back door.”

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: Six hopefuls in running for Kitikmeot Inuit Association president
content:
Six candidates have put their name forward in the Kitikmeot Inuit Association’s presidential election.


The organization that manages lands in trust for Kitikmeot Inuit will elect its president, a vice-president and three regional board of directors on Dec. 14.


Two other Inuit organizations, Nunavut Tunngavik Inc. and Qikiqtani Inuit Association, will also host their

leadership elections

 the same day.


The KIA presidential nominees are Jeannie Ehaloak, Rosabelle Klengenberg and Lawrence Otokiak from Cambridge Bay; Simon Komangat and Raymond Quqshuun Sr. from Gjoa Haven; and David Audlatak Nivingalok from Kugluktuk, according to a news release from the organization.


Since late June, Nivingalok has served as acting president after KIA announced former president James Eetoolook had to take leave “for personal matters.”


James Aiyout, Abel Aqqaq, David Aqqaq, and Ashoona Iroqiut hope to be elected to the board to represent Taloyoak.


Kugluktuk and Kugaaruk have one person running for their community’s spot on the board of directors: Leah Kadlun put her name forward for the Kugluktuk seat, and Tars Angutingunirk put his name forward to represent Kugaaruk.


The nomination period for KIA’s social and cultural vice-president position has been extended until Friday.


Successful candidates will hold onto their roles until 2030.

author: Jesse Hagopian
title: Paulo Freire’s Revolutionary Approach to Literacy Still Threatens Those in Power
content:
The new documentary Reading the World reveals how teaching literacy in Brazil became a struggle for political power.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

In 1963, Brazilian educator Paulo Freire helped launch a revolutionary literacy campaign in the impoverished northeastern Brazilian town of Angicos, where hundreds of rural workers learned to read and write in just 40 hours of instruction. Freire’s approach was about much more than literacy. Rather than emphasizing memorization and repetition, he developed “Culture Circles” where participants discussed their experiences, examined the conditions shaping their lives, and developed the critical consciousness to challenge oppression.

The experiment helped lay the groundwork for Freire’s groundbreaking book, Pedagogy of the Oppressed, which would become one of the most influential works in the history of education. But the literacy campaign was violently interrupted when a U.S.-backed military coup overthrew Brazilian President João Goulart in 1964. Freire was imprisoned and forced into exile, while students burned or buried their educational materials to escape persecution.

A powerful new documentary Reading the World (Lendo o Mundo) explores this formative period in Freire’s life, before he became an internationally celebrated educational philosopher. Drawing on rare archival footage of 1960s Brazil and the memories of the farmers, students, and educators who participated in the Culture Circles, the film reveals how Freire’s ideas emerged from grassroots struggles for literacy, land, voting rights, and democracy.

The film, which premiered in New York and aired on PBS WORLD Channel this October, arrives at a time when educators in the United States are confronting renewed censorship, book bans, and political attacks on teaching about racism and inequality.

I spoke with Catherine Murphy, co-director of Reading the World, about the revolutionary potential of literacy, the political forces that sought to destroy Freire’s educational experiment, and why his ideas continue to threaten those in power.

The interview that follows has been lightly edited for clarity and length.

Jesse Hagopian: One of my favorite moments in the film is the opening scene, when Paulo Freire tells his audience that he wants to have a dialogue with them rather than give a lecture. He also promises that if he doesn’t know an answer, he won’t lie. It seems like such a simple statement, but it represents a profound departure from traditional teaching. Who was Freire, and what made his approach so revolutionary?

Catherine Murphy: Paulo Freire was a Brazilian educator born in Recife in 1921. He became one of the world’s most celebrated educational philosophers. His most famous book, Pedagogy of the Oppressed, was published while he was in exile.

I also love that opening quote because it lays the groundwork for the entire film. Freire says that ever since he was a child, he understood that not knowing is part of knowing.

That gets to the essence of Freire’s philosophy: Knowledge belongs to all of us. Knowledge is generated by all of us. Education is a reciprocal, collective process. It’s about sharing what we know, and learning from each other. Freire critiqued what he called “the banking model of education” and favored a “dialogic” process based on horizontal dialogue, problem-posing, and really listening to each other.

As Freire became internationally recognized, he was increasingly invited to speak at conferences and educational institutions around the world. But his collaborators repeatedly told me stories about how he didn’t want to simply deliver lectures. He wanted dialogue with people, to listen.

When Freire visited the Highlander Center in 1987 or attended the Chicago Alternative Schools Network Conference in 1977, he wanted to know what people were doing themselves. What were popular educators doing? What were classroom teachers, community educators, and activists doing? What was working? What were they struggling with?

Freire was willing to share his ideas and experiences, but he also wanted to learn from others.

That is a beautiful lesson for all of us, not only in formal educational spaces, but in life.

Before we get into Freire’s literacy campaign, can you describe the conditions in northeastern Brazil in the early 1960s? How did illiteracy help maintain existing relations of economic and political power?

author: Derek Seidman
title: WWII Sparked Anti-Fascist Ideas Among War Workers. What Lessons Can We Learn?
content:
Historian Tejasvi Nagaraja explains how wartime mobilization generated wider organizing around labor, race, and empire.

Historian Tejasvi Nagaraja explains how wartime mobilization generated wider organizing around labor, race, and empire.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

World War II was a period of enormous mobilization in U.S. society that brought together tens of millions of “war workers” — soldiers and laborers in war-essential industries, spanning the globe. While mainstream mythologies persist of the World War II years as a period of “consensus,” Black Americans fought in a Jim Crow military while Japanese Americans were interned by the U.S. government. Moreover, the wartime mobilization generated massive conflict and resistance around labor, race, and empire.

Tejasvi Nagaraja is a historian of labor and racial capitalism at Cornell University, and the author of Troop Movements: Labor, Race, and Global Freedom Struggles in America’s World War II. As he shows in this new book, soldiers and defense workers, stationed across much of the world, waged and linked struggles for labor and civil rights and against colonialism and imperialism throughout the 1940s. Furthermore, many World War II veterans and war workers, drawing on wartime political experiences forged in a period of rising anti-fascist consciousness, went on to lead and provide guidance for major postwar U.S. social movements into the 1960s and beyond.

In this exclusive Truthout interview, published on Veteran’s Day, Nagaraja discusses Troop Movements and what lessons its history might hold for organizers and activists today. This interview has been lightly edited for length and clarity.

Derek Seidman: The military is sometimes imagined as separate from the rest of society, but your book shows how blurred these lines really were during the 1940s. Can you elaborate on this?

Tejasvi Nagaraja: World War II was, at least for the United States, the closest thing to a total war mobilization. Most employment was converted to military service in the armed forces and to working in war-essential industries. Virtually every family and community had members in the military and defense industries.

The story I tell about World War II is about what happened in this realm, where tens of millions of people were in the armed forces and defense industries, and their experiences at home, but also abroad — in Africa, Asia, Europe, and the Caribbean.

Labor during World War II was not just working at a Michigan auto factory or Appalachian coal mine, but also cooking and cleaning on a military base in Texas and Mississippi or France, or building the Ledo Road across China, Burma, and India. These were sites of labor experience and labor struggle.

The 1930s and 1940s were a peak period of union membership growth and strike activity in U.S. history. Wildcat strikes were happening in defense industries during World War II. Service members in the Army, Navy, and Air Force engaged in wildcat strikes, hunger strikes, and mutinies to protest labor conditions.

The 1930s and 1940s were a peak period of union membership growth and strike activity in U.S. history. Wildcat strikes were happening in defense industries during World War II.

Black men and women protested labor, policing, and jailing conditions. They experienced race and class struggles — not just in Georgia, but in Massachusetts, as well as in France, India, and the Philippines. Their struggles linked up to global questions.

There was a real blurring of defense industry and service member labor, and civil rights and worker struggles, at home and abroad. It was a time of global anti-fascist struggle and global decolonial possibility, linking the U.S. working class, in some moments, to working people from other regions.

A huge part of the U.S. working class was tied to the war machine during World War II. How did leftists and anti-imperialists who opposed war and militarism engage with this reality?

The 1940s were a crucible through which the longer struggles of economic, racial, and global politics were transformed. In this context, labor, civil rights, and global justice activists navigated a contradictory and double-edged terrain. They sometimes made a devil’s bargain that we can understand as partly a question of choice and political ideology, but also of not making history as we please and having to navigate things bigger than …

author: infolibre
title: Απελευθέρωση του Μπαρίς Ερχάν – Συλλογή υπογραφών
content:
Σκίτσο: Γιώργος Κωνσταντίνου


Μια κραυγή μέσα από τους τοίχους της φυλακής, η επιστολή του Barış Erhan. Είναι η φωνή ενός ανθρώπου που εγκατέλειψε την Τουρκία αναζητώντας ασφάλεια και ελευθερία, για να βρεθεί στην Ελλάδα αντιμέτωπος με μια πρωτόδικη καταδίκη 74 χρόνων και ενός μήνα για διακίνηση μεταναστών. Θύμα της θανατοπολιτικής του ελληνικού κράτους και της ΕΕ.


Πολιτικός ακτιβιστής, σοσιαλιστής και καλλιτέχνης, ο Barış περιγράφει τη διαδρομή του και τη δράση του, τις διώξεις στην Τουρκία, τις συνθήκες σύλληψης και δίκης στην Ελλάδα, αλλά και την οδυνηρή εμπειρία της φυλάκισης. Καταγγέλλει σοβαρές αδικίες και ζητά να ακουστεί…


Η μαρτυρία του ξεπερνά τα όρια μιας προσωπικής υπόθεσης. Θέτει ένα κρίσιμο ερώτημα για τη δικαιοσύνη, τα δικαιώματα των προσφύγων και τη μεταχείριση όσων κατηγορούνται για διακίνηση ανθρώπων. Πίσω από τους αριθμούς και τις βαριές ποινές υπάρχουν άνθρωποι, ζωές και αξιοπρέπειες που δεν μπορούν να αγνοούνται.


Ο Barış ζητά να μην παραμείνει αόρατος και ξεχασμένος. Η επιστολή του είναι μια έκκληση για αλήθεια, δικαιοσύνη και ελευθερία. Γιατί η αλληλεγγύη δεν σταματά στις πόρτες των φυλακών — και η ανθρώπινη αξιοπρέπεια δεν φυλακίζεται.

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: Meet David Morales: Providence Voters Elect Democratic Socialist Mayor, Approve Israel Divestment
content:
Voters in Providence, Rhode Island, approved a ballot measure last week that could result in the city divesting from Israel. The successful grassroots campaign makes Providence the first U.S. city to pass a binding divestment measure through a popular vote. The measure instructs the city to divest from countries and companies implicated in “ethnic cleansing, apartheid, illegal military occupation, or genocide.” The language does not mention Israel by name. We speak with one of the key backers of the divestment measure, Mayor-elect David Morales, a 28-year-old democratic socialist who made history on election night as the youngest mayor ever elected in Providence.


“What we saw was our neighbors coming out in the thousands to demonstrate that we are ready for change,” Morales says, promising to enact his affordability-focused platform. “It’s the responsibility of local government to take action. And for that reason, we are seeing a rise in democratic socialism and the representation of democratic socialists all across the country.”

author: CMI Argentina
title: A 4 años de la condena, detienen al policía bonaerense Pablo Moresco
content:
El Tribunal en lo Criminal N° 2 de San Nicolás, a cargo del juez Alejandro Gabriel López, ordenó la detención de Pablo Nicolás Moresco, el policía condenado en 2022 por atropellar con el patrullero y matar a Ulises Rial y Ezequiel Corbalán. A pesar de la decisión unánime de los jueces que lo encontraron culpable y lo sentenciaron a 17 años de prisión por homicidio doloso con dolo eventual, la Sala IV del Tribunal de Casación provincial integrada por Mario Kohan y Carlos Natiello cambió arbitrariamente la calificación por la de homicidio culposo y redujo la pena a 5 años de prisión. Moresco quedó en libertad hasta ahora. En ese juicio la CPM actuó como particular damnificado institucional en su función de Mecanismo Local de Prevención de la Tortura de la provincia de Buenos Aires.


Desde el Tribunal en lo Criminal N° 2 de San Nicolás libraron una orden de allanamiento y detuvieron al responsable de atropellar con el patrullero a dos jóvenes en junio del 2020. El policía Pablo Nicolás Moresco fue juzgado en 2022 y condenado a 17 años de prisión por el delito de homicidio con dolo eventual y en concurso real. Teniendo en cuenta que en octubre de este año la sentencia quedó firme por cinco años de prisión de cumplimiento efectivo, las partes que fueron particulares damnificados en el juicio -la Comisión por la Memoria en su calidad de Mecanismo Local de Prevención de la Tortura y el abogado Gabriel Ganon- solicitaron que se efectivice la prisión. El Ministerio Público Fiscal acompañó el pedido de manera tal que el tribunal libró este 4 de noviembre la orden de detención.


Durante la madrugada del 1 de junio de 2020 en el barrio San Jorge de San Nicolás, en el marco del aislamiento social preventivo y obligatorio, Ulises Rial y Ezequiel Corbalán salieron en moto a comprar bebidas y un móvil policial intentó identificarlos. Como no se detuvieron, los policías comenzaron a perseguirlos y dieron el aviso radial para detener la moto. El patrullero conducido por Pablo Nicolás Moresco se sumó al operativo, conducía con la sirena y balizas policiales apagadas por la calle Carbajo en sentido contrario a la moto, y cuando la vio cruzó el patrullero hacia el carril de circulación contraria (a contramano) para forzar su detención. Fue esa maniobra la que derivó en un violento impacto de la moto sobre el lateral del patrullero y que provocó la muerte de Corbalán y Rial.


Como resultado del juicio, la sentencia condenatoria reconoció la total desproporción entre la maniobra policial que provocó la muerte de ambos jóvenes respecto al objetivo de identificarlos en el marco del ASPO. Pero no quedó detenido al terminar el juicio porque el fiscal de juicio no lo solicitó en sus alegatos y los magistrados del TOC 2 de San Nicolás resolvieron que sin pedido del Ministerio Público no podían ordenar su detención.


Luego de que quedara firme el fallo de la Sala IV del Tribunal de Casación provincial que cambió la calificación por homicidio culposo y condenó a 5 años de prisión se dispuso su detención efectiva.


La muerte producida por policías mediante el uso de patrulleros que se utilizan con este fin ha provocado 62 muertes en los últimos 10 años en territorio provincial. Muchos de estos hechos son calificados como homicidios culposos -accidentes de tránsito- y quedan impunes sin juzgarse o sancionarse las responsabilidades policiales.

author: Nehaa Bimal
title: $575M commitment a ‘first step’ in Inuit Child First transition, minister says
content:
The $575-million, five-year commitment to the Inuit Child First Initiative in Budget 2026 is the “first step” in a broader transition, says Indigenous Services Minister Mandy Gull-Masty.


The program, rebranded as Pirutsiagutiit and developed with Inuit Tapiriit Kanatami and the four Inuit treaty organizations, is expected to launch April 1, 2027. Delivery will be transferred from Indigenous Services Canada to the treaty organizations or their designates.


“I’m really proud of the work that was done by ITK and all of the partners in the space for Inuit Child First Initiative,” Gull-Masty said during a news conference at the Inuusirvik Community Wellness Hub in Iqaluit on Saturday.


“We’ve had a lot of feedback. They’ve given us a lot of data. They’ve given us a lot of information. That’s what helped us to be able to bring forth the funding commitment.”


Gull-Masty said further announcements are expected from Northern and Arctic Affairs Minister Rebecca Chartrand and Crown-Indigenous Relations Minister Rebecca Alty.


“This is the first step in what you are going to see. The next step that comes forward is built with the essential input of our partners,” she said. 


ITK said in an email to Nunatsiaq News that it would provide more details in the coming weeks, as well.


Nunavut MP Lori Idlout said the change in program delivery could have significant impacts for Nunavummiut. 


“Inuit leading how the program will be delivered could have creative solutions, like maybe providing more for hunters so that they can provide for their families, for their children, so that children can go to school with having food in their bellies,” Idlout said in an interview with Nunatsiaq News on Saturday.


The federal government launched the Inuit Child First Initiative in September 2018. It provides health, social, educational and other supports to Inuit children and youth.


The program’s funding ran out in 2025 and was extended through one-year commitments while Ottawa and Inuit partners worked on a replacement.


In November 2025, Gull-Masty told Nunatsiaq News the program would be retooled and made permanent but did not provide a timeline for the replacement.


The new funding commitment is $25 million below the $600 million ITK requested in its pre-budget submission.


“The fact that they can find billions of dollars for military spending — in fact, one in five dollars is going towards military spending, much of which is going to happen in Nunavut — but couldn’t even meet by $15 million what was requested, I think is kind of patronizing,” said NDP Indigenous services critic Leah Gazan in an interview with Nunatsiaq News Monday. 


Gazan also criticized changes introduced last February that required funding requests to demonstrate a child’s individual needs and include supporting documentation.


The changes also restricted funding for community-wide programs, including hamlet food voucher programs.


“We will continue to push the government to make sure that this actual transition occurs and it doesn’t fall by the wayside, like we’ve seen in the past,” Gazan said.


—

With files from Daron Letts.

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: "American Scoundrel": From Roy Cohn to Stephen Miller, "McCarthyism Lives On," Says Author Kai Bird
content:
We speak with historian Kai Bird about

American Scoundrel

, a new biography of the notorious political fixer Roy Cohn, who rose to fame as chief counsel to Joe McCarthy during the senator’s anti-communist campaign, served as a lawyer for the New York mob, and was an influential voice in Republican circles until his death from

AIDS

-related complications in 1986. His most impactful relationship, however, would prove to be with a young Donald Trump, whom he mentored in business and politics during the 1970s and ’80s.


Facing political setbacks during his first term as president, Trump reportedly asked, “Where’s my Roy Cohn?” Bird, who co-authored

American Scoundrel

 with his wife Susan Goldmark, says Trump may have found his Cohn in Stephen Miller, the architect of the administration’s mass deportation policies whom Trump just elevated to chief of staff.


“It’s not really a surprise that, cornered and wounded by the recent election results, he reaches out and pulls up Stephen Miller, who’s very similar in his willingness to go on the offensive and never back down, and to say outrageous things to try to change the narrative,” says Bird.

title: El reclamo de Mirtha Baravalle vuelve a poner en cuestión a la Justicia: convocan a Comodoro Py por los bebés apropiados en la dictadura
content:
«O lloro o lucho», sentenció Mirtha Baravalle en un acto del 24 de marzo. | Foto: Osiris Martí.


«Que digan dónde están lxs nietxs». Con esa consigna, este jueves 12 de noviembre, a las 11, familiares y organizaciones de derechos humanos convocan a concentrarse frente a la Cámara Federal de Casación Penal, en Comodoro Py, donde se realizará una audiencia por el hábeas corpus que reclama conocer el destino de Ana María Baravalle, Julio César Galizzi, sus hijos o hijas nacidos en cautiverio y María del Carmen Gualdero, también desaparecida cuando cursaba un embarazo a término. La presentación incluye además un pedido de alcance general para que el Estado busque e identifique a todas las personas que pudieron haber sido apropiadas durante el terrorismo de Estado. La convocatoria recupera la lucha de Mirta Acuña de Baravalle, cofundadora de Madres y Abuelas de Plaza de Mayo, quien buscó durante casi cinco décadas a su hija, su yerno y a su nieto o nieta, a quien imaginaba como Camila o Ernesto. Mirta murió en noviembre de 2024 sin haber podido abrazar a ese nieto o nieta. Ahora, sus familiares continúan el reclamo judicial y exigen análisis genéticos masivos, apertura de archivos y el cese del ocultamiento de las identidades.

Por ANRed.

El reclamo llegó a Casación luego de que la Sala IV de la Cámara Federal de Casación Penal habilitara el recurso presentado por Ricardo Baravalle y Estela Gualdero contra el rechazo del hábeas corpus. Los jueces consideraron que la denegación del recurso anterior había sido errónea y dispusieron que se revisen los planteos. La resolución no implica todavía que el tribunal haya concedido el hábeas corpus ni ordenado las medidas solicitadas: abre una instancia para discutir la decisión que había rechazado inicialmente la acción judicial. El planteo fue presentado en los términos de la Ley 23.098, que contempla el hábeas corpus ante situaciones de desaparición forzada.

. La madre de Ana María fue

Mirta Acuña de Baravalle

,

una de las fundadoras de Madres y Abuelas de Plaza de Mayo

, quien dedicó casi cinco décadas a buscar a su hija, a su yerno y a su nieto o nieta.

Falleció en noviembre de 2024, a los 99 años, sin haber podido encontrarles

permaneció detenida en la Comisaría 11 y en la Sección de Seguridad General de la Policía Federal

Tanto ella como el niño o niña que debió nacer durante su cautiverio continúan desaparecidos

author: Simon Childs
title: Broadcasters Ignored Warning About David Walliams, TV Agent Says
content:
Broadcasters failed to take action on “inappropriate behaviour” by David Walliams years before allegations against him came to light, it has been claimed.


Walliams is facing a police investigation after it was alleged he kissed and groped a 15-year-old in his north London flat when he was 36.


On Tuesday, the comedian and children’s author was accused in a joint investigation by the Guardian and ITV News of using his celebrity to prey on girls. The report was published after a failed attempt by Walliams to block it with an injunction.


Dermot McNamara, a TV agent, told Newsnight that his friend, whose name was not given, was 16 when Walliams invited her to a Britain’s Got Talent screening, after which he invited her and another girl back to his home “where inappropriate behaviour happened”.


The incident had a “profound effect on her mental health and her wellbeing,” he said.


It had been a “struggle” for her to “see him in the media, still getting jobs, still being able to conduct himself in public life.”


McNamara said: “I reported it to authorities and broadcasters.”


Asked if any action was taken, he said, “Not that I’m aware of, no… He was still on TV for many, many years. He was still allowed to, by the sounds of it, be involved with other young women – no.”


Walliams denies any wrongdoing.


The allegations have raised other questions about what was known about Walliams’ behaviour at the time.


TV personality Jonathan Ross released a statement saying he is “as horrified by the revelations about David Walliams and the crimes of Russell Brand as the rest of the nation”, after footage circulated of him making a joke at the 2004 Comedy Awards about Walliams going home with a 15-year-old.


Ross said the joke was “submitted to me by the Comedy Awards scriptwriting team, and I believed that the punchline was a reference to the fact he had publicly dated younger women, exaggerated for comic effect.


“Had I had any reason to suspect that it might be referring to actual events, I would not only have refused to use it, but I would not have felt comfortable continuing a personal or professional relationship with him. I also like to think that I would have acted upon that knowledge.”

author: Unknown
title: Spring named after Martyr Zinar
content:
A spring flowing down the slopes of the Pirîz region in the mountains of Kurdistan not only brings life to its surroundings but also preserves the memory of the friendship between local villagers and guerrilla Zinar. Used by local residents as a source of drinking water and by travellers as a place to rest, the spring became known as “Kanîya Şehîd Zinar” (Martyr Zinar’s Spring) following Zinar’s death as a martyr. He had devoted considerable effort to protecting and maintaining it.


With their natural caves, steep cliffs and cold-water springs, every corner of the mountains of Kurdistan holds its own story. Among the hidden natural wonders high in the mountains, springs play an important role in sustaining the lives of both people and other living creatures.


 


Various species of plants grow around Martyr Zinar’s Spring. As the water nourishes the surrounding vegetation, greenery spreads throughout the valley, turning the area into a resting place for travellers as well. Those crossing the mountain roads stop by the spring to catch their breath and cool off with a bowl of cold water.


Despite the harsh natural conditions and airstrikes in the area, the spring continues to flow, also meeting the water needs of nearby villagers. The cleaning and maintenance of this water source, which holds an important place in local life, is carried out through the collective efforts of those who use it. Villagers clean the spring and maintain its surroundings at regular intervals.


A friendship forged by the spring


One of those who devoted their efforts to protecting the spring was the young guerrilla fighter Zinar. Whenever villagers came to clean the spring, Zinar would help them and take part in building its stone walls. His care for the water source and participation in collective work helped forge a strong friendship between him and the local community.


Believing that a life of freedom could only be achieved through collective labour and struggle, Zinar saw taking part in the maintenance of the spring as an expression of this way of life. Working alongside the villagers, he contributed to protecting a water source that everyone could benefit from.


Villagers gave the spring Zinar's name


After Zinar fell as a martyr, the villagers named the spring after him so that his labour and sacrifice would not be forgotten. In this way, the water source they had worked together to maintain became a place where Zinar’s memory would live on.


Today, villagers continue to collect water from the spring, while travellers still stop there to rest. Nourishing the surrounding plants and bringing life to the valley, the spring also preserves the memory of the shared labour and friendship between Zinar and the villagers.

author: cnt.es
title: La huelga general del 11N transcurre con normalidad generalizada, con incidencias en varios puntos del Estado
content:
Imagen

: 07:30h. Piquete informativo en el Poligono do Tambre (Compostela) | Fuente: CNT


CNT denuncia que, en algunas localidades, los cuerpos policiales están impidiendo a los comités de huelga ejercer su labor de comprobación del cumplimiento de los servicios mínimos, obstaculizando así el legítimo ejercicio de las funciones que corresponden a la representación de las personas trabajadoras durante la huelga.


La huelga general convocada este 11 de noviembre está teniendo un seguimiento e incidencia desigual en los distintos territorios, con una situación de relativa normalidad generalizada, aunque con actuaciones destacadas de los piquetes informativos y algunos incidentes policiales.


Todo esto, después del establecimiento de servicios mínimos abusivos, como ha ocurrido en Madrid, donde el Tribunal Supremo ha anulado los servicios mínimos establecidos por la Comunidad para esta huelga.


En varios puntos, sobre todo en Valencia y Cataluña, se han producido cortes de tráfico en los accesos a la ciudad o a los polígonos industriales, en una acciones conjuntas de los comités de huelga de barrio, sindicatos de vivienda y CNT.


La situación más tensa se ha vivido en Zamora, donde durante el primer piquete en el servicio de autobuses se han producido agresiones policiales, con un compañero detenido y varias personas identificadas. En Madrid, también se ha producido una detención durante las actuaciones de los piquetes.


CNT continuará informando del desarrollo de la jornada y de las incidencias que se produzcan en los distintos territorios.


La entrada

La huelga general del 11N transcurre con normalidad generalizada, con incidencias en varios puntos del Estado

 se publicó primero en

Confederación Nacional del Trabajo

.

author: ROAPE
title: A demand that can be checked
content:
Africa is not poor. Africa is drained. What changed for the generation that filled Nairobi’s streets in 2024 was not courage but the ability to prove it.


I was raised inside a sentence. Before I could find my grandparents’ country on a map, I had been handed a verdict: it was poor. The word arrived with the settled cadence of fact, and it lodged so early that I mistook it for a thing I had discovered rather than a thing I had been given.


What broke the sentence was not a feeling. It was a number. The continent I had been taught to grieve over is not a debtor to the world. It is a creditor. More wealth leaves it each year than arrives. I had accepted that poverty the way one accepts weather. Weather has no author. A transaction has two parties.


A generation is now doing the arithmetic in public, and it has begun to ask who the other party is.


That question travels further than the ledger. It begins as arithmetic: whose wealth leaves, and by what route. It becomes politics the moment enough people can do that arithmetic at once, which is what happened in Nairobi in June 2024. And it arrives, finally, at the governments that have taken up the same grievance and answered it by making the arithmetic impossible to check. Nairobi and Ouagadougou are not two subjects. They are the same demand at two different stages of what happens when it is made.


The lie and the ledger


Across most of the colonized continent, a child was taught a single proposition: Africa is poor, as though penury were a fact of the soil rather than a condition imposed on it. The word arrived early and without cease, in the textbook, the telethon, the appeal letter. Poor Africa. It was the first sentence the world pronounced over its people, and it was a falsehood, an inversion so total that once seen, it cannot be unseen.


One fact undoes it. In 2015, a high-level panel convened jointly by the African Union and the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa, chaired by Thabo Mbeki, reported that

Africa loses on the order of fifty billion United States dollars each year to illicit financial flows

. The money is spirited out through trade misinvoicing, transfer mispricing, and outright theft, most of it effected by multinational corporations. Mbeki stated the arithmetic without embellishment: “The continent is losing an estimated US $50 billion a year through illicit capital outflows. This amount of money is larger in volume than the assistance the continent receives annually.”


The panel’s estimate rested on trade misinvoicing alone, the gap between customs records for the same shipment on each side of a border. A later UNCTAD accounting used a broader methodology, adding capital flight and criminal proceeds to the same trade data. It put the annual loss at

$88.6 billion, 3.7 percent of Africa’s GDP, with a cumulative total of $836 billion between 2000 and 2015

.


The abstraction “illicit financial flows” conceals how ordinary the theft is: not the suitcase of cash but the routine of commercial mispricing. A subsidiary in Lusaka or Kinshasa sells its ore to a related company abroad at a fraction of market value. The profit settles in a low-tax jurisdiction while the producing country records a loss on wealth that was demonstrably its own. Each transaction is individually deniable, papered with defensible transfer prices, so a systematic drain presents itself as a thousand unrelated, lawful-looking transfers. Estimates built on mirrored trade statistics are themselves debated among economists, and the panel’s figure is best read as an order of magnitude rather than a ledger line.


The poverty, then, is real but not native. It is manufactured: the classic paradox of plenty, in which the ground beneath the poorest villages holds the minerals the wealthy world cannot function without, and the wealth flows outward rather than up. Africa is not poor; Africa is drained. The entire moral theatre of the preceding century – the rescue, the aid, the loan – has depended upon the colonized believing the first sentence rather than the second. This is coloniality in its economic register: the extractive periphery maintained long after the flag has changed, its dispossession renamed as assistance.


The paradox of plenty


To speak of a resource curse risks the fatalism the inversion is meant to dispel: the suggestion that mineral wealth simply ruins whatever it touches, a law of nature no one need answer for.

Terry Lynn Karl’s study of oil booms …

author: TGEU
title: A Monitorização de Assassinato Trans de 2026 mostra que a cada 32 horas, uma pessoa trans foi morta.
content:
A Monitorização de Assassinato Trans [Trans Murder Monitoring] (TMM) da TGEU registou 273 pessoas trans e de género diverso assassinadas mundialmente ao longo do ano passado, em média, um homicídio registado a cada 32 horas. Assassinatos foram registados em 35 países, o segundo número mais elevado desde que a monitorização começou, e pela primeira vez na Roménia e no Camarões. No total, a TMM registou até à data mais de 5,500 assassinatos globalmente desde que a recolha de dados começou em 2009.


A TGEU – Trans Europe and Central Asia publica a actualização anual do seu projecto global Monitorização de Assassinato Trans no âmbito da Semana de Consciencialização Trans, que termina com o Dia da Memória Trans (TDoR) a 20 de Novembro.


O projecto da TMM conta apenas com números registados, e o trabalho de monitorização está a tornar-se mais difícil. O número total de assassinatos registados é inferior a 300 apenas pela segunda vez numa década, mas a violência não terminou. O espaço cívico em declínio, a hostilidade contra pessoas trans incentivada pela media e pelo estado, e cortes a financiamento tornam menos provável que um assassinato seja relatado e registado.


Principais Conclusões


273 pessoas trans e de género diverso foram registadas como assassinadas

 entre 1 de Outubro de 2025 e 30 de Setembro de 2026 – um assassinato a cada 32 horas.


35 países diferentes

 registaram um assassinato –

o segundo maior número de sempre

. Apenas em 2024 os números de países com dados foram mais altos (38).


Uma em três vítimas eram trabalhadoris do sexo (32%), que continuam a ser o grupo mais atingido

 de todas as ocupações.


Ecoando os padrões de anos anteriores,

quase todos os assassinatos registados (95%) foram feminicídios

 (vítimas foram mulheres trans ou pessoas transfemininas), e

três quartos (75%) das vítimas eram pessoas Negras ou Marrom trans

.


O perfil etário das vítimas de assassinato parece estar a mudar para uma

idade ligeiramente  mais avançada

. Mais de um terço (35%) tinham idades compreendidas entre os

31-40

 anos em 2026, enquanto uma em cinco (21%) das vítimas tinham idades entre os

19-25

 – o que era, consistentemente o maior grupo etário na primeira década da TMM. Uma em vinte (5%) das vítimas do ano anterior foram

menores de 18 anos de idade

.


Sete em cada dez (69%) dos assassinatos ocorreram na América Latina e nas Caraíbas

. O Brasil lidera na lista mais uma vez, representando um em três (32%) do total mundial. Números continuam a cair no

México

, com o número mais baixo de assassinatos registados (29) desde 2011.


No entanto, 2026 viu o mais alto total de sempre na

Argentina

 (16) e o segundo maior no

Equador

 (16) desde que o TMM começou.


O número de assassinatos registados na

Ásia

 (32) caiu desde o mais alto de sempre do ano passado (51). O total deste ano é

muito provavelmente uma subcontagem

 – alguns parceiros na Ásia relataram não terem capacidade para fornecer dados este ano, citando falta de recursos e até mesmo de eletricidade.


13 assassinatos foram registados na Europa,

o total mais elevado desde 2023

 – tantos como 2024 e 2025 combinados. A

maioria das vítimas eram migrantes internacionais

.


Um em dez assassinatos foram registados nos

Estados Unidos

 (29), um valor semelhante a 2025 (31).


Dois em cinco (40%) dos assassinatos registados foram

a tiro

, enquanto que um quarto (24%) foram

por esfaqueamento

. Três em dez (30%) dos assassinatos ocorreram na

rua

, e um quarto (25%) ocorreram

na casa

 da própria vítima.


Dos autores dos crimes de que se tem conhecimento, um em cada quatro (25%) era um ex ou actual parceiro, namorado ou marido. Outros autores comuns dos crimes registados eram grupos/gangues organizados de ódio (15%), estranhos (14%), polícia/militares/exército (12%) e clientes de trabalhadoras do sexo (8%).


Apenas um  agressor foi preso

 em cinco assassinatos (21%) onde autoridades locais documentaram uma resposta.


Violência Interseccional


Ano após ano, o mesmo perfil demográfico de pessoas trans são assassinadas. Quase todas as vítimas registadas (95%) foram mulheres trans e pessoas transfemininas. Trabalhadoras do sexo, que fazem uma em cada três vítimas, permanecem o grupo mais atingido de todas as ocupações, e três em quatro vítimas eram pessoas Negras ou Marrom de experiência trans.


Isto é como a opressão de intersecção se parece na prática. Misoginia, transfobia, racismo, xenófobia e putofobia se reforçam …

author: TGEU
title: El Trans Murder Monitoring 2026 muestra que cada 32 horas, una persona trans fue asesinada
content:
El Monitoreo de Asesinatos de Personas Trans de TGEU (TMM por sus siglas en inglés) ha registrado 273 personas trans y de diversidad de género asesinadas en todo el mundo durante el último año, en promedio, un asesinato informado cada 32 horas. Se reportaron asesinatos en 35 países, el segundo número más alto desde que comenzó el monitoreo, y por primera vez en Rumania y Camerún. En total, el TMM ha registrado ahora más de 5,500 asesinatos en todo el mundo desde que comenzó la recopilación de datos en 2009.


TGEU – Trans Europa y Asia Central publica la actualización anual de su proyecto global de Monitoreo de Asesinatos de Personas Trans en la antesala de la Semana de Conciencia Trans, que culmina con el Día de la Remembranza Trans (TDoR por sus siglas en inglés) el 20 de noviembre.


El proyecto TMM solo cuenta los asesinatos reportados, y el trabajo de monitoreo se está volviendo más difícil. El número total de asesinatos reportados está por debajo de 300 por segunda vez en una década, pero la violencia no ha disminuido. El espacio cívico se está reduciendo, hay hostilidad hacia las personas trans desde los medios y el Estado, y los recortes de financiamiento hacen menos probable que un asesinato sea reportado y registrado. 


Conclusiones clave


Se informó que 273 personas trans y de género diverso fueron asesinadas

 entre el 1 de octubre de 2025 y el 30 de septiembre de 2026

, lo que equivale a un asesinato cada 32 horas.


35 países diferentes

 reportaron un asesinato,

el segundo número más alto hasta ahora.

 Solo en 2024 fue mayor el número de países que reportaron (38).


Una de cada tres víctimas eran trabajadoras sexuales (32%), que siguen siendo el grupo más atacado

 de todas las ocupaciones conocidas.


Siguiendo los patrones de años anteriores,

casi todos los asesinatos reportados (95%) fueron feminicidios

 (las víctimas eran mujeres trans o personas transfemeninas),

y tres cuartas partes (75%) de las víctimas eran personas trans negras o morenas.


El perfil de edad de las víctimas de homicidio parece estar cambiando hacia

edades un poco mayores.

 Más de un tercio (35%) tenía entre

31 y 40

 años en 2026, mientras que uno de cada cinco (21%) tenían entre

19 y 25

 años, siendo consistentemente el grupo de edad más grande en la primera década de TMM. Uno de cada veinte (5%) de las víctimas del último año eran

menores de 18 años.


Siete de cada diez (69%) asesinatos ocurrieron en América Latina y el Caribe.

 Brasil vuelve a liderar la lista, representando uno de cada tres (32%) del total mundial. Los números siguieron bajando en

México

, con los asesinatos más bajos reportados (29) desde 2011. Sin embargo, 2026 registró el total más alto de la historia en

Argentina

 (16) y el segundo total más alto en

Ecuador

 (16) desde que comenzó la TMM.


El número de asesinatos reportados en

Asia

 (32) cayó después del récord histórico del año pasado (51). Es probable que el total de este año esté subestimado: algunos socios de monitoreo en Asia informaron no tener capacidad para proporcionar datos este año, citando

falta de recursos

 e incluso de electricidad.


Se reportaron 13 asesinatos en Europa,

el total más alto desde 2023

, tantos como en 2024 y 2025 juntos.

La mayoría de las víctimas eran migrantes internacionales.


Uno de cada diez casos se registró en

Estados Unidos

 (29), un nivel similar al de 2025 (31).


Dos de cada cinco (40%) de los

asesinatos

 reportados fueron tiroteos, mientras que una cuarta parte (24%) fueron

apuñalamientos

. Tres de cada diez (30%) de los asesinatos ocurrieron en la calle, y una cuarta parte (25%) ocurrieron en el propio

hogar

 de la víctima.


De los perpetradores conocidos, uno de cada cuatro (25%) era una pareja, amante o cónyuge actual o anterior. Otros perpetradores comúnmente reportados fueron grupos/ pandillas de odio organizadas (15%), desconocidos (14%), policía/militares/ejército (12%) y clientes de trabajo sexual (8%).


Se arrestó a un agresor

 en solo uno de cada cinco casos (21%) donde las autoridades locales registraron una respuesta.
