author: Stelinsky
title: Η γαλλική νεολαία στους δρόμους ενάντια σε ένα ζοφερό μέλλον
content:
Το παρακάτω κείμενο προέκυψε κατόπιν μετάφρασης και διαλογής αποσπασμάτων από το “French Youth Take the Streets against a Bleak Future”, 6 Οκτωβρίου 2026, CrimethInc. Διαθέσιμο στο: https://crimethinc.com/2026/10/06/french-youth-fight-against-a-bleak-future.

Την περασμένη εβδομάδα, χιλιάδες έφηβοι κατέβηκαν στους δρόμους της Γαλλίας, συγκρουόμενοι με την αστυνομία, καθώς διαδήλωναν ενάντια στις άθλιες συνθήκες που επικρατούν στα λύκειά τους, αλλά και απέναντι σε ένα μέλλον που μοιάζει να καταρρέει με ταχύτατους ρυθμούς. […] Πρόκειται για ένα ενθαρρυντικό σημάδι, καθώς μετατοπίζει την προσοχή από τη φαινομενικά ασταμάτητη άνοδο της ακροδεξιάς προς το ερώτημα του τι μπορούν να κάνουν οι άνθρωποι από τα κάτω για να υπερασπιστούν τον εαυτό τους. Μέσα σε μια περίοδο κατά την οποία ενισχύεται ολοένα περισσότερο η δημοτικότητα του ακροδεξιού Εθνικού Συναγερμού, έχει ιδιαίτερη σημασία το γεγονός ότι έφηβοι αρχίζουν να οργανώνονται σε επίπεδο βάσης. […] Η οργάνωση αυτή πήρε νέα δυναμική την περασμένη εβδομάδα, όταν αποκλεισμοί λυκείων, διαδηλώσεις και ταραχές ξέσπασαν σε ολόκληρη τη Γαλλία, αιφνιδιάζοντας τους πάντες. Τοιχογραφία που απεικονίζει στιγμιότυπο στο Saint-Ouen-l’Aumone. 14χρονος χτυπήθηκε στο πρόσωπο από αστυνομικό που χρησιμοποιούσε εκτοξευτή χειροβομβιδών, προκαλώντας του διπλό κάταγμα στη γνάθο και σπασμένα δόντια. Όλος ο κόσμος μισεί την αστυνομία. Άδεια για να σκοτώνουν; Από την πρώτη εκλογή του Εμάνουελ Μακρόν στην προεδρία, τον Μάιο του 2017, ο πολιτικός λόγος στη Γαλλία διακατέχεται όλο περισσότερο από αυταρχικές και ακροδεξιές αντιλήψεις, ιδιαίτερα για ζητήματα ασφάλειας, μετανάστευσης, αλλά και οικονομικών και κοινωνικών πολιτικών.[…] Αυτή η μετατόπιση προς μια ακόμη πιο επιθετική μορφή διακυβέρνησης έχει συνοδευτεί από αυξανόμενη κρατική βία απέναντι στα κοινωνικά κινήματα και τις εξεγέρσεις που έχουν ξεσπάσει τα τελευταία χρόνια. […] Μια «βουτιά σε έναν κόσμο επιτήρησης, καταστολής και απώλειας ατομικών ελευθεριών», που έχει πλέον μετατραπεί στη «νέα κανονικότητα». […] Στο ίδιο πλαίσιο εντάσσουν και την προτεινόμενη αλλαγή της νομοθεσίας για τη χρήση πυροβόλων όπλων από την αστυνομία και τη χωροφυλακή. Εφόσον ψηφιστεί, υποστηρίζουν, θα μπορούσε να δημιουργήσει ένα επικίνδυνο προηγούμενο, καθώς θα καθιέρωνε «ένα τεκμήριο “νόμιμης χρήσης όπλων” από αστυνομικούς και χωροφύλακες “κατά την άσκηση των καθηκόντων τους”». Ο νέος νόμος αποτελεί ένα νομοθετικό εργαλείο που επιτρέπει στις δυνάμεις επιβολής του νόμου και, κατ’ επέκταση, στο κράτος, να συγκαλύπτουν μελλοντικές δολοφονίες*. …Αυξανόμενη απογοήτευση Τα αιτήματα των μαθητών αφορούν, μεταξύ άλλων, τη μείωση του αριθμού των μαθητών ανά τάξη, τη μείωση των εβδομαδιαίων διδακτικών ωρών και τη βελτίωση των υποδομών των λυκείων. Ζητούν επίσης το τέλος του Parcoursup, της ηλεκτρονικής πλατφόρμας μέσω της οποίας οι μαθητές δηλώνουν τις επιλογές τους για σπουδές. Η πλατφόρμα έχει δεχθεί κριτική για την αδιαφάνεια των κριτηρίων επιλογής, και για τον ανταγωνισμό και την πίεση που δημιουργεί μεταξύ των μαθητών. Ένα ακόμη αίτημα αφορά την πρόσληψη περισσότερων αναπληρωτών εκπαιδευτικών, ώστε να διασφαλίζεται η συνέχεια της διδασκαλίας όταν απουσιάζουν οι μόνιμοι καθηγητές. Όλο και περισσότερο, τα δημόσια σχολεία διοικούνται σαν ιδιωτικές επιχειρήσεις, και αναγκάζονται να ανταγωνίζονται μεταξύ τους για να είναι πιο αποτελεσματικά. Στον καπιταλισμό, το εκπαιδευτικό σύστημα αποτελεί εργαλείο του κράτους για να μας εξαναγκάζει, να συνθλίβει την ατομικότητά μας, να υποτάσσει το επαναστατικό μας πνεύμα και τις επιθυμίες μας, προκειμένου να μας μετατρέψει σε πειθήνιο εργατικό δυναμικό που μπορεί να εκμεταλλεύεται για το υπόλοιπο της ζωής.[…] Παρανάλωμα του Πυρός Μέχρι τη Δευτέρα 28 Σεπτεμβρίου, η είδηση είχε πλέον διαδοθεί μεταξύ των μαθητών και άρχισαν να συντονίζουν δράσεις σε μεγαλύτερη κλίμακα. Οι εικόνες που διαδίδονταν στα μέσα κοινωνικής δικτύωσης πιθανότατα βοήθησαν στη διάδοση της είδησης, δημιουργώντας ένα φαινόμενο ντόμινο μεταξύ των εφήβων: «Κοίτα τι κάνει το άλλο λύκειο. Ας το κάνουμε κι εμείς!» […] Αυτή η πρώτη ημέρα δράσης έθεσε τον τόνο για την υπόλοιπη εβδομάδα, καθώς το κίνημα εξαπλώθηκε πέρα από το Παρίσι και τα προάστιά του. Χωρίς δισταγμό, ο Λοράν Νουνιέζ, ο σημερινός υπουργός Εσωτερικών και πρώην αρχηγός της Αστυνομίας του Παρισιού από το 2022 έως το 2025, αποφάσισε να καταστείλει το αναδυόμενο κίνημα μέσω ωμής βίας. Αστυνομικές δυνάμεις στάλθηκαν στα λύκεια για να διαλύσουν τους αποκλεισμούς και να διασκορπίσουν τα πλήθη των εφήβων. Οι συγκρούσεις …

author: Qassam Muaddi
title: What Will a New Israeli Government Actually Mean for Palestinians?
content:
The Arab vote made it possible to oust Netanyahu for the first time in nearly two decades.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Israel might be coming closer to resolving its political impasse following last month’s elections, as Israeli President Yitzhak Herzog officially tasked Gadi Eisenkot, the main rival of Benjamin Netanyahu, with forming a government.

Netanyahu, who ran with the hopes of staying in power, lost seven of the 54 seats won by the camp under his leadership. On Thursday, the Ashkenazi Haredi ultra-Orthodox party, Yehodot HaTorah, announced that it would no longer support Netanyahu, effectively reducing his camp to 46 seats in the Knesset, Israel’s parliament. Yehodot HaTorah decided not to nominate any candidate for prime minister during the consultations that the Israeli president concluded on Thursday with different parties, before deciding to tap Eisenkot to form a government. The Haredi party’s decision came as a response to Netanyahu not delivering on his promise to the Haredi community to put their exemption from the military draft into law.

On the other hand, Arab-Palestinian parties allied in the Joint List have stated that they will nominate Gadi Eisenkot, thereby contributing to the majority needed to form a government, provided that Eisenkot’s other allies, especially Avigdor Liberman, who refuses to ally with Arab parties, maintain their support.

Netanyahu might be in his final days as head of the Israeli government, after 18 years and six governments in office. He might also be facing an investigation by a commission over the security failure on October 7, and charges in Israeli courts for his ongoing corruption cases. However, although significant for Israeli politics, how much difference would such a change mean for the Palestinian people, and for the region?

The scene could have looked very different, as it did after the 2015 and 2022 elections, with Netanyahu easily achieving a majority and staying in power. The difference, this time, is the massive turnout of Palestinian citizens of Israel, descendants of the minority who weren’t expelled in 1948, who represent around 2 million people today, and a fifth of Israel’s population. Two weeks ago, for the first time in Israel’s history, their 80% turnout gave the two main Arab lists 19 seats in the Knesset, blocking both Netanyahu and Eisenkot from reaching the 61-seat majority required to form a government.

This development didn’t come in a vacuum. In the past three years, the world witnessed an unrestrained display of what has been Israel’s policy towards the Palestinian people since 1948. But what Palestinians witnessed was even more crude. In Gaza, Palestinians lived the genocide in their own flesh. Outside of Gaza, Palestinians were forced to watch what the Israeli war machine did to their own people in Gaza, with threats of unprecedented repression if they spoke out. In other words, they were forced to normalize these new levels of brutality and accept them as the new norm. For Palestinian citizens of Israel, this was particularly consequential. In the years before October 2023, Palestinian mobilization within Israel was on the rise, with citizens protesting home demolitions, the expulsion of Bedouin communities in the Negev, the state’s indifference towards organized crime in Arab communities, the events of Sheik Jarrah and Jerusalem, and also in Gaza. That mobilization was forced into silence.

The past three years also saw a very aggressive and explicit affirmation of the most anti-Arab racist tendencies. This included resolutions voted on in the Knesset, such as the resolution rejecting any Palestinian statehood west of the Jordan River, passed in July 2024, and the rhetoric of politicians and the media calling for the expulsion and extermination of Gaza, or calling for the “transfer” of Arabs in Israel by ministers like Bezalel Smotrich. The Palestinian community needed some kind of response to remind Israel that they are present and part of the country. This is, in part, what their massive turnout in the recent Israeli elections was about.

But it was also more than just making a point or sending a message. After all, the Palestinian vote put its weight behind the immediate project of ousting Netanyahu, which could only come through a government headed by Gadi Eisenkot, which makes it imperative to ask: what …

title: Bakan Bak’tan kredi ve burslara ilişkin açıklama: “Sıkıntı yok, halledeceğiz”
content:
AKP Samsun Milletvekili Mehmet Muş başkanlığında toplanan TBMM Plan ve Bütçe Komisyonu'nda Gençlik ve Spor Bakanlığı ile bağlı kuruluşlarının 2027 yılı bütçesi, 2025 yılı kesin hesabı ve Sayıştay raporlarının görüşmeleri tamamlandı. Gençlik ve Spor Bakanı Osman Aşkın Bak, milletvekillerinin değerlendirmelerinin ardından soruları yanıtladı.

Bak, eski milli sporcuların futbol müsabakalarını ücretsiz izleyebilmesine yönelik talebine ilişkin, mevcut yönetmelikte bu konuda düzenleme bulunduğunu, ancak güncelleme yapacaklarını belirtti. Stadyumların kulüpler tarafından işletilmesi nedeniyle uygulamada bazı sorunlar yaşandığını ifade eden Bak, ilgili kulüplerle görüşerek talebi sisteme yerleştirmeyi planladıklarını söyledi.

KYK yurtlarının kapasitesine ilişkin eleştirilere yanıt veren Bak, yurt kapasitesini 1 milyona çıkardıklarını belirtti. Yurt yatırımlarının sürdüğünü ifade eden Bak, 2026 yılı sonuna kadar yapım ve kiralama yoluyla 29 yurdun tamamlanacağını, bunların toplam kapasitesinin 31 bin olacağını söyledi.

İnşaatı devam eden 21 yurdun 25 bin kişilik kapasite sağlayacağını belirten Bak, ihale aşamasında da yaklaşık 32 yurt bulunduğunu ve bunların tamamlanmasıyla 34 bin kişilik kapasite daha oluşturulacağını kaydetti.

Yurt başvurularının yüzde 96'sının karşılandığını ifade eden Bak, öğrencilerin aylık bin 300 ila bin 450 lira arasında değişen ücretlerle barındığını, sabah kahvaltısı ve akşam yemeğinin ücretsiz verildiğini söyledi. Yurtlardaki denetimlere ilişkin de bilgi veren Bak, mutfaklara kamera yerleştirildiğini, öğrencilerin denetim süreçlerine ve öğrenci temsilcilikleri aracılığıyla yönetime dahil edildiğini belirtti.

Adana Sarıçam'da bin kişilik, Ankara Beştepe'de 2 bin 500 kişilik yurt inşaatlarının sürdüğünü aktaran Bak, Antalya Konyaaltı'nda 2 bin 667 kişilik yurdun yüzde 82 seviyesine ulaştığını, Finike'de de yurt inşaatlarının devam ettiğini söyledi. Tekirdağ'da yeni yurt yatırımı bulunduğunu, Çorlu, Ergene, Malkara ve diğer ilçelerde gençlik merkezlerinin hizmet verdiğini de sözlerine ekledi.

Öğrenci burs ve kredilerine ilişkin değerlendirmelerde de bulunan Bak, 4 bin lira olan burs miktarının 2026-2027 döneminde artırılacağını söyledi. Yaklaşık 650 bin öğrenciye karşılıksız burs verildiğini, 800-850 bin öğrenciye ise kredi sağlandığını belirten Bak, 2022 yılında yaklaşık 22 milyar liralık öğrenci kredi borcunun silindiğini hatırlattı.

Kredi geri ödemelerinin öğrencinin eğitimini tamamlamasının ardından başladığını, mezuniyet sonrasında işe girene kadar iki yıl boyunca ödeme talep edilmediğini ifade eden Bak, tahsilat işlemlerinin Hazine ve Maliye Bakanlığı tarafından yürütüldüğünü söyledi.

Bak, "Sıkıntı yok. Bütçe yapıyoruz. Merak etmeyin. Bütçe içerisinde kaydırma yaparak halledeceğiz" ifadesini kullandı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Unknown
title: Evrensel'in HABAŞ gerçeğini katliamdan önce ortaya koyan haberleri TBMM gündeminde
content:
İzmir'in Aliağa ilçesindeki HABAŞ Demir Çelik Fabrikası'nda meydana gelen patlamada 18 işçinin yaşamını yitirmesi üzerine TBMM'de Yeni Yol, CHP, DEM Parti ve Yeni Parti gruplarının verdiği Meclis araştırma önergeleri, AKP ve MHP'nin oylarıyla reddedilirken milletvekilleri konuşmalarında sık sık Evrensel'in HABAŞ haberlerine atıf yaptı. Bazı milletvekilleri Evrensel'in İzmir bürosunun HABAŞ patronu hakkında attığı manşetin ardından kurşunlandığını hatırlattı, bazı milletvekilleri ise Çalışma Bakanlığının "gerekli denetimler yapıldı" açıklamasına Evrensel haberlerinde yer alan bilgilerle tepki gösterdi ve aslında şirketin kendi kendini ihbar ettiğini ortaya koyan "HABAŞ patronu katliamın geleceğini biliyordu" haberimizdeki bilgileri aktardı.

Konuşmasında Türkiye'nin dört bir yanında işçilerin yaşadığı sorunlara değinen DEM Parti İstanbul Milletvekili Cengiz Çiçek, "Bu ülkeyi patronlar kulübü yönetiyor. Evrensel gazetesi, ilgili şirketle ilgili manşet yaptığında gazete kurşunlandı" dedi.

Yeni Parti Ankara Milletvekili Gamze Taşcıer ise Çalışma Bakanı'nın HABAŞ'taki denetimlerde ciddi bir sorun bulunmadığı yönündeki açıklamasına karşın Evrensel'in daha önce yayımladığı haberleri gündeme getirerek "Oysa daha bir buçuk yıl önce Evrensel gazetesi bu fabrikayla ilgili haberleri manşete taşımıştı ve çok uzağa gitmeye gerek yok, şirketin kendi raporunda bile kendini ihbar ettiği çok açık bir şekilde gözüküyor ancak ciddiye alan bir Bakanlık yok" dedi.

Taşcıer, şirketin verilerine dayanarak ağır iş kazalarının bir yılda yüzde 56, taşeron işçilerin geçirdiği kazaların yüzde 120 arttığını söyledi. İş güvenliği eğitiminin 66 bin saatten 9 bin saate düştüğünü ve şirket raporunda haftalık çalışma süresinin 61 saat olarak yer aldığını belirterek “Çalışma Bakanlığı neyi denetledi?” diye sordu.

DEM Parti İstanbul Milletvekili Kezban Konukçu da HABAŞ’ın kayıp günlü iş kazası sayısının 2024’te 109’dan 2025’te 146’ya çıktığını belirterek Bakanlığın denetimlerini eleştirdi. Konukçu, "HABAŞ patronu Mehmet Rüştü Başaran 2025’te işçilerin ücretlerini yüzde 33 düşürerek 4,7 milyar lira kazanç sağlamıştı. Bunu haber yaptığı için Evrensel gazetesi silahlı saldırıya maruz kalmıştı yani organize suç örgütü olarak çalışan bir kuvvet görüyoruz karşımızda; iktidarından patronuna, yargısına kadar ve yer altı örgütüne kadar işçiler ölsün, patronlar kâr etsin diye çalışıyorsunuz" ifadelerini kullandı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Chris Walker
title: Trump Attacks Massie After Lawmaker Files Impeachment Articles Against Hegseth
content:
The president falsely claimed that Hegseth is “the most popular” military official in the country.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

President Donald Trump made a surprise appearance at a White House press briefing on Monday, attacking Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Kentucky) following the lawmaker’s submission of articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

Massie is “a sick, sick guy. There’s something wrong with him, actually,” Trump said during the presser. “Now he’s after Pete Hegseth. He doesn’t like Hegseth, but really, what has Hegseth done?”

“He shouldn’t be taking up the time of Congress, or the Senate or anything that he’s doing. The guy’s a stone-cold loser,” Trump added.

The president told the press that he didn’t watch Massie’s announcement of the impeachment articles. He also didn’t respond to any of the charges the lawmaker is leveling against Hegseth, instead focusing on belittling Massie’s character.

Earlier in the day, Massie filed eight articles of impeachment against Hegseth, which included accusations that the defense secretary engaged in unlawful war or military actions, ignored statutes designed to minimize civilian casualties, and suppressed the free speech rights of members of Congress.

“Secretary Hegseth knowingly executed and implemented unlawful orders to initiate war against a foreign nation,” Massie’s impeachment articles stated, adding that Hegseth “has demonstrated that he will remain a threat to civilians, the lawful conduct of United States military operations, the integrity and credibility of the United States Armed Forces, and the Constitution if allowed to remain in office.”

Trump continued his attacks against Massie on Truth Social on Monday night.

“Defeated Republican Congressman Thomas Massie, a total loser, is trying to Impeach perhaps the most popular and successful military official in the Country, Secretary of War, Pete Hegseth,” Trump wrote.

“Pete Hegseth should be praised, not Impeached,” the president added.

On Tuesday morning, following a press conference in which Hegseth attempted to defend himself against Massie’s impeachment efforts, Trump again attacked Massie.

“Pete Hegseth gets an ‘A’ PLUS, PLUS, PLUS for his defense against a disgruntled, angry, defeated, former Congressman, Thomas Massie, a TOTAL LOSER!” Trump wrote.

Despite Trump’s characterization of Hegseth as “popular,” several polls indicate that the American public is upset with him and wants him out of his position of power.

According to an Economist/YouGov poll conducted in September, 51 percent of Americans support impeaching Hegseth for “starting a war with Iran without authorization from Congress,” while only 34 percent are opposed to the idea. A Quinnipiac University survey from that same month found that only 34 percent of Americans give Hegseth a positive job approval rating, while 57 percent disapprove.

That same poll found that, unlike Trump, most Americans are not confident in Hegseth’s ability to lead the U.S. military, with 56 percent expressing that view and only 39 percent saying they have confidence in him.

author: Unknown
title: Giresun’da “temizlik personeli ameliyatlara girdi” iddiasına adli ve idari soruşturma
content:
Giresun İl Sağlık Müdürlüğü, kentte özel bir hastanede temizlik personelinin ameliyatlara girdiği yönünde basına ve sosyal medyaya yansıyan iddialar üzerine adli ve idari soruşturma başlatıldığını bildirdi. Müdürlük, Sağlık Bakanlığının iddiaların araştırılması için müfettiş görevlendirdiğini duyurdu.

Zafer Partisi Giresun İl Başkanı Mesut Aydın, Özel Giresun Ada Hastanesi’nde temizlik görevlisi veya yardımcı personel olarak çalıştığını öne sürdüğü S.T.’nin, tıbbi eğitim ve yetkisi bulunmadan ameliyatlara katılarak hastalara cerrahi müdahalede bulunduğu iddiasıyla Cumhurbaşkanlığı İletişim Merkezine (CİMER) başvurmuştu. Aydın, fotoğraf ve video kayıtlarına dayandırdığı başvurusunda ameliyat kayıtlarının ve geçmiş operasyonların incelenmesini istemişti.

Giresun İl Sağlık Müdürlüğü, iddialara ilişkin yayımladığı açıklamada şu ifadelere yer verdi:

“Bazı basın yayın organları ve sosyal medyada yer alan; Giresun’da özel bir hastanede bir temizlik personelinin ameliyatlara girdiği yönündeki iddialar üzerine, adli ve idari soruşturma başlatılmış olup Bakanlığımızca konuyla ilgili müfettiş görevlendirilmiştir. Kamuoyunun bilgisine saygıyla duyurulur.”

Hastanenin Başhekimi Dr. Cenap Damcı, daha önce yaptığı açıklamada iddiaları reddetmiş, söz konusu kişinin ameliyathanede yardımcı personel olarak görev yaptığını belirtmişti. Hastanede görev yapan Genel Cerrahi Uzmanı Op. Dr. Korhan Arslan da kamuoyuyla paylaşılan görüntülerdeki ameliyatları kendisinin gerçekleştirdiğini açıklamıştı.

author: Dominique Gené - Local Journalism Initiative Reporter
title: Kuujjuaq festival organizer hopes to spark conversation about Inuit identity
content:
For organizer Saali Kuata, the Path to 100 Festival offers an opportunity to move beyond commemorating the James Bay and Northern Quebec Agreement. It allows for Inuit to examine how it has shaped their communities.


Art can start that conversation.


“Art is just another language that we can use that can transcend language,” said Kuata, Avataq Cultural Institute program director, in an interview.


The Path to 100 festival celebrates the 50th anniversary of the JBNQA and takes place at the Katittavik Theatre in Kuujjuaq from Sunday to Wednesday. It features an art exhibition, performances and workshops, as well as discussions about cultural identity, futurism and economic development.


The governments of Quebec and Canada, as well as representatives for Nunavik Inuit and Crees of Eeyou Istchee, signed the the JBNQA on Nov. 11, 1975. It led to

the creation

 of a school board, a regional government and health-care system in Nunavik.


The festival’s name, Path to 100, reflects a long-term vision for Inuit.


That means Inuit having greater control over the decisions that affect their communities while protecting their cultural identity and rights.


“If we want a sustainable future, we have to put our feet down and determine for ourselves, as we have done before, that nothing goes without us,” he said.


Kuata said he worries that as more Inuit adopt English and participate in the western education system and economy, they risk losing touch with what makes their culture unique.


“We find ourselves attaching our identity and our language to the common culture,” he said.


Besides throat singing, drawing, carving and printmaking workshops, the festival also had performances.


Singer Niivi Snowball, child of musician Etua Snowball, performed on Monday night and dedicated the song

No Pride in Genocide

 to Etua, who was in the audience.


“My writing style is so heavily influenced by him,” Snowball told the audience. “The way he writes music, this heavy-hitting, unapologetically political way of writing his songs influenced me without me even realizing.”


Before performing the song, which addresses suicide and the impacts of colonization, Niivi Snowball urged Inuit to reject the idea that death is their only way out.


“I want you to know that this is not our fault,” Snowball said. “The government, colonization wants us to think that the only way out is to die. But we are strong, and we can fight against it.”

title: Başsavcılıktan Kaşif Kozinoğlu'nun adli tıp raporuna itiraz
content:
Silivri Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı, 2011 yılında tutuklu bulunduğu Silivri Cezaevi’nde yaşamını yitiren eski Milli İstihbarat Teşkilatı (MİT) Dış Operasyonlar Daire Başkanı Kaşif Kozinoğlu’nun ölümüne ilişkin Adli Tıp Kurumu 1. İhtisas Kurulu tarafından hazırlanan rapora itiraz etti.

Başsavcılık, rapordaki tespitlerin ayrıntılı biçimde değerlendirilmesi amacıyla Adli Tıp Genel Kurulundan yeni rapor hazırlanmasını talep etti. Adli Tıp Kurumunun 3 Kasım 2026 tarihli raporunda, Kozinoğlu’nun kalp hastalığı nedeniyle hayatını kaybettiği, zehirlenme veya travmatik etki sonucu öldüğüne ilişkin tıbbi delil bulunmadığı belirtilmişti.

Başsavcılığın itirazının, özellikle ölüm nedeni ve zehirlenmeye ilişkin değerlendirmeler üzerinde yoğunlaştığı bildirildi.

title: GENAR Başkanı Aktaş: "Yolsuzluğa karışan AKP’li siyasetçi ve idareciler hesap versin"
content:
GENAR Araştırma'nın sahibi İhsan Aktaş, 8 Kasım'da Yeni Şafak'ta yayımlanan "Bu millet AK Parti'den ne istiyor?" başlıklı makalesinde, Türkiye'yi sarsan "fon krizi"ni "AKP yönetiminin içinden kaynaklanan bir sorun" olarak tanımladı. Aktaş, yolsuzluklara karışan iş insanlarının yanı sıra kamu görevlileriyle onları koruyan siyasetçilerin de hesap vermesini istedi.


"AKP 3 puan kaybetti"


Aktaş'ın değerlendirmeleri, GENAR'ın ekim araştırmasında AKP'nin "fon krizi" sonrasında kendi araştırmalarında yaklaşık 3 puan oy kaybettiğinin ortaya çıkmasının ardından geldi.


Aktaş, 18 Ekim'deki ilk yazısında "fon krizinin AK Parti'nin oylarını yüzde 36 bandından yüzde 33,7'ye düşürdüğünü" açıklamış, kaybın sınırlı kalmasını ise "muhalefetin dağınıklığı"na bağlamıştı.


Ancak üç hafta sonra meseleye yalnızca seçim sonuçları açısından yaklaşmadı. 8 Kasım tarihli

yazısında

 krizin kaynağını doğrudan iktidarın yönetim mekanizmasında aradı.


"Dış güçler değil, iktidarın içindeki ilişkiler"


Aktaş, yazısının büyük bölümünü AKP'nin tarihsel misyonunu ve Erdoğan'ın uluslararası önemini savunmaya ayırdıktan sonra sözü "fon krizi"ne getirdi. 


Krizin kaynağının yabancı güçler, darbeciler veya eski vesayet kurumları olmadığını vurgulayan Aktaş, iş insanları, imza yetkisi bulunan kamu görevlileri ve onları koruyan siyasetçiler üzerinden ortaya çıkan tabloyu şöyle tanımladı:


"Doğrudan AK Parti yönetiminin iç travmasıdır."


Bu ifade, başta Erdoğan olmak üzere AKP yetkililerinin sorunu "dış güçler"e bağladıkları bir saldırıyla açıklama teşebbüslerini benimsemeyişiyle dikkat çekiyor.


Aktaş, krize karışan herkesin hukuken hesap vermesini, denetim ve yönetim mekanizmalarının yeniden düzenlenmesini, AK Parti'nin kuruluş dönemindeki reformcu siyasi kimliğinin güçlendirilmesini istedi:


Bu işe bulaşan dolandırıcı, amir, memur, siyasetçi kim varsa hukuk karşısında hesabını vermeli ve milletin sisteme olan güveni yenilenmelidir.


Ancak sorumluluğu Erdoğan'ın liderliğinden ayrı tuttu. Sistem eleştirilerinin Cumhurbaşkanı'na yöneltilmiş eleştiriler gibi gösterilmesine karşı çıkarak liderlik ile yönetim mekanizması arasında kesin bir ayrım yaptı:


"Lider bir misyondur, bir ruhtur."


Buna karşılık sistemi, aksayan parçaları değiştirilmesi gereken teknik bir aygıt olarak tanımladı.


Üç haftada üç yazı: Anketten sistem eleştirisine


Aktaş'ın 8 Kasım'daki değerlendirmesi, 18 Ekim'de GENAR'ın sonuçlarını açıklamasıyla başlayan tartışmanın üçüncü halkası.


18 Ekim'de yayımladığı "AK Parti seçmeni olana razı olmadı fakat partisini terk etmedi" başlıklı yazısında, AKP'nin oy kaybını kabul etmiş ancak seçmenin bütünüyle partiden kopmadığı görüşünü savunmuştu.

author: Mike Ludwig
title: “Green Economic Populism” Candidates Won 39 Out of 56 Races for Congress
content:
Support for climate action tied to the economy was also visible in the results of state-level ballot initiatives.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

The dominant narrative about the Democratic sweep of the midterm elections has focused on President Donald Trump’s brash ineptitude and voters fed up with the costs of living amid reports of corruption emanating from the White House. The climate crisis appeared to take a backseat to concerns about rising energy prices driven by data center build-out and inflation linked to the U.S.-Israel war on Iran, but experts say an emerging class of Democrats successfully fused momentum behind economic populism with the need for climate action to win over voters.

“Voters rewarded economic populists who tied that message to climate, and I think there is a lot of appetite and movement in that direction,” said Patrick Bigger, research director at the Climate and Community Institute (CCI), in an interview with Truthout.

In surveys, potential voters ranked climate change behind most other concerns, with the economy, health care, and the war on Iran consistently topping the list. However, Bigger said victories for Democrats such as Senators-elect Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan and Troy Jackson in Maine suggest that voters are making connections between an economy rigged by elites and environmental concerns such as fossil fuel extraction and noise pollution from data centers.

“We had Troy Jackson in Maine talking about heat pumps and cost of fuel oil, and Abdul El-Sayed talking about reining in Michigan’s utility companies and data centers,” Bigger told Truthout. “How our economy is being organized and its link to the natural world, that is very much front of mind even if people don’t say they’re voting on climate specifically.”

Bigger is the co-author of a new report tracking the success of midterm candidates that embedded messages about climate action within a broader populist economic agenda, reflecting what CCI calls “Green Economic Populism.” The report finds that the 2026 candidates aligned most strongly with Green Economic Populism — virtually all of them Democrats — won 39 out of 56 races for Congress, including six of the seven Senate seats that were up for grabs.

Multiple green populist-aligned candidates also won state and local races or defeated moderates in primary races, most notably Angie Nixon of south Florida, a progressive who won a Democratic congressional primary by tying climate to broken housing insurance markets, according to the report. Nixon narrowly lost to Republican Ashley Moody, and the progressive’s supporters complained that she received little support from the Democratic Party.

According to the CCI report, these candidates offered policy platforms that drew connections between the climate crisis and the rising cost of living by identifying many of the same culprits driving both, including energy utilities, fossil fuel companies, corporate landlords, AI companies, and data center developers. Candidates such Democrat Claire Valdez, the first Native American woman to win a U.S. House seat from New York, and Sen.-elect Peggy Flanagan in Minnesota, argued that one way to lower costs is to “take back power from the elite” and invest in cheap clean power and green infrastructure built by union labor.

”Our polling shows that people link these costs of living crisis to the climate crisis,” Bigger said.

Other incoming House members who ran on a green economic populist platform include Democrats Angela Gonzales-Torres of California, Melat Kiros of Colorado, Patty Garcia of Illinois, Will Lawrence of Michigan, and Chris Rabb of Pennsylvania, according to the report. Incumbent green populist Democrats returning to Congress after fending off GOP challengers include Rep. Ro Khanna of California, Sen. Ed Markey of Massachusetts, and Rep. Adelita Grijalva of Arizona, among others.

Climate and energy policy remains a challenge for Democrats. On November 9, the Senate voted 73-25 to advance a permitting “reform” bill that split the Democratic caucus, with Sen. Ron Wyden (D-Oregon) arguing Democrats should negotiate a new deal once they take the majority.

“I cannot support a bill that relies on a handshake promise from the same administration that’s spent the last two years waging a war on new clean energy projects to hold up its end of the bargain …

author: Chris Walker
title: Trump Administration Seeks to Strip 6.3 Million More People of SNAP Food Aid
content:
The proposed rule change comes as 34 percent of Americans report that they are suffering from food insecurity.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

A proposed rule change by the Department of Agriculture (USDA) seeks to limit eligibility standards for some households with low incomes when it comes to automatic enrollment into the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), sometimes referred to as the food stamps program.

Currently, any household that receives cash or in-kind assistance from the Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) program is automatically enrolled into SNAP. The USDA proposal would change that, requiring individuals who receive TANF assistance to apply for SNAP separately.

The administration claims that cuts would occur “because their income or resources exceed the Federal statutory limits.” USDA’s draft proposal states that more than $44 billion would be saved by the changes, but admits that the cuts would kick 6.3 million people off of the program in its first year.

The formal notice was published on Monday. It requires a 30-day comment period before it can be fully implemented.

The changes to SNAP would follow similar cuts that were made last year, when Republicans and President Donald Trump passed the “One Big Beautiful Bill” Act into law. In the year after that act was passed, 5.1 million people lost SNAP eligibility, amounting to a 13 percent decrease in total participation and dropping enrollment numbers for the program to the lowest levels seen in almost two decades.

The new rule would be even more drastic, dropping participation by 17.6 percent from its current numbers.

Major cuts to SNAP have long been a goal of conservatives — indeed, changes to the program, like those being proposed this week by the Trump administration, were part of Project 2025, the Heritage Foundation-backed blueprint for how Trump should govern that was published during the 2024 presidential campaign.

Trump has claimed that he had nothing to do with Project 2025, but his administration has implemented over 55 percent of its published objectives so far, and two-thirds of his first round of executive orders were taken directly from the document.

The SNAP changes, if the administration does indeed move forward with them, come at a time when more Americans are becoming food insecure. According to one survey, more than a third of consumers (34 percent) reported that they have skipped meals or cut meal sizes for financial reasons over the past year — an 11 percent increase from the previous year’s rates.

Relief doesn’t appear to be coming anytime soon, as the latest federal inflation report, published Tuesday morning, indicates that costs on most goods continue to increase, despite Trump’s claims last week that “inflation is solved.”

At the same time, movement media is vital in the fight against Trump’s authoritarian reign. Our mandate to tell the truth, share strategies for resistance, and speak against fascism is ever more urgent in this deluge of political censorship and misinformation. Yet, we are struggling to meet our publishing costs when our work is so urgently needed.

We are fundraising right now for those basic operating expenses — we need $50,000 in the next 9 days. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our work. Anything you can do makes a difference.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Democrats Demand Admin Stop Shredding Records Related to Trump’s DC Projects
content:
Reports find that the Interior Department has been routinely shredding official documents.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

House Democrats are demanding that key federal agencies and corporations retain their records after receiving a whistleblower report that the Trump administration is shredding records related to the president’s expensive, scandal-ridden construction projects around Washington, D.C.

CNN reports that administration officials are rushing to shred key paperwork before Democrats take charge of Congress in January. Democrats have pledged to conduct a wide variety of hearings and investigations into Trump administration actions, and are planning a “high-profile hearing on one or several projects early in the new Congress,” CNN reported.

President Donald Trump’s plans to build a massive arch and revamp the East Potomac golf course are two major areas of focus because Democrats believe they may be able to stop construction before it starts. The Trump administration, on the other hand, is trying to move as fast as possible on the president’s arch, golf course, Lafayette Square, and Tidal Basin projects before the new Congress is sworn in on January 3.

Huffman said the Democrats “have standing to go to court if we have to” over the projects, per CNN. “We’ll have tools to be able to stop a lot of it.”

The Interior Department has denied reports that it is violating federal records preservation requirements.

The Democratic push against the records deletions is more wide-ranging than just Trump’s D.C. projects, however.

On Monday, the House Natural Resources Committee’s top Democrat, Rep. Jared Huffman (California), sent letters to 36 federal agencies and corporate donors ordering them to preserve records and communications related to the committee’s investigation of the Trump administration and corporations that have donated to Trump’s projects. The records requests require a certification from recipients, and include requirements to recover lost records that may have been deleted.

“For two years, this administration has stonewalled us and kept the American people in the dark while Democrats have fought tirelessly to daylight and stop their corruption,” said Huffman in a statement. “I am sending a message to President Trump and his allies: our investigations will continue full steam ahead. And to every agency official and corporate executive receiving these letters: save everything.”

The committee, which oversees federal lands, is slated to take the lead on the investigations into the projects. It’s also working with the powerful House Oversight and House Judiciary committees on other as-yet unspecified investigations into the Trump administration.

Agencies that received letters from the Democrats include the Department of Agriculture, Department of Interior, and Department of Commerce. Non-governmental recipients include military contractors like Boeing, Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, Oracle, and Palantir, as well as other entities like ExxonMobil, Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC), and UnitedHealth Group.

Huffman’s office cited a report from August by Politico that found that the Interior Department has “devolved into secrecy” and hemorrhaged staff under Doug Burgum. The agency, which oversees federal lands and agencies like the National Parks Service, has blocked over 100 projects being undertaken at national parks while working to help fast-track Trump’s D.C. projects, even sometimes against court orders.

That report found that Interior Department officials have “routinely shredded official documents and use disappearing Signal messages — even for mundane scheduling matters — to avoid communications being preserved, as is required by the Federal Records Act.”

Burgum has created an environment of paranoia, apparently asking for the installation of a second sensitive compartmented information facility (SCIF) in the building. A SCIF is a unit used to house and access classified government information, typically used by the Department of Defense.

“They’re terrified of written records,” one former Interior Department official told Politico.

author: David Venn
title: Preparations for Nunavut devolution entering ‘final phase,’ premier’s office says
content:
Preparations for devolution are entering “their final phase,” Nunavut Premier John Main’s office said Tuesday in a news release.


The release provides an update on the Government of Nunavut’s devolution process, which will see control over a vast majority of Crown land in the territory

transferred

 to the GN.


To enable devolution, Nunavut must

mirror

 six pieces of federal legislation: The Waters Act, Public Lands Act, Archaeological and Palaeontological Sites Act, Surface Rights Tribunal Act, Nunavut Planning and Project Assessment Act, and the Canada Oil and Gas Operations Act.


MLAs passed four of those acts through second reading during the fall sitting of the legislative assembly. They include the Waters Act, the Surface Rights Tribunal Act, Public Lands Act and Archaeological and Palaeontological Sites Act.


The final two bills will be tabled during the winter sitting, said the release.


Work is also ongoing to create a new Department of Mines, Natural Resources and Land. The department has a new organizational structure and Inuktitut name: Nunalirijikkut.


“Many Nunavummiut who will work in the new department are currently employed by the [federal government],” the release said, adding that the deadline for such employees to respond to the GN’s job offer is Nov. 22.


“Their knowledge and technical expertise are highly valued.”


The GN is also offering training through the Namminiqsurniq Professional Project Administrator Program to boost Inuit employment, according to the release.


The federal and territorial governments are finalizing the transfer of properties, staff housing, vehicles and records, the release said.


Devolution is

set to take place

 April 1, 2027.

author: Sophia Sheera
title: Israeli Apartheid-Linked Firms Win UK Contracts Despite Sanctions Pledge
content:
Companies with links to illegal Israeli settlements in the West Bank have won £10.7m worth of UK government contracts since Ed Miliband’s

pledge to sanction businesses

 facilitating the settlements.


The foreign secretary said on 8 September that Andy Burnham’s government would “take action” against companies and individuals involved in settlement activities.


“To those who finance or facilitate illegal settlements, let me say this: you will face the full force of UK sanctions,” he said, adding: “Settlements are illegal.”


But businesses

named and shamed by the UN

 for their involvement in Israeli settlements have since been awarded new public sector contracts,

analysis by Tussell for Al Jazeera shows

. 


The vast majority were signed with Heidelberg Materials, a German-headquartered firm. It has been granted 14 UK contracts worth £10.4m since Miliband announced sanctions. 


“Britain cannot credibly claim that it is imposing sanctions on Israeli settlements while letting contracts continue through the back door,” said former Labour leader and Your Party MP Jeremy Corbyn. 


“The fact that public money is still going to firms that could be targeted under the government’s own sanctions regime… is outrageous and frankly insulting to the public.”


Heidelberg operates an Israeli subsidiary, Hanson Israel, which runs a quarry on land belonging to the Palestinian villages of

Al-Zawiya and Rafat

. In the UK, materials from Heidelberg will be used to resurface roads in Nottingham and Lincolnshire.  


Two contracts worth about £87,900 were granted to Motorola Systems to provide communications for the police service. The US company is the sole provider of the Israeli military’s 4G cellular network,

according to the Who Profits

 research centre. 


Companies Fosun and Egis were also flagged in the Al Jazeera report for taking home contracts worth more than £100,000 each. Heidelberg, Motorola and Fosun did not respond to Al Jazeera’s requests for comment whilst Egis said it “formally expressed its disagreement” with being included in the UN database.


Novara Media contacted the UK foreign office for comment.

author: Unknown
title: YPG internationalist Konstantin Gedig remembered in Kiel
content:
This Saturday, the seventh annual commemoration of Konstantin Gedig – Şehîd Andok Cotkar was held in Kiel. Andok was martyred on October 16, 2019, in an attack by the Turkish Air Force on the western Kurdish border city of Serêkaniyê (Ras al-Ain), in violation of international law. Since 2016, he had fought against the Islamic State (ISIS) as a member of the People’s Protection Units (YPG). To this day, Andok’s killing has had no political consequences for Turkey, a NATO member, and there is still no information about the whereabouts of Konstantin’s body.


Shortly after 3 p.m., the Kurdish Community Center in Kiel was filled to capacity. More than 100 friends, comrades and family members gathered in the hall, lovingly decorated with flowers, flags and photographs, to commemorate Konstantin Gedig – Şehîd Andok Cotkar and remember his struggle. They came to remember Konstantin, the humorous and lively person, the son, the friend, the brother, the farmer, the student of Kurdish, the medic and the fighter for justice. They also came to remember the struggle for freedom waged against ISIS and Turkey’s war of aggression. In this struggle, Andok and 11,000 other fighters lost their lives, while 19,000 were wounded, in an effort to protect the lives of countless others.


“When you lose your child, every memory is sacred”


In a moving speech, Konstantin’s mother, Ute Ruß, once again described how the family had experienced his journey to Rojava. On September 1, 2019, Konstantin contacted his family to say that he was on his way to Sulaymaniyah to join the fight against ISIS. From that moment on, time took on a different meaning for the family: researching the political situation in North and East Syria, searching for photographs of Andok and hoping for signs that he was alive.


Since his killing seven years ago, their daily lives have been shaped by efforts to reconstruct Andok’s final moments, the search for his body and the struggle for justice. Even today, new information about Andok, a fighter and frontline medic, continues to emerge: small mementos handed over to the family, stories shared by fellow fighters and photographs brought to them. This year’s invitation to the commemoration, for example, features a photograph of Andok taken in the summer of 2017, which filmmaker Pedro Brito da Fonseca gave to the family.


The struggle for justice is directed against what the family describes as deliberate attempts by the Turkish and German governments to erase the memory of Andok. Ute Ruß spoke in harrowing terms: “Nothing terrible is impossible. The Turkish state’s treatment of fallen enemies is profoundly degrading. Graves and bodies are desecrated on an unimaginable scale. Families have to beg for the return of their loved ones’ remains. A dead person is no longer treated as a human being; they are degraded, regarded as dirt in the eyes of the Turkish state.”


The search for Andok’s body has been made more difficult, according to the family, by the German government’s lack of interest and its unwillingness to confront Erdoğan. As a result, even seven years after Andok’s death, there is still no grave where his family can mourn him with dignity.


A special form of remembrance is the Konstantin Andok Literature Prize. Awarded since 2023, the prize is supported by Konstantin’s parents and was initiated by the Soli-Netz solidarity network, with contributors including Dario Azzellini, Yossi Bartal, Christian Baron, Jörn Boewe and Kerem Schamberger. Nearly 500 entries were submitted for the third edition of the competition, held under the motto “Speak. Write. Break the silence.”


During the commemoration, an excerpt was also shown from a laudatory speech delivered by Christian Baron at the most recent award ceremony. Baron emphasized that, under capitalism, literature and art must always take a stand against the existing order, exploitation, oppression and NATO wars waged in the name of Germany’s

raison d’état

.


The flower of Heval Andok


Musical performances accompanied the commemoration. As has almost become a tradition at these gatherings, 

Zana û Andok

 was sung, a tragic song about comrades Zana and Andok, who symbolize the pain and resistance of the Kurdish resistance movement. Following performances of 

Ez Nisêbin Tu Qamişlo

 and 

Çû

, everyone joined together to sing 

Bella Ciao

, including a verse rewritten in honor of Heval Andok.


Thus ended a deeply emotional, yet beautiful and defiant Saturday …

author: Unknown
title: Turkey steel factory explosion kills at least 16 people
content:
A fire broke out following an explosion at the HABAŞ Iron and Steel Factory in the Bozköy neighbourhood of Aliağa, Izmir. The death toll among workers has risen to 16, while 15 injured workers, four of whom are in critical condition, continue to receive treatment in hospital.


It was announced that search and rescue operations are continuing to reach four workers trapped beneath the rubble. According to initial assessments, the explosion is believed to have occurred when an overhead crane broke loose during the pouring of molten steel and fell into an electric arc furnace.


As part of the investigation launched into the incident, four public prosecutors have been assigned to the case, and five people have been taken into custody.

author: Unknown
title: Muratakan: Lack of concrete steps undermines public trust in the process
content:
Yunus Muratakan, Co-Chair of the Peoples' Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) in Diyarbakır (Amed), spoke about the resolution of the Kurdish question and the ongoing peace process, drawing attention to its historical background, legal guarantees, participation in democratic politics and the importance of social reckoning. Muratakan said that the Kurdish question could not be addressed solely through security-oriented policies, emphasizing that a lasting solution would only be possible through the recognition of democratic rights and the establishment of constitutional guarantees.


 


Muratakan discussed the historical development of the Kurdish question, saying that the centralized and uniform approach to governance that emerged with the founding of the Republic restricted the rights of different identities, languages and cultures. He stated that this approach, institutionalized through the 1924 Constitution, paved the way for policies of denial and repression targeting Kurdish identity and cultural rights. Muratakan added that restrictions on democratic expression, organization and political participation contributed to the emergence of the armed conflict.


'A process without a legal framework cannot become permanent'


Muratakan said that the period of armed conflict had imposed heavy human, economic and social costs on Turkey, recalling that tens of thousands of people had lost their lives, villages had been burned and evacuated, and forced displacement and serious human rights violations had occurred.


Muratakan also discussed peace and dialogue initiatives that emerged from the 1990s onwards, noting that the peace process launched in 2013 had received significant public support. He described the work of the Wise Persons Committee, the participation of political parties in discussions and public support as important achievements of the process. Muratakan said that Turkey had entered another period of intense conflict following the collapse of the process in 2015.


Muratakan stressed that past experiences offered important lessons, saying, "A process may begin through political will, but it cannot become permanent without legal guarantees. Any process that lacks a legal framework remains vulnerable to provocations and political interference."


'The process must move towards building positive peace'


Muratakan described the developments following the 27 February call as the beginning of a new era, saying that the declaration of a ceasefire, the decision to dissolve the organization and steps towards disarmament were significant. He also noted that the legal regulation introduced in Parliament represented an important beginning but contained shortcomings in its scope and content.


Muratakan said, "At this point, attention must be drawn to the DDR mechanism used in international conflict resolution experiences. Disarmament, demobilization and reintegration must be addressed as an integrated process. It is crucial to establish legal and institutional arrangements that enable people who have participated in armed struggle to reintegrate into social life and democratic politics. Negative peace means the end of armed conflict. Positive peace, however, requires addressing the structural problems that caused the conflict, guaranteeing rights and freedoms, and establishing a democratic social order. What we need today is a process that does not remain limited to negative peace but also builds positive peace."


Muratakan also criticized the scope of the legal regulation introduced in Parliament, saying that a step, albeit limited, had been taken towards seeking a solution through legal means with an organization that had waged an armed struggle against the government in Turkey's history.


Muratakan drew attention to shortcomings in the regulation's scope, saying, "For the first time in the history of the Republic of Turkey, a very small step has been taken towards recognizing through law an organization that has engaged in armed struggle, an insurgent organization, and resolving the rebellion through legal means. The fact that the law covers only a particular group involved in armed struggle, while excluding intentional homicide and related offenses, as well as people who were investigated before 2005, is a serious shortcoming. This process is also not entirely consistent with the conventional DDR processes implemented around the world."

author: Unknown
title: Call for truth and justice on the 21st anniversary of attack on Umut Bookshop
content:
The Şemzînan district organisations of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) and the Democratic Regions Party (DBP) held a press statement in front of the DEM Party’s district office to mark the anniversary of the bombing of Umut Bookshop on 9 November 2005. Civil society organisations from the district also took part in the event.


Reading the press statement, DBP District Co-Chair Senar Duyan said that the attack was not an isolated incident, but a significant turning point that once again brought to the fore the shadowy relationships within the state and illegal structures in Turkey’s recent political history.


Senar Duyan stated that an approach which regarded the Kurdish people’s identity, language, culture and demands for democratic freedoms as security threats had, for years, laid the groundwork for policies of denial, assimilation, repression and violence. He said these practices had inflicted deep wounds on society’s collective memory.


Emphasising that the dark events of the past must be confronted if the Peace and Democratic Society Process is to have any genuine impact, Senar Duyan called for the truth to be brought to light and for policies of impunity to come to an end.


Duyan said: “ For the ongoing discussions on peace and a democratic society to have any genuine meaning, the dark pages of the past must be confronted, the truth must be brought to light, and policies of impunity must come to an end. We know that peace is built not by forgetting the past, but by confronting its pain, uncovering the truth and establishing justice. Shemdinli events of 9 November must be fully investigated and brought to light. This is a shared responsibility not only of the people of Şemdinli, but of everyone who stands for a democratic and just future.”

author: Unknown
title: IOM: 3,834 displaced people return home in Iraq
content:
Pascal Reyntjens, Chief of Mission of the International Organization for Migration (IOM) in Iraq, issued a statement on the return of displaced people to their homes in Iraq.


Reyntjens said that the organization continues to coordinate with the Iraqi government on closing displacement camps and facilitating the integration of displaced people, with the participation of government institutions, United Nations (UN) agencies and relevant organizations.


Reyntjens stated that the Iraqi government remains determined to consolidate the Behirkê and Dîbegê camps in Erbil (Hewlêr), along with three camps east of Mosul, into a single camp.


He added that the IOM, the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) and the Iraqi government continue to engage with camp residents to discuss possible solutions.


The IOM Chief of Mission in Iraq reported that 639 families, comprising 3,834 people, have returned to their homes or been relocated to other areas as part of integration efforts under the facilitated voluntary return program since the beginning of 2026. He added that financial assistance for camp residents is continuing.


The statement also noted that Iraq's Ministry of Migration and Displacement is overseeing the closure of camps in Sulaymaniyah (Silêmanî), with approximately 1,100 families having returned as part of the process. Most of these residents, primarily from Ashti Camp, have been resettled in the Dujail district of Saladin Governorate. Families meeting the eligibility requirements for return have received financial assistance of 4 million Iraqi dinars.

title: Çite: Mining, geothermal and solar projects accelerate in Kurdistan
content:
As the Peace and Democratic Society Process is being discussed, the mountains, pastures and waters of Northern Kurdistan have once again fallen under the shadow of excavators, axes and drilling machines over the past year. Developments stretching from Gabar, Cudi and Besta to the valleys of Dersim covered by mining licenses, from the geothermal fields of Varto (Gimgim) and Karlıova (Kanîreş) to the pastures of Kervanpınar (Arzoxlî), are not isolated incidents. Records from the past year reveal a series of interconnected acts of environmental destruction.


Tree felling, which has continued almost uninterrupted for seven years in Cudi, Gabar and Besta, showed no signs of slowing over the past year. In just one week, 1,950 tons of trees, equivalent to approximately 3,000 stacked cubic meters of timber, were cut down in Besta and Gabar. The logging spread to the slopes of Mount Gabar overlooking the Eruh (Dêh) district of Siirt (Sêrt). The felled trees were stacked along roadsides.


Şırnak and Siirt: The axe of 'security' in Besta


Hundreds of trees were cut down in October in the Çemê Tahlo area of Besta by village guards brought from Hosyan village in Siirt's Pervari district, under military supervision. Footage published in late September showed tons of trees that had been felled in February and left to dry being transported out of the area in trucks bearing Ankara registration plates, covered with tarpaulins, and passing through military checkpoints.


The Şırnak and Siirt bar associations filed criminal complaints with public prosecutors on 29 October against those responsible for the logging and relevant public officials, citing allegations of unauthorized tree felling and illegal transportation of forest products. The bar associations also demanded the disclosure of logging permits and Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) decisions. Media reports also indicated that some of the felled trees had been transported to military bases.


Forest cover in Şırnak recently declined from 44 percent to 36 percent. Although authorities announced last year that logging had been halted, new footage subsequently emerged.


Muş and Bingöl: More than 185 days of protest in Varto


Two geothermal power plant (GPP) exploration projects by a US-based company, covering 16 villages in Varto, Muş (Mûş), and six villages in Karlıova, Bingöl (Çewlîg), have sparked widespread opposition. A protest vigil that began in early May in Çalıdere village in Varto reached its 185th day on 4 November. Villagers have taken legal action against plans to open their pastureland to company operations. An administrative court ordered an on-site inspection of the project area on 8 October. The arrival of construction machinery in Kaynarpınar village under gendarmerie escort in August caused tensions between villagers and security forces.


Residents of Varto continuing their resistance had issued a new call for action on 2 November. The protesters and the Varto Ecology Platform called for mass participation in a crucial court-appointed expert inspection as part of the lawsuit seeking cancellation of the project, urging people to gather at the drilling site.


Diyarbakır: Pastures threatened by solar projects, heritage by excavators


A protest led by village women began in October in Kervanpınar (Arzoxlî), a village in the Sur district of Diyarbakır (Amed), against plans to build a solar energy plant (SEP) on communal pastureland. The company reportedly entered the site accompanied by security forces before the legal process had been completed. A stone believed to contain a coral fossil was discovered during excavation work. Concerns were also raised that the project area overlapped with an archaeological site.


Villagers from Ağaçlı (Cixse) in the Kulp (Pasûr) district, who had maintained a protest vigil against a solar power project for more than two months, joined the resistance. They were accompanied by villagers from Lice (Licê), who had succeeded in stopping similar projects. Representatives of the city's local administration also participated in a march at the site. In central Diyarbakır, attempts to cut down or relocate trees aged between 25 and 30 years as part of the Fırat Boulevard project also drew criticism.


Dersim: Munzur on the mining license map

title: Duygu Özbay: Centralized exams deepen educational inequalities
content:
The Common Written Examination System introduced by the Ministry of National Education has drawn criticism from education workers. Teachers warn that centralizing examination procedures will diminish their decisive role in teaching and assessment, while disregarding differences in the physical, economic and social conditions of schools.


Teachers emphasize that the system is far from ensuring equal educational opportunities. They warn that a standardized approach to assessment, which fails to consider students' different learning conditions and needs, will further deepen existing inequalities in education.


Duygu Özbay, co-chair of Branch No. 2 of the Education and Science Workers' Union (Eğitim Sen) in Diyarbakır (Amed), spoke to ANF about the Common Written Examination System.


'Centralized exams make teachers passive'


Duygu Özbay said that the common examination system increases centralization in education and weakens teachers' decisive role in teaching and assessment.


Özbay said: "We have previously stated that the common examination system is highly centralized. The education system has become even more centralized with the introduction of the Turkey Century Education Model (Maarif Model), the Ministry of National Education's new national curriculum framework. We regard the common examination system as one of the methods used to implement this model. In a sense, the Ministry is trying to make the model appear more comprehensive and successful. However, making assessment and evaluation so centralized places teachers in a very passive position in the classroom.


When preparing examination questions, we take into account our students' readiness to learn, their living conditions, their specific needs, the physical conditions of the school and how prepared each child is to absorb particular knowledge. Every student's learning process is different. Educational policies must therefore take these differences into account. However, the centralized examination system operates without considering children's individual circumstances. It also removes teachers' decisive role in the classroom and establishes an even more centralized structure."


'

Children do not start from equal positions'


Duygu Özbay said that students do not begin their education under equal conditions. She emphasized that poverty, the denial of mother-tongue education, overcrowded classrooms and difficulties accessing education directly affect learning processes.


Özbay also said: "It is particularly important to recognize that children have different starting points. The learning conditions of a child studying in an overcrowded classroom are very different from those of a child studying in what we consider an ideal classroom of twenty students. There are also children who cannot receive education in their mother tongue. There are children living in poverty and others who cannot access educational opportunities. The education system must therefore recognize these different starting points and, above all, address the inequalities between them.


The right to education in one's mother tongue is one of the most important dimensions of these inequalities. Poverty is another. We are still confronted with the reality of children who have not been able to enter the education system. Our assessments in Diyarbakır show that there are still children who cannot attend school. Months have passed, yet many children remain excluded from education because school transportation services have not started and tenders for these services have not been completed. Subjecting these children to a common examination system before they have even gained access to education is itself a form of inequality.


We therefore believe that the problems within the education system must be resolved before children are subjected to this examination system. Children must enter the education system with equal opportunities. However, simply attending a classroom does not mean that a child benefits from equal educational opportunities. If schools and the education system continue to reproduce existing inequalities, that structure must first be changed. Children must be able to receive education in their mother tongue, develop their reading and comprehension skills, and participate in education according to their individual needs."

Students' learning conditions are being ignored'

author: Unknown
title: Following in Şaristan's footsteps...
content:
Some people come into this world merely to breathe; others are born as the embodiment of an ideal. Martyr Şaristan represented a determined will that refused to surrender to the comfort of an ordinary life, even from her first breath, and carried storms within her soul. Her story is not simply the account of one person's life, but an epic tale of a land's suffering, a people's resistance and a woman's unwavering rebellion against the system.


Her childhood unfolded in a land where there was nothing ordinary about life. There was no room for being "ordinary" in the environment in which she grew up; one either stood tall or bowed down. Şaristan felt this reality deep within herself from a very young age. Even as a child, she was driven by a burning desire to stand on her own feet.


She was a child who possessed the courage to forge her own path rather than follow those laid out by others. The dignity she displayed when she took on her family's burdens and supported them despite financial hardship was the first sign of her iron will. The injustices she encountered at an early age and her confrontation with the true face of the enemy planted a seed of rebellion within her. Over time, that seed would grow into a mighty tree of resistance.


Her struggle did not begin in the present. It had started years earlier as a great battle for existence, through which a woman sought to prove that she would not be crushed by the machinery of the system. Standing against the system with such courage and determination required more than physical strength; it demanded extraordinary character and unwavering conviction. Şaristan had developed that strength of character.


She rejected the role of the "silent woman" imposed on her by the system and chose instead to become the architect of her own freedom.


The years she spent in prison were not a breaking point for her. Rather, they became a fortress in which her spirit matured. She paid the price for her honorable resistance against the enemy's oppression behind the cold walls of prison, where she developed herself, remained faithful to her ideals and forged her spirit into steel armor.


By 2012, the hunger strikes had left deep marks on her body, but they had also strengthened her unwavering determination. That hunger strike was not merely a protest; it was a battle for existence against the darkness that had descended upon her people and their struggle. She continued her resistance without regard for the damage to her body, the pain or the exhaustion, demonstrating the unshakable strength of her character. Time did not simply pass behind those walls. Şaristan emerged from prison as a pioneer.


Then the mountains of freedom called to her. By the time she was released from prison at the end of 2012, Şaristan was no longer the person she had once been. She was a fighter who had come to understand the impossibility of living within the system and knew the price of freedom. She entered the mountains not as a new student, but as an experienced pioneer who could guide others and whose every step was deliberate. Her character was so strong that she earned a special place in the hearts and minds of her comrades as someone sincere, pure-hearted and inspiring.


She knew not only how to fight, but also how to complement her comrades, clear the way for them and fill every gap through self-sacrifice. She understood that helping a comrade meant fulfilling one's own struggle. Overcoming an obstacle in a comrade's path was, for her, one of the greatest steps she could take along her own.


Today, when we remember her, we recall not only her smiling face but also her upright stance, unwavering courage and the heart with which she filled every void with a spirit of comradeship. When I watched the last footage of her recorded in the war tunnels, I saw more than an "end." In her eyes, I saw the radiance of victory, the light of freedom and an unmistakable message: "Either we will live through resistance, or, if death is inevitable, it must be an honorable death."


Those words are not a cry that calms the storm within me, but one that transforms it into an even greater ideal. Our martyrs have only one wish: to live freely or die with honor. The history of our struggle is built upon this unshakable truth.


We are not the true owners of this path. We are merely those entrusted with the path they left behind. The martyrs are the true owners of this struggle, and by walking this path, they transformed …

author: Unknown
title: Dilan Kunt Ayan: Abdullah Öcalan is the coordinator of the process
content:
Budget discussions began amid protests as Justice Minister Akın Gürlek arrived at the parliamentary commission. MPs from the New Party protested by refusing to shake hands with Gürlek, while MPs from the Peoples' Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) held placards featuring photographs of Figen Yüksekdağ, Selahattin Demirtaş, politicians imprisoned in the Kobanê trial and Can Atalay.


DEM Party MPs also displayed photographs of Rojin Kabaiş and seriously ill prisoner Tuncer Sağlam, alongside placards reading "Rojin Kabaiş did not commit suicide" and "You have a budget, but no justice."


DEM Party MP Ömer Faruk Gergerlioğlu interrupted Minister Gürlek's presentation, protesting, "We did not come here to listen to stories."


'Lawlessness is everywhere'


DEM Party MP Dilan Kunt Ayan said that Turkey was experiencing a crisis of justice alongside its economic crisis. She recalled that Gürlek had declared upon taking office that he was the justice minister of all 86 million people. Ayan said that this declaration had not been reflected in practice, stressing that people from every section of society were seeking justice and facing unlawful practices.


Ayan referred to the Law on National Solidarity and Strengthening Social Integration, adopted by Parliament on 20 August 2026, and criticized the work of the commission established under the law. She said that holding only two meetings was insufficient and emphasized that responsibility for peace could not be postponed.


'Why are imprisoned politicians still behind bars?'


Dilan Kunt Ayan criticized the continued imprisonment of Selahattin Demirtaş, Figen Yüksekdağ, politicians imprisoned in connection with the Kobane trial, Can Atalay, Tayfun Kahraman and Osman Kavala. Ayan condemned the failure to implement rulings by the Constitutional Court and the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR), calling on the justice minister to provide an explanation.


She argued that there were no legal obstacles to the release of the imprisoned politicians and told the minister, "As justice minister, you are obliged to answer this."


'Peace carries responsibilities'


Dilan Kunt Ayan emphasized the need to advance the Peace and Democratic Society Process, saying that thousands of families had suffered because the necessary courage had not been shown in the past. She argued that the process should not be shaped by militaristic approaches or statements from small groups.


Ayan referred to Abdullah Öcalan's Call for Peace and Democratic Society on 27 February, saying that he had effectively been directing and coordinating the process. Ayan said, "Mr. Öcalan made the Call for Peace and Democratic Society on 27 February. Since that day, he has effectively been directing and coordinating this process. Mr. Öcalan is now the Coordinator of Peace and Political Participation in this process, and it is time to call this role by its proper name. We need to move beyond these debates and take the process further."


New Party Deputy Parliamentary Group Chair Gökhan Günaydın also demanded an explanation regarding an investigation into a list allegedly containing the names of 60 MPs and 30 ministers. Günaydın asked why the list had not been made public and why the investigation had not progressed.
